title: 基于多模态神经符号推理的动态知识图谱构建与更新
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for constructing and dynamically updating knowledge graphs (KGs) based on multi-modal neural symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of deep learning for understanding complex semantic information from diverse data modalities (images, text, audio, etc.) and traditional knowledge representation methods through symbolic reasoning. The proposed system employs a multi-modal encoder to map data from various modalities into a unified embedding space. Subsequently, a neural symbolic reasoning engine, utilizing Transformer-based models, performs inference to derive new entities, relations, and attributes from these embeddings. These inferences are integrated into the KG, and continuous updates and corrections are implemented via feedback loops incorporating user interactions and external knowledge sources. Crucially, the system proactively identifies and addresses ambiguities and uncertainties within multi-modal data, translating them into probabilistic representations of relationships within the KG. This approach overcomes the limitations of static, manually-annotated KGs and enables a dynamic, autonomous KG construction and evolution process, capable of handling the inherent complexities of multi-modal data.

title: Adaptive Neuron Network Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network modeling, specifically designed for simulating complex biological neural networks. The core innovation lies in the implementation of a dynamic neuron network, which allows for continuous adjustment of neuron activations and synaptic weights, mimicking the dynamic and adaptive nature of biological neural systems. Traditional static models struggle to accurately represent the intricacies of complex biological neural networks, and this work offers a significant advancement in the field through the incorporation of a dynamically adjusted network architecture. The paper details the design of the dynamic neuron network, its underlying principles, and its potential applications in biological simulation.

title: ## Bluefin Optimization Algorithm (BOA): An Inspired Approach
abstract: This paper introduces the Bluefin Optimization Algorithm (BOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of bluefin tuna. BOA leverages the fish's ability to dynamically adjust its swimming direction and speed based on environmental pressure and the perceived positions of other individuals to navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a dynamic velocity adjustment mechanism mimicking the fish's orientation changes, a distributed pressure assessment system reflecting the collective intelligence of the group, and a localized exploration strategy based on individual bluefin's proximity to potential solutions. BOA aims to achieve efficient global convergence while maintaining adaptability to varying problem landscapes. The core mathematical representation of the algorithm is presented, outlining the parameters and equations governing its operation. This paper details the theoretical underpinnings of BOA and establishes a framework for future research and application.

title: Non-Linear Adaptive Topology
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel non-linear adaptive topology algorithm designed to optimize data representation and transmission. The core principle behind this algorithm lies in leveraging machine learning to dynamically adjust topological structures based on the inherent patterns within the input data distribution. Traditional approaches often lack this adaptability, hindering optimal data handling in dynamic environments. This work presents a rigorous exploration of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its efficacy in improving data representation and transmission through a continuous adaptation process. The paper details the core mechanism, highlighting the role of machine learning in identifying and responding to data shifts. We present quantitative results showcasing the algorithm's superior performance compared to baseline methods in a simulated data environment.

title: Ant Colony Optimization for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Ant Colony Optimization for Complex Optimization Problems (ACOCP), inspired by the foraging behavior of ants. The algorithm leverages concepts from Artificial Intelligence, specifically mimicking ant trail formation and pheromone deposition to navigate and solve complex optimization problems. ACOCP employs a probabilistic approach, where ants explore the search space probabilistically, guided by pheromone trails that reflect the quality of solutions found by previous iterations. The algorithm incorporates mechanisms for pheromone evaporation and reinforcement, promoting convergence towards optimal or near-optimal solutions. This paper details the algorithm's design, including the representation of the problem space, the probabilistic movement rules, the pheromone update rules, and a discussion of parameter tuning. The core formula for pheromone update is: ΔΦij = Σk=1N ηk * Tij, where Φij is the pheromone on edge (i, j), ηk is the heuristic value of ant k, Tij is the transmission rate of pheromone from ant k. The probability of choosing a neighboring node is calculated as: Pij = (Cij / Σl Cil) * (Φij / Σl Φil), where Cij is the cost of moving from node i to node j, and Φij is the pheromone level on the edge (i, j). The algorithm is then demonstrated through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting its potential and limitations.

title: Admiralties Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Admiralties Rat
abstract: This paper presents Admiralties Rat, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the behavior of the Admiralties Rat, a rare and intriguing rodent known for its complex navigational strategies. The algorithm leverages the rat's ability to explore and exploit its environment efficiently to solve optimization problems. Admiralties Rat combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), incorporating a dynamic adaptation of the Lévy flight mechanism to enhance exploration. The core innovation lies in a novel 'Rat's Path' representation, where solutions are encoded as sequences of directional movements, mimicking the rat's route-finding process. This representation is coupled with a 'Territory Awareness' mechanism, allowing the algorithm to prioritize regions of the search space with higher potential for optimal solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. Results demonstrate that Admiralties Rat consistently outperforms traditional metaheuristic algorithms in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's adaptability and exploration capabilities make it a promising candidate for various complex optimization challenges.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Topology Verification
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating area of theoretical physics, offers potential for novel computational paradigms. This paper explores the application of self-adaptive quantum topology verification as a means to validate quantum computation models and optimize their parameters. We introduce a novel framework predicated on the manipulation of quantum topology to rigorously assess model fidelity, ultimately leading to improved quantum system performance. This approach departs from traditional validation methods, leveraging the inherent robustness of topological structures to provide a more reliable and efficient verification process. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of parameters based on topological analysis, promoting accuracy and minimizing error. This research highlights the potential of self-adaptive verification to significantly advance the field of quantum computation.

title: Dicke superposition probes for noise-resilient Heisenberg and super-Heisenberg metrology
abstract: Phase sensing with entangled multi-qubit states in the presence of noise is a central theme of modern quantum metrology. The present work investigates Dicke state superposition probes for quantum phase sensing under parameter encoding generated by one- and two-body interaction Hamiltonians. Under linear collective-spin encoding, near-optimal Dicke superposition states are shown to exhibit significantly enhanced robustness against phase damping noise compared with Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ), W-superposition, and balanced Dicke states, while maintaining favorable metrological performance under realistic decoherence channels. For two-body interactions, optimal probe states maximizing the quantum Fisher information are identified. Their noise resilience and metrological scaling behaviour under phase damping, amplitude damping, and global depolarizing channels are analyzed. The associated near-optimal Dicke superposition states are found to exhibit improved resilience to phase damping, for the system sizes considered. These results establish tailored near-optimal Dicke state superposition probes as versatile and noise-resilient resources for Heisenberg and super-Heisenberg quantum phase sensing governed by one- and two-body interactions.

title: Investigating Hyperparameter Optimization and Transferability for ES-HyperNEAT: A TPE Approach
abstract: Neuroevolution of Augmenting Topologies (NEAT) and its advanced version, Evolvable-Substrate HyperNEAT (ES-HyperNEAT), have shown great potential in developing neural networks. However, their effectiveness heavily depends on the selection of hyperparameters. This study investigates the optimization of ES-HyperNEAT hyperparameters using the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) on the MNIST classification task, exploring a search space of over 3 billion potential combinations. TPE effectively navigates this vast space, significantly outperforming random search in terms of mean, median, and best accuracy. During the validation process, the best hyperparameter configuration found by TPE achieves an accuracy of 29.00\% on MNIST, surpassing previous studies while using a smaller population size and fewer generations. The transferability of the optimized hyperparameters is explored in logic operations and Fashion-MNIST tasks, revealing successful transfer to the more complex Fashion-MNIST problem but limited to simpler logic operations. This study emphasizes a method to unlock the full potential of neuroevolutionary algorithms and provides insights into the hyperparameters' transferability across tasks of varying complexity.

title: CAST: Critique-Aware Supervision for Training Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Calling Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in long-horizon, interactive, and stateful environments. In these settings, a single wrong action, such as refunding the wrong purchase, can cause irreversible task failure and must be intercepted before execution. Such failures may not appear in every single run, but can emerge across repeated trials, making reliability across steps and trials critical. However, ensuring agentic reliability is challenging: even frontier LLMs struggle to explain why an action may be wrong, especially in long, intertwined trajectories governed by domain-specific policies. Much recent work relies on prompt-based critique agents, while optimization-based methods lack a systematic way to produce rich verification rationales for training. We address this gap with CAST, a critique-aware training framework that converts sparse task outcomes into action-level supervision for critique learning and policy optimization. CAST analyzes agent trajectories to synthesize structured rationales explaining action validity under partial observability. The resulting critique model is used to construct critique-aware training data for optimizing the policy model. Fine-tuning Qwen3-family models on dynamic tool-calling benchmarks, CAST improves reliability across domains, outperforming GPT-OSS-120B by over 10% pass^4 on Retail tasks and yielding an additional 9% improvement on Telehealth in an out-of-domain setting. These results demonstrate that critique-aware training improves the robustness of LLM agents in realistic dynamic environments.

title: Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Using PCA–KNN: A Comparative Study with SVR and MLP on Historical Operational Data
abstract: The transition toward renewable energy integration in power systems presents challenges in managing photovoltaic (PV) power output owing to variations in operating conditions. This study evaluated the performance of K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), with and without Principal Component Analysis (PCA), for PV power output prediction. The dataset comprised 420 observations recorded at five-minute intervals over seven days of measurements from a PV system. The data were chronologically divided into 80% training and 20% testing sets, while normalization and PCA were exclusively fitted to the training data to prevent information leakage. The model performance was evaluated using the Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R²). The results show that KNN and PCA-KNN achieved the best and identical performance, with an MSE of 265.3385, RMSE of 16.2892, and R² of 0.8421. PCA did not improve KNN accuracy but maintained its predictive performance after the dimensional transformation. PCA-MLP showed a slight improvement over MLP, whereas SVR and PCA-SVR yielded lower performances. These findings indicate that the effect of PCA depends on both the dataset characteristics and the learning algorithm. Further studies with longer observation periods, more diverse datasets, and external validation are recommended to assess the generalizability of the models.

title: Symbolic Regression with Quantum Annealing
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, the exponential growth in the solution space with increasing data complexity often presents a significant challenge. This paper investigates the potential of quantum annealing to accelerate symbolic regression. We propose a framework where a quantum annealing algorithm is directly employed to search for symbolic expressions that accurately represent the underlying relationship between input and output variables. The core idea is to leverage the quantum tunneling effect to efficiently navigate the complex, multi-modal cost function associated with symbolic regression, thereby escaping local minima and identifying optimal symbolic solutions more quickly. We demonstrate that quantum annealing can offer a viable approach to tackling this problem, particularly for datasets with moderate complexity. The approach's effectiveness stems from its ability to explore a vast solution space in parallel, a capability inherent to quantum computation. The results suggest that quantum annealing provides a novel and potentially significant enhancement to traditional symbolic regression methods.

title: Adaptive Probability Field Theory: A Novel Computational Approach
abstract: Adaptive Probability Field Theory (APFT) presents a paradigm shift in modeling complex systems by dynamically adjusting probability field parameters through neural networks. This novel approach enhances prediction and control accuracy compared to traditional methods reliant on static parameter adjustments. The core mechanism involves introducing a "dynamic probability field" that learns parameters based on environmental changes, ensuring adaptability to evolving conditions. This research investigates the feasibility and performance of APFT, demonstrating its potential for advanced modeling and control applications.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Probabilistic Logic Programming
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic programming that leverages the strengths of both neural networks and probabilistic logic programming. The core idea is to utilize neural networks to learn and generate logical rules, which are then executed within a probabilistic logic programming engine for reasoning and inference. This framework offers a more robust and interpretable solution for neuro-symbolic integration compared to traditional methods, by anchoring symbolic reasoning within a probabilistic framework. We present a detailed description of the architecture, including the neural rule generator and the probabilistic logic programming engine, and outline the key mechanisms for rule learning and execution. The approach addresses the challenges of brittle rule learning and lack of interpretability often associated with purely symbolic systems, while mitigating the instability and limited reasoning capabilities of conventional neural networks. Ultimately, this work demonstrates the potential for creating intelligent systems that seamlessly combine the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the logical deduction abilities of probabilistic logic programming.

title: Explainable Graph Neural Networks for Causal Inference
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph neural networks (GNNs) that integrates causal inference capabilities, addressing the long-standing "black box" problem inherent in traditional GNNs. The core idea is to develop explainable GNN models capable of discerning causal relationships between nodes within a graph, moving beyond mere correlation. We introduce causal graph embeddings, combining graph structure with explicit causal knowledge, and leverage attention mechanisms to learn and propagate causal weights. This framework allows for a more robust and interpretable understanding of complex systems, facilitating better decision-making and predictive modeling. The primary contribution lies in providing a structured method for incorporating causal reasoning into GNNs, significantly enhancing their utility in domains requiring nuanced understanding of interdependencies. Our approach offers a pathway toward building truly intelligent and trustworthy GNN systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Geometry of Quantum Computing Topology Analysis
abstract: Quantum computing offers unique computational capabilities, particularly in the realm of topological quantum information. This paper explores the application of adaptive geometry to analyze topological quantum information, investigating how quantum computation can enhance the efficiency of geometric topology. We develop a framework that leverages the inherent properties of quantum systems to model and understand topological quantum data structures. The core claim is that utilizing quantum computation allows for a significant improvement in the analysis and manipulation of geometric topology, ultimately leading to enhanced computational efficiency. The research will focus on establishing a methodology for quantifying and optimizing the impact of quantum algorithms on topological data analysis.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Data Analysis for Time Series Prediction
abstract: Quantum-enhanced topological data analysis (TDA) offers a novel approach to time series prediction, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper proposes a new quantum algorithm designed to enhance the accuracy of predictive modeling by simultaneously exploring multiple temporal patterns. We explore the potential of quantum superposition and entanglement to identify subtle correlations that are often missed by classical methods. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum algorithms to represent and process time series data in a fundamentally different manner, potentially leading to improved predictive capabilities. We detail the algorithm's design, its mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating enhanced accuracy in a simulated time series dataset. The core claim centers on the potential for quantum algorithms to surpass classical methods in identifying complex, non-linear patterns inherent in time series data.

title: Bio-Inspired Neural Architecture Optimization via Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural architecture optimization (NAO) inspired by biological neural networks. Traditional NAO methods primarily rely on mathematical optimization techniques, often neglecting the intricacies of biological neuron dynamics and adaptation. We propose a simulation-based framework that mimics the learning and adaptive behavior of biological neurons within complex environments. This framework utilizes a detailed, biologically plausible neuron model incorporating synaptic plasticity, neuronal communication, and noise adaptation, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively optimize the neural architecture. title: Bicolored Shrew Optimization Algorithm (BSOA): A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Uropsilus rutilus*
abstract: This paper presents the Bicolored Shrew Optimization Algorithm (BSOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Uropsilus rutilus*, a small shrew species known for its unique and efficient foraging strategy. The algorithm mimics the shrew's ability to rapidly search for food sources by utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, guided by a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a dynamic probability distribution. The BSOA incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) to achieve robust performance in a variety of optimization problems. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the core mechanics of the algorithm, including the position update equation, the velocity update equation, and the probability calculation for food source selection. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of BSOA in solving benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's key innovations lie in its adaptive inertia weight control and the dynamic probability distribution, which contribute to its ability to escape local optima and converge to global solutions efficiently. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to complex real-world problems.

title: Title: Universal Quantum State Transfer Protocol for Information Transfer
abstract: Quantum information transfer presents significant challenges due to the fragility of quantum states and the potential for decoherence. Traditional quantum communication methods, reliant on complex quantum repeaters, are limited in their reach and require substantial resources. This paper introduces a novel quantum state transfer protocol, dubbed the "Universal Quantum State Transfer Protocol," designed to overcome these limitations by leveraging entanglement swapping to enable efficient and robust state transfer across any distance, minimizing decoherence and error. The protocol's core principle centers around rapid and lossless state transfers, drastically reducing the need for complex quantum repeaters. This work explores the implementation of a unique entanglement swapping mechanism to achieve this goal, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize quantum communication. The resulting protocol offers a pathway towards more practical and scalable quantum communication systems.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Simulating Complex Systems with Uncertainty
abstract: This paper explores the application of probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) for simulating complex systems characterized by inherent uncertainty. Traditional simulation methods often require significant manual effort in defining stochastic elements, handling uncertainty, and performing Bayesian inference. PPLs offer a more declarative approach, allowing users to specify the underlying probabilistic model directly, facilitating automated inference and sensitivity analysis. We argue that PPLs provide a more intuitive and efficient workflow for modeling and simulating complex systems, leading to improved understanding and decision-making in the face of uncertainty. The core mechanism involves defining a simulation model within a PPL, incorporating stochastic elements and leveraging the language's built-in support for Bayesian inference. This approach simplifies the entire simulation process, reducing the need for manual intervention and enabling more robust and reliable results. We demonstrate this principle through a conceptual framework and highlight the advantages of using PPLs for complex system simulation.

title: Ansell's Wood Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Apodemus sylvaticus*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Ansell's Wood Mouse" (AWM), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Apodemus sylvaticus*, commonly known as the wood mouse. Wood mice exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in locating and exploiting food resources within their environment. AWM leverages these observed behaviors – specifically, the combination of exploratory and exploitative movements, coupled with a dynamic adjustment of search radius – to construct a robust and effective optimization algorithm. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel mutation operator designed to mimic the erratic, yet purposeful, movements of the wood mouse during its foraging expeditions. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to effectively navigate complex search spaces and achieve competitive results compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization. The core of AWM is the "Radius Adjustment Mechanism" (RAM), which dynamically scales the search radius based on the current population's convergence rate. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be relatively insensitive to specific problem instances, offering a degree of robustness. We provide a detailed description of the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and a comparative analysis of its performance against other metaheuristic techniques. The results suggest that AWM holds significant promise as a versatile optimization tool, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptability and efficient exploration.

title: ## Coral Crab Optimization Algorithm (CCOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Coral Crab Optimization Algorithm (CCOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of coral crabs (Stenoplax). CCOA leverages this behavior by simulating coral crab movement within a search space, employing a "crab" representation, a "reef" structure to represent the search space, and a "current" flow mechanism to guide the crabs towards promising regions. The algorithm incorporates adaptive parameters controlling exploration and exploitation, mimicking the crabs' response to environmental changes and food availability. The core of CCOA lies in its dynamic adjustment of crab positions, reef structure, and current flow, aiming to achieve efficient convergence while maintaining a balance between exploring new areas and refining solutions around promising regions. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and provides a conceptual overview, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Random Walk Algorithms for Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired concepts to enhance the performance of random walk algorithms for optimization problems. Classical random walk algorithms are susceptible to getting trapped in local optima, limiting their efficacy in tackling complex and high-dimensional search spaces. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that incorporates principles of quantum superposition and tunneling into the random walk process. The algorithm leverages these concepts to enable more extensive exploration of the search space, thereby increasing the probability of converging towards the global optimum. We present a detailed formulation of the algorithm, outlining the key parameters and their influence on the optimization process. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential advantages of this quantum-inspired approach compared to traditional random walk methods. The algorithm's ability to escape local minima is evaluated through simulations, showcasing its effectiveness in a variety of benchmark optimization problems. The results highlight the promise of quantum-inspired techniques in improving the robustness and efficiency of random walk algorithms, offering a viable strategy for solving challenging optimization tasks.

title: Group Adaptive Clipping Policy Optimization
abstract: Group relative policy optimization for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically uses a fixed importance-sampling (IS) ratio clipping boundary across all rollouts. We identify a key limitation: rare correct rollouts on harder problems and abundant correct rollouts on easier problems are clipped at comparable rates, despite contributing very different learning signals. Rollouts with low group success exhibit larger IS ratios and carry stronger gradient signal for exploration and solving new problems, yet are disproportionately suppressed by fixed clipping. To address this, we propose Group Adaptive Clipping Policy Optimization (GAPO), a plug-in modification to GRPO methods that adapts the clipping boundary to the rollout advantage. GAPO is motivated by a reverse-KL trust-region perspective, which suggests that rollouts with larger learning signal should receive proportionally greater update headroom. GAPO requires no reward shaping and preserves the standard PPO/GSPO surrogate while adapting only the clipping threshold. Across Qwen and Llama models, GAPO consistently improves both Pass@1 and Pass@k over fixed clipping and advantage-shaping baselines on math reasoning and coding benchmarks where the pass rates by the base model are relatively low.

title: Verification-Aware Training for Speculative Decoding
abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a draft model to generate candidate tokens, which are verified by the target model in a single forward pass. Verification proceeds sequentially and discards every position from the first rejection onward, yet existing draft training relies on token-level imitation of the target with a fixed per-position weighting that reflects neither property. We introduce Verification-Aware Training (VAT), a plug-in framework that simulates verification at every training step and turns the resulting accept and reject patterns into supervision. VAT consists of two components: (i) a verification head, a lightweight jointly trained binary classifier that supervises the draft model on whether each position survives sequential verification; (ii) verification-adaptive weighting, which replaces the fixed weighting schedule by keeping full weight up to each sample's first rejection point and re-anchoring the decay to start there. VAT modifies only the training objective, so it can be layered on top of existing methods without changing the draft architecture, the target model, or the inference procedure. Applied to EAGLE-3 and DFlash on Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and LLaMA-3.1-8B, VAT improves average acceptance length by up to 11.4% and wall-clock speedup by up to 8.7%, with consistent gains across math, code, and chat benchmarks. Code will be available at https://github.com/naver-ai/vat

title: Quantum Information Entropy Encoding: A Novel Approach Utilizing Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum information entropy, a fundamental concept in quantum physics, represents the uncertainty associated with information. Traditional encoding methods struggle to efficiently represent and transmit this uncertainty, limiting their potential for advanced computation and secure communication. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement as a novel encoding mechanism, proposing a method that leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled states to create a robust and potentially transformative encoding process. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the design of a quantum entanglement protocol for information encoding, extraction, and compression. The research focuses on the inherent advantages of quantum entanglement over conventional encoding techniques, specifically highlighting its ability to provide enhanced information protection and computational capabilities. We conclude with a discussion of the potential implications and challenges of this approach, emphasizing its promise for revolutionizing information security and quantum computing.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis via Dynamic Bayesian Networks
abstract: Program synthesis, the automated generation of computer programs, faces significant challenges when dealing with complex, real-world problems. Traditional approaches often rely solely on symbolic methods or neural networks, each with limitations in capturing the full complexity of program logic and data patterns. This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic approach that combines the strengths of Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) and neural networks to achieve more effective and adaptable program synthesis. The core idea is to construct a hybrid system where a DBN provides a structured symbolic representation and execution engine, while a neural network learns and refines the probabilistic model of the DBN based on observed program execution outcomes. This iterative process allows the system to dynamically adjust its synthesis strategy, leading to improved program generation accuracy and efficiency. The system's architecture and mechanism are presented, highlighting its ability to integrate symbolic reasoning with neural pattern recognition, ultimately addressing a critical gap in current program synthesis techniques. The system demonstrates the potential to generate complex programs by learning the underlying patterns of successful program executions.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Simulation of Biological Systems
abstract: The simulation of complex biological systems, such as protein folding and gene regulation, presents significant challenges due to the inherent complexity and often intractable nature of these systems. Traditional computational methods struggle to capture the nuanced dynamics of biological processes, limiting our ability to understand and potentially manipulate them. This research proposes an innovative approach – adaptive quantum simulation – that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to create dynamic, self-adjusting simulations of biological systems. We aim to develop an algorithm that continuously refines simulation parameters, automatically mimicking biological behavior to achieve unprecedented accuracy and fidelity. This work explores the potential of quantum computation to overcome limitations inherent in classical simulation techniques, offering a fundamentally new pathway for biological system modeling and analysis. This includes a detailed explanation of the algorithm's core mechanisms, potential applications, and preliminary results demonstrating its adaptability. The core claim is that this adaptive quantum simulation method will allow for a level of detail and accuracy previously unattainable through conventional computational methods.

title: Bio-Inspired Neural Network Architecture Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network architecture design, drawing inspiration from the intricate structures and functionalities of biological neural networks. The core idea is to leverage bio-inspired algorithms to automatically optimize the architecture and parameters of artificial neural networks. Traditional methods for neural network design often rely on manual tuning or heuristic search, which can be computationally expensive and may not always yield optimal results. Our proposed methodology utilizes principles observed in biological systems, specifically focusing on self-organization and adaptive learning mechanisms, to guide the design process. The resulting architecture is evaluated based on performance metrics such as accuracy, convergence speed, and computational efficiency. The primary contribution lies in providing a systematic and potentially automated framework for creating neural networks tailored to specific tasks, offering a promising avenue for improved neural network performance and efficiency. The design incorporates key biological concepts like recurrent connections, sparse connectivity, and hierarchical organization.

This work represents a significant step toward a more efficient and robust quantum simulation methodology, opening avenues for broader applications in diverse fields.

title: Quantum-Inspired Feature Selection for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel feature selection method inspired by quantum mechanics, termed Quantum-Inspired Feature Selection (QIFS). Traditional feature selection techniques often struggle to capture complex correlations between features, leading to suboptimal model performance. QIFS leverages the principles of quantum superposition and interference to evaluate feature importance. The core mechanism involves simulating a quantum measurement process, where features are treated as quantum states and their relevance is determined by the interference patterns resulting from interactions. This approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of feature dependencies compared to methods like mutual information or correlation coefficients. The proposed method aims to identify a subset of features that maximizes the overall model performance while minimizing redundancy. The evaluation framework outlined in this paper provides a foundation for future research and development in this promising area. ---

abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric information encoding as a novel approach to enhance quantum computation's efficiency and stability. The core concept revolves around leveraging the inherent geometric properties of quantum systems to guide algorithm design and improve quantum state preservation. The investigation focuses on the potential benefits of this technique in specific quantum algorithms, particularly those involving complex rotations and transformations. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including theoretical analysis and experimental validation.

title: # Black Bonneted Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, "Black Bonneted Bat" (BBB), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black Bonneted Bat (Hypsignathus monstrosus). The algorithm leverages the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to navigate the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. BBB incorporates elements of pulse-frequency modulation (PFM) for exploration and a modified convergence mechanism mimicking the bat's social interaction. The algorithm's core components include an initial population, a position vector for each individual, a frequency parameter representing exploration intensity, and a loudness parameter controlling the convergence rate. Mathematical formulations describing the update rules for position, frequency, and loudness are detailed. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods. The results indicate that BBB offers a robust and adaptable approach for solving complex optimization challenges.

title: Fractal-Based Constraint Relaxation
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for applying constraint relaxation to fractal-based systems, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency of optimization processes. We leverage the inherent properties of fractals – their self-similarity, complex geometry, and recursive structure – to generate a diverse set of constraints that are distributed across a larger space. This approach reduces computational cost while maintaining the structural integrity of the fractal system, offering a promising avenue for tackling complex optimization problems. The core mechanism centers around the creation of fractal-derived constraints, strategically positioned to improve the exploration of the solution space and ultimately lead to more robust and efficient optimization results.

title: Quantum-Inspired Simulation of Biological Neuronal Networks
abstract: Biological neuronal networks represent a fundamental component of complex systems, including the brain. Simulating these networks accurately and efficiently is a significant challenge, largely due to the intricate, non-linear interactions between neurons. Traditional simulation methods, often relying on numerical integration techniques like the Hodgkin-Huxley model, are computationally intensive, particularly when scaling to large networks. This paper proposes a novel approach to neuronal network simulation inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically leveraging concepts of superposition and entanglement. We introduce a framework that utilizes quantum-inspired algorithms to represent and evolve neuronal states, aiming to dramatically reduce computational overhead. The core idea involves mapping neuronal dynamics onto a quantum system, where neurons are represented by qubits, and synaptic connections are modeled as quantum gates. The simulation process then utilizes quantum algorithms to evolve the system, effectively capturing the parallel and interconnected nature of neuronal networks. We present a mathematical formulation of the simulation process, focusing on the evolution equation for neuronal states. We explore key concepts like wave function collapse and measurement in the context of neuronal network simulation, offering a potential pathway for more realistic and efficient modeling of biological neural systems. The ultimate goal is to provide a computationally tractable method for simulating large-scale neuronal networks, leading to improved understanding of brain function and potentially facilitating the development of advanced neurotechnologies. The presented framework offers a distinct alternative to conventional methods, promising significant advantages in terms of speed and scalability.

title: Angola Colobus-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Colobus," inspired by the foraging behavior of Angola colobus monkeys. These monkeys exhibit a complex and adaptive strategy for locating food resources, characterized by exploration, exploitation, and a dynamic adjustment of search parameters based on environmental feedback. The Colobus algorithm leverages these principles to develop a new optimization technique. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism, utilizing a 'resource density' concept mirroring the colobus's assessment of food availability. This density is dynamically adjusted through a weighted sum of past successful moves and random exploration. The algorithm employs a population-based approach with a unique 'social learning' component, where individuals share information about promising regions of the search space, promoting convergence while maintaining exploration capabilities. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that Colobus is a promising approach for tackling complex optimization challenges, particularly those exhibiting non-convexity and multi-modality.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Graph Strategies: An Adaptive Aggregation Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive aggregation strategy for quantum graphs based on nonlinear quantum graphs. Traditional quantum graph aggregation methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, which struggle to adapt to dynamic input data. We propose a dynamic self-organizing aggregation approach, leveraging the inherent non-linearity of quantum graphs to dynamically adjust aggregation parameters, thereby enhancing quantum algorithm performance. The core mechanism involves establishing a dynamic self-organizing structure within the quantum graph, allowing for adaptive weighting of graph elements based on input data. This approach addresses the limitations of static aggregation techniques and offers a promising path toward improved quantum computation. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in a specific quantum algorithm.

title: Title: Adaptive Error Correction in Quantum Error Correction Networks
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical enabling technology for quantum computation, offering the potential for fault-tolerant quantum computers. However, the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates sophisticated error correction schemes. Static error correction protocols, while conceptually simple, struggle to maintain optimal performance in the presence of fluctuating error rates. This paper introduces an adaptive error correction scheme leveraging Bayesian principles and a dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm to enhance the fidelity of quantum computations. The core mechanism centers on a 'Bayesian Error Correction' algorithm that continuously monitors error rates and dynamically adjusts correction parameters to maximize quantum fidelity. We analyze the potential advantages of this approach, focusing on improved robustness and adaptability to evolving error profiles within quantum error correction networks. The proposed scheme is presented with detailed mathematical formulations and illustrative examples, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and simulation.

title: Graph Embeddings with Contrastive Learning for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) is a crucial task in leveraging the wealth of information stored in knowledge graphs. Traditional graph embedding methods often struggle to capture the complex relationships and structural nuances within these graphs, leading to suboptimal performance in tasks such as link prediction. This paper proposes a novel approach to KGC utilizing contrastive learning. We introduce a model that learns entity embeddings by explicitly contrasting similar and dissimilar entities within the knowledge graph. This is achieved through a carefully designed contrastive loss function that encourages embeddings of related entities to be close together while pushing embeddings of unrelated entities apart. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showing significant improvements compared to established graph embedding techniques. The core claim is that contrastive learning provides a powerful mechanism for enhancing the quality of graph embeddings. The primary mechanism involves learning to differentiate between similar and dissimilar entities using a contrastive loss. This new approach offers a promising direction for advancing KGC research.

title: The Pecking Parrot Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Woodpecker Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Pecking Parrot Metaheuristic (PPMH), a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of woodpeckers. PPMH leverages the woodpecker's instinctive pecking strategy, characterized by alternating between exploratory and exploitative phases, to navigate search spaces effectively. The algorithm incorporates a 'pecking radius' parameter to define the search area, a 'peck frequency' to control the balance between exploration and exploitation, and a 'memory' mechanism mimicking the woodpecker's retention of preferred feeding locations. PPMH's core mechanism involves iteratively selecting points within a defined radius, evaluating their fitness, and adjusting the search area based on the best fitness found. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, PPMH's design emphasizes adaptability and resilience in complex, multi-dimensional search landscapes, aiming for rapid convergence while avoiding premature convergence. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and conceptual basis, highlighting its potential advantages over existing methods.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Wavefunction Collapse for Signal Processing
abstract: Quantum-enhanced wavefunction collapse offers a potentially transformative approach to signal processing, addressing limitations in traditional computational methods. This paper explores the concept of utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to accelerate the collapse of a wavefunction, resulting in enhanced detection and filtering capabilities. We delve into a proposed quantum algorithm that strategically manipulates quantum states to expedite this crucial step in the signal processing pipeline. The core mechanism involves a carefully designed quantum circuit that exploits the inherent properties of entanglement and superposition to drastically reduce the time required for wavefunction evaluation. This research investigates the theoretical underpinnings, potential advantages, and challenges associated with this quantum-driven paradigm shift. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a significant improvement in detection and filtering accuracy compared to classical algorithms.

title: Title: Fractal Dimension-Based Parameter Tuning for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of fractal dimension as a parameter tuning method for machine learning models. Traditional parameter optimization methods often rely on grid search or gradient descent, which can be computationally expensive and may not always converge to optimal solutions. We propose a novel approach where the model's performance is continuously monitored using fractal dimension, allowing for adaptive adjustments to parameters to maximize predictive accuracy. The core mechanism involves establishing a relationship between the fractal dimension and model performance, iteratively refining parameter values based on this relationship. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method in several benchmark datasets, showcasing potential improvements in model generalization and performance compared to existing techniques. The research explores the benefits of this approach in scenarios where model complexity is high, and parameter optimization is crucial for achieving desired performance.

title: SpecMind: Enabling Spectrum Intelligence via Multi-Agent Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: The exponential growth of wireless devices is driving unprecedented spectrum demand, pushing spectrum management toward more fine-grained decisions across space, time, and device constraints. As a result, spectrum policymakers and engineers must process large volumes of data that come from diverse sources and take many different forms, such as text and tables. These data sources are often disaggregated and require significant time and effort to integrate, search, and interpret. Furthermore, most of this information is formatted for human understanding and is not readily accessible to automated systems. To address this challenge, we propose SpecMind, a novel Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system for spectrum intelligence that performs reasoning over heterogeneous data sources. This system enables autonomous agents to coordinate specialized sub-agents that retrieve and synthesize knowledge across policy proceedings, legal regulations, and license databases. We develop SpecBench, a question and answer (Q&A) dataset based on real-world license records and policy proceedings, addressing the lack of evaluation resources for RAG systems in the spectrum domain. Experimental results demonstrate that SpecMind outperforms traditional, general-purpose RAG systems across spectrum-related tasks, achieving over 80% win rate against strong baselines. The agent-based design enables more accurate retrieval, better contextual reasoning, and improved task completion across diverse query types.

title: VIBE: Video Instruction-aligned Background music gEneration
abstract: Current video-to-music (V2M) models lack semantic control and fail to penalize instruction violations, largely due to their reliance on reconstruction objectives and the representational bottleneck of static cross-modal conditioning in Diffusion Autoregressive (DAR) architectures. To resolve this, we introduce VIBE, a novel text-and-video-to-music (T+V2M) generation model that leverages: (1) Conditioning Connection, a depth-wise cross-layer conditioning mechanism that dynamically bridges the planning and diffusion refinement heads and (2) a comprehensive reward modeling taxonomy, optimizing for both hard, verifiable constraints (e.g., tempo, key) and soft, subjective qualities (e.g., musicality, multimodal alignment) with a structured 5-stage training curriculum. Upon evaluation using audio-visual alignment, instruction following, and audio quality metrics, along with a subjective human evaluation study, we observe that VIBE demonstrates enhanced controllability and instruction adherence while performing comparably to most evaluated baselines on generation fidelity and multimodal alignment.

title: Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Agent Credit Assignment
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to decentralized federated reinforcement learning (DFRL) that tackles the critical challenge of multi-agent credit assignment. Traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) struggles to scale effectively in decentralized settings due to the difficulty in determining which agents are responsible for the overall reward. Our method introduces a decentralized credit assignment algorithm leveraging Shapley values, providing a fair and efficient mechanism for distributing rewards among agents. Combined with a communication protocol, this architecture enables scalable and robust learning across multiple agents operating independently. The core claim is that innovative credit assignment solutions are necessary to scale MARL in decentralized environments. This work offers a foundational framework for developing more practical and effective DFRL systems.

title: High-Order Quantum Phase Transition Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high-order quantum phase transition algorithm designed to precisely simulate and control quantum phase transitions. Traditional approaches often struggle with the complexity of these transitions, limiting their applicability to materials optimization and design. This algorithm leverages a sophisticated quantum simulation framework and advanced operations to achieve accurate modeling and control, offering a significant advancement in this field. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic quantum state evolution, guided by a tailored control scheme, facilitating the exploration of multiple phase transitions simultaneously. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework and demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of applied examples, showcasing its potential for rapid and accurate material design. The algorithm's focus is on enhancing the ability to predict and manipulate phase transitions, thereby unlocking new possibilities in materials science.

title: Title: Hierarchical Geometric Modeling for Neural Network Interpretability
abstract: Neural networks are increasingly deployed in various applications, but their complex internal representations often hinder interpretability. This paper proposes a novel hierarchical geometric modeling approach to decompose neural network activations into smaller, more understandable components. We develop a nested model structure, where each level represents a simpler geometric abstraction. This allows us to analyze the network's decision-making process through the lens of geometric intuition, offering a potential pathway toward improved model transparency and explainability. The core mechanism involves constructing a hierarchical model, progressively simplifying the network's representation. This framework will be tested with a variety of neural network architectures, and the results will demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in identifying key factors influencing network behavior.

title: Title: Emergent Information Coding via Modular Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the potential of modular neural networks to achieve self-organization and distributed intelligence. Traditional neural networks are often viewed as deterministic, limiting their ability to exhibit complex, adaptive behavior. We propose a novel architecture – modular neural networks – that leverages interconnected units to encode and propagate information through a system of communication and exchange, fostering emergent behavior without explicit control. The core mechanism centers around the design of modular units that dynamically adapt and communicate, enabling the network to spontaneously reorganize itself. This approach moves beyond the limitations of traditional deep learning by introducing a fundamental shift in how information is processed and represented. We present preliminary results demonstrating the emergence of complex patterns and functionalities within a modular network, suggesting a paradigm shift towards more robust and adaptable AI systems.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint Feedback Loops in Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Evolutionary algorithms have proven effective in solving complex optimization problems, but often struggle with finding optimal solutions, particularly in dynamic and uncertain environments. This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm that leverages dynamic constraint feedback loops to actively shape the evolution of constraints. We propose a mechanism for continuous monitoring of algorithm performance and adaptive constraint adjustment based on the outcomes of previous iterations. This approach aims to enhance the algorithm's ability to navigate complex landscapes and discover optimal solutions more efficiently. The core claim is that this dynamic constraint feedback loop significantly improves the effectiveness of evolutionary algorithms by integrating feedback.

title: Distributed Differential Privacy via Graph-Based Correlation Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to achieving stronger differential privacy guarantees in distributed machine learning settings. The core idea centers around leveraging the inherent correlations between data points within a distributed network, represented as a graph. We propose utilizing a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to learn a "correlation embedding" that explicitly models these relationships. This embedding is then used to refine the privacy protection applied during model updates, effectively masking individual contributions while maintaining the overall accuracy of the learning process. Our method represents a significant departure from traditional aggregation techniques, offering a more nuanced and adaptive approach to privacy preservation in the face of complex data dependencies. We demonstrate the potential for improved privacy bounds and accuracy through theoretical analysis and illustrate the concept with a conceptual framework. This approach provides a pathway towards more robust and practical distributed machine learning systems where privacy and utility are effectively balanced.

title: Quantum Entanglement Non-Asymmetry Computation – Topological Information Coding
abstract: Quantum entanglement forms the bedrock of quantum computing, offering unique capabilities for computation and communication. This paper investigates a novel non-asymmetric computation framework predicated on the manipulation of entangled states, aiming to unlock its potential for information encoding and processing. We propose a computational model centered around the exploitation of entanglement's inherent asymmetries, designing algorithms to leverage these properties for data manipulation and computation. Our work explores the theoretical implications of this approach, highlighting the potential for achieving significant advancements in quantum information processing. Specifically, this research investigates the feasibility of utilizing entangled states to perform complex calculations and offers a preliminary assessment of the framework's potential for quantum algorithms. The core claim is that this approach offers a distinct path toward quantum computing, leveraging the unique properties of entanglement.

title: Black-headed Spider Monkey Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Black-headed Spider Monkey Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSMMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of black-headed spider monkeys. These monkeys exhibit complex strategies for food acquisition, including exploration, exploitation, and adaptive movement patterns. The BSMMA leverages these observed behaviors to develop a new optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, incorporating elements of Lévy flight, adaptive step size adjustment, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. The core of the algorithm is a 'hunting' mechanism mimicking the spider monkey's search for food, where individuals move strategically through the search space, adjusting their movement based on food density estimations. The performance of the BSMMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's adaptability and robustness are highlighted, and future research directions are discussed. The primary objective is to provide a robust and efficient optimization method drawing inspiration from the intricate foraging strategies of a fascinating primate. The algorithm's key parameters are designed to reflect the adaptive nature observed in spider monkey behavior. The results show that BSMMA can outperform traditional metaheuristic algorithms in certain problem landscapes.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Chaos Simulation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, presents a revolutionary approach to simulating complex systems, particularly chaotic dynamics. This research explores the potential of leveraging entanglement to create a novel simulation technique, aiming to achieve more stable and predictable chaos behavior than currently employed methods. The core mechanism centers around designing a highly sophisticated entanglement algorithm that actively monitors and manipulates entanglement states, introducing carefully controlled decoherence events to induce specific chaotic dynamics. This paper details the design of such an algorithm, its underlying principles, and the potential implications for understanding and, potentially, controlling chaotic systems. We present a framework for generating and analyzing chaotic behavior through the application of quantum entanglement, highlighting the advantages and challenges associated with this approach.

title: ## Big Free-tailed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Big Free-tailed Bat" (BFB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the big free-tailed bat (Syracuseya brevicauda). These bats exhibit sophisticated strategies for locating food sources in complex and dynamic environments. The BFB algorithm leverages these strategies, specifically their echolocation and movement patterns, to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, mimicking the bats' collective search process. Key components include a position representation based on bat location and flight direction, an energy function reflecting the success of a bat in finding food, and a communication mechanism inspired by bat social interactions. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment of flight direction and a probabilistic exploration strategy to avoid premature convergence. This paper details the theoretical framework, algorithm design, and a conceptual analysis of the BFB algorithm. We demonstrate its potential applicability across a range of optimization challenges, highlighting its adaptability and performance relative to established metaheuristic techniques. The algorithm's core mechanism relies on the following formulaic representations: `x_i(t) = x_i(t-1) + α * rand() * (x_best(t-1) - x_i(t-1))`, where `x_i(t)` is the position of the i-th bat at time t, `x_i(t-1)` is the position of the i-th bat at the previous time step, `x_best(t-1)` is the best position found so far, `α` is the learning rate, and `rand()` is a random number between 0 and 1. The energy function is defined as `E_i(t) = -log(fitness(x_i(t)))`, where `fitness(x_i(t))` represents the fitness of the i-th bat at time t. The algorithm's convergence is monitored through the tracking of the best fitness value: `f_best(t) = max{fitness(x_i(t)) | i = 1, 2, ..., N}`, where N is the population size. The algorithm's exploration strategy employs a probability distribution: `P(direction) = A * (1 - exp(-β * distance))`, where `A` is a scaling factor, `β` is a steepness parameter, and `distance` is the distance to the best solution.

title: Based on Evolutionary Algorithms for Hardware Design Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic algorithms, to the optimization of hardware design. The core claim is that evolutionary algorithms can effectively automate the process of enhancing both the performance and power consumption of hardware systems. The mechanism involves representing hardware design parameters as genes within a population, utilizing a genetic algorithm to drive iterative evolution, and employing selection, crossover, and mutation operators to refine the design. This approach offers a novel design methodology with the potential to significantly improve hardware efficiency. We present a framework for this approach and discuss its potential benefits and challenges. The focus is on the conceptual design and algorithmic foundations, without the need for experimental validation.

title: # Bear-Sloth: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavioral Patterns of Bears and Sloths
abstract: This paper introduces Bear-Sloth, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core inspiration stems from the unique behavioral patterns observed in bears and sloths – the bear's deliberate, methodical searching for food, and the sloth's slow, deliberate movement and clinging to trees. Bear-Sloth combines elements of Simulated Annealing (SA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with a novel "Momentum-Adaptive Exploration" mechanism, mimicking the bear's foraging strategy and the sloth's stability. The algorithm incorporates a 'resting' phase, mirroring the sloth's inactivity, and a 'searching' phase, analogous to the bear's active searching. The performance of Bear-Sloth is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with improved convergence speed and robustness compared to standard PSO and SA. Key features include adaptive inertia weights, a dynamically adjusted exploration rate, and a 'resting' phase to escape local optima. The algorithm's design aims for a balance between exploration and exploitation, leading to efficient optimization performance.

title: ## The Kiwi-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (KIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Kiwi-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (KIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies and navigational abilities of the New Zealand kākāpō (Kiwi parrot). KIMO leverages the kākāpō's unique combination of scent-based navigation, localized foraging, and risk-averse decision-making to achieve efficient and robust optimization. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a scent-gradient-based exploration phase, a localized search utilizing a 'patch' concept mirroring the kākāpō's territorial behavior, and a risk-averse adjustment mechanism reflecting the bird's cautious approach to novel food sources. KIMO aims to provide a more adaptable and resilient optimization strategy, particularly in complex and uncertain environments. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the mathematical formulations governing its core components and emphasizing its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Every Nonrecursive Many-One Degree Contains Either One or Infinitely Many Finite-One Degrees
abstract: This paper proves that every nonrecursive many-one degree contains either exactly one or infinitely many finite-one degrees. This gives a negative answer to Open Question 2 of Richter, Stephan, and Zhang~\cite[p.~17]{RSZ}. Earlier work established that, for almost every AsubseteqN with respect to the standard product measure on 2^N, the degree [A]_{m} contains an infinite antichain of finite-one degrees~Cintioli. Thus the question had already received an almost-sure negative answer; the present theorem settles it for every nonrecursive many-one degree.

title: Manacá-1B: An Open, Reproducible Brazilian-Portuguese Language Model and a Tokenizer-Aware, Paired Evaluation
abstract: Brazilian Portuguese remains under-served by open language models, and the few that exist are difficult to reproduce and are often compared without measures of uncertainty. We release Manacá-1B, an open decoder-only model of 1.72 billion parameters trained from scratch for Brazilian Portuguese with a fully containerized, reproducible pipeline. The pretraining is stable, with zero skipped or NaN steps and self-recovering loss spikes, and we release its full log and dynamics. We evaluate the model against nine open baselines on four Portuguese benchmarks under a single harness. Every comparison reports a standard error and a paired significance test, and the harness is validated against previously published numbers. On last-word prediction Manacá-1B is the strongest model below the 7B scale, exceeding both Tucano-1b1 and Tucano-2b4 on LAMBADA-PT with large paired margins; it is competitive on commonsense completion and near chance on multiple-choice reasoning, as are all small base models. Along the way we document a concrete evaluation pitfall: converting a SentencePiece tokenizer with case-folding normalization to the HuggingFace fast format silently drops the normalizer, routing every capitalized token to byte-fallback and depressing scores in a way that is invisible in aggregate metrics. The uncorrected tokenizer lowered LAMBADA-PT accuracy from 45.3 to 25.0; we quantify the effect and provide a one-line fix that reproduces the training tokenizer exactly. Code, raw training and evaluation logs, per-example prediction vectors, the model weights, and the corrected tokenizer are released so that every number in this paper can be recomputed.

title: The Voronoi of Data: A Narrative Review of K-Means Clustering, from MacQueen's Method to Careful Seeding and the Triangle Inequality
abstract: K-means is unsupervised learning's workhorse: partition the data by minimizing distances to means---an objective whose simplicity hides a hard optimization, a sensitive initialization, and a fifty-year engineering record. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that workhorse. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the origins and convergence, in which Steinhaus's objective, Forgy's and MacQueen's methods, Lloyd's quantization algorithm, and Selim and Ismail's convergence theorem fixed the algorithm's mathematical frame; the efficiency and initialization era, in which BIRCH's summaries, Bradley's database scaling, Elkan's triangle-inequality pruning, Kanungo's analysis, and Arthur--Vassilvitskii's k-means++ seeding made the method scale and stabilized its starts; and the theory's extensions, in which Jain's fifty-year retrospective and Xing's metric learning reframed the question the means answer. It is concluded that k-means' history is the field's lesson in productive simplicity: an objective that everyone can state, an algorithm everyone can run, and a literature whose every paper---convergence, seeding, pruning, metrics---is the answer to one of the simple idea's hidden questions.

title: Title: Dynamically Generated Modular Quantum Circuits
abstract: Quantum computing is rapidly advancing, driven by the need for scalable and adaptable architectures. Modular quantum circuits, where individual components can be combined and rearranged, offer a promising path towards this goal. This paper introduces a novel dynamic system for generating modular quantum circuits – the "Adaptive Circuit Generation" algorithm – which iteratively adds and removes modules based on input data, allowing for evolution and the creation of circuits capable of adapting to diverse conditions. This approach represents a significant departure from traditional static circuit design methods, providing a flexible and dynamic framework for quantum system development.

title: 基于自适应参数调整的联邦学习 (Adaptive Parameter Adjustment Federated Learning)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning technique that enables training models on decentralized data sources while preserving data privacy. However, traditional FL approaches often rely on global model updates, which can be vulnerable to adversarial attacks and suboptimal performance on heterogeneous data. This paper proposes a novel framework called Adaptive Parameter Adjustment Federated Learning (APAFL) that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on local data characteristics, enhancing model robustness and privacy. We present a mechanism for adaptive parameter adjustment using a weighted aggregation of local model updates, mitigating the impact of noisy data and promoting better generalization. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in model accuracy and privacy compared to existing FL techniques.

title: Hierarchical Evolution of Topology in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) by introducing an evolutionary mechanism focused on the hierarchical topology of agent connections. Traditional MARL primarily concentrates on optimizing individual agent policies, often neglecting the significant impact of the network structure on overall system performance. We propose a framework where agents dynamically evolve their communication topologies through reinforcement learning, guided by their collaborative outcomes. This evolution is driven by a competitive and cooperative process, allowing agents to adapt their connections to form a more efficient and robust network. The core claim is that by strategically evolving the topology, we can significantly improve the collaborative efficiency of multi-agent systems. The key mechanism involves agents exchanging information via communication and adjusting their connection topologies based on observed performance. This approach represents a shift from solely policy optimization to a holistic system-level optimization strategy. The proposed methodology offers a promising path towards designing truly adaptive and intelligent multi-agent systems.

title: Title: Cognitive Resonance Networks for Algorithmic Coherence
abstract: Cognitive Resonance Networks (CRNs) represent a promising paradigm for advancing neural network learning, particularly in the context of algorithmic coherence. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging cognitive resonance – the tendency for neural networks to converge on similar states – to enhance the stability and reliability of learning algorithms. We propose a novel attention mechanism that actively promotes the formation of these resonant states, fostering a feedback loop that encourages convergence. The core claim is that incorporating CRNs can mitigate instability and divergence, ultimately leading to improved algorithmic coherence. This work explores the theoretical implications of cognitive resonance and its practical implementation within neural network architectures. The paper will present a detailed analysis of the proposed attention mechanism and its impact on training dynamics, offering a framework for leveraging this phenomenon to improve the performance of various algorithmic tasks.

title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Neural Network Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of deep neural networks from an information-theoretic perspective. Traditional methods for analyzing neural network behavior often rely on gradient-based approaches or black-box testing, which can be insufficient for understanding the underlying mechanisms driving network evolution. We propose a novel framework utilizing entropy, mutual information, and related measures to quantify information flow within the network's activation space. This approach aims to identify critical information bottlenecks, assess the complexity of internal representations, and ultimately, contribute to the design of more efficient and robust neural network architectures. We demonstrate the application of these measures across several simplified network architectures, illustrating the potential for extracting meaningful insights into dynamic behavior. The core contribution lies in shifting the analytical focus from network output to the internal information processing, offering a new lens for understanding and controlling neural network dynamics.
