title: Blockchain-Based Federated Learning with Differential Privacy
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, traditional FL systems remain vulnerable to privacy breaches and data manipulation. This paper proposes a novel blockchain-based architecture that addresses these concerns by integrating data provenance tracking, integrity verification, and differential privacy mechanisms. The system leverages blockchain technology to create an immutable record of model updates and data contributions, ensuring transparency and accountability. Simultaneously, differential privacy techniques are applied during the training process to protect the privacy of individual data contributors. This combined approach significantly enhances the security and trustworthiness of FL systems, enabling secure and collaborative model training across diverse data sources. The proposed system utilizes cryptographic hashing and Merkle trees to guarantee data integrity and employs noise injection strategies within differential privacy mechanisms to protect user data. The core contribution is a secure and verifiable FL framework with enhanced privacy guarantees.

title: Knowledge Graph Completion Model Based on Semantic Constrained Hybrid Scoring
abstract: Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims to predict missing links in knowledge bases. However, existing methods often struggle with reasoning over complex semantic relations and generate predictions that violate common-sense logic. In this paper, a knowledge graph completion model based on semantic constrained hybrid scoring (SCHS) is proposed, which integrates three synergistic mechanisms. First, an Adaptive Feature Gating (AFG) mechanism is designed for feature recalibration. Unlike static embeddings, this module dynamically recalibrates the importance of different semantic aspects based on the relation context. Second, a Relation-Concept Matrix Projection (RCMP) mechanism is introduced to act as an explicit semantic constraint. This mechanism maps triplets to a latent concept space to capture the inherent consistency between relations and concepts, providing a penalization mechanism to filter out noise that is topologically close but semantically invalid. Third, an Adaptive Fusion Strategy (AFS) utilizing a soft-start mechanism is introduced to effectively balance structural and semantic scores without early-training collapses. This tri-fold synergy essentially resolves the rigid trade-off between geometric alignment and flexible semantic matching. Extensive experiments on the WN18RR and FB15k-237 datasets demonstrate that SCHS achieves substantial performance improvements, verifying the robustness and effectiveness of the dynamically regulated fusion of semantics and structures in the alleviation of long-tail errors.

title: Impact of Channel Integration on Brand Equity Empowered Based on Deep Learning and Graph Neural Network Approaches
abstract: This study employs a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to identify predictive associations between channel integration structures and brand equity, with a particular focus on heterogeneous nodes and multi-relation edges in multi-channel commercial data. A Multi-Relation Integrated Graph Neural Network (MRI-GNN) is developed by incorporating node alfeature fitting, relation weight learning, and ensemble message passing into a unified optimization process. In the generalization evaluation, MRI-GNN achieves an accuracy of 93.54% and a recall of 92.39% for node classification on the Digital Bibliography & Library Project (DBLP) dataset, and an accuracy of 90.87% and a recall of 90.84% on the Association for Computing Machinery Citation Network dataset. When only 10% of the DBLP training data is used, the model still achieves an accuracy of 87.68%. In the brand equity prediction task based on multi-source commercial data, MRI-GNN achieves a root mean square error of 15.23, a mean absolute error of 12.11, and a coefficient of determination ([Formula: see text] of 0.81. Ablation results indicate that node feature fitting, information consistency, and price coordination make relatively substantial contributions to prediction performance. The results demonstrate that MRI-GNN can jointly represent node attributes and multi-relation structures, providing data-driven support for analyzing the association between channel integration and brand equity.

In the generalization evaluation, MRI-GNN achieves an accuracy of 93.54% and a recall of 92.39% for node classification on the Digital Bibliography & Library Project (DBLP) dataset, and an accuracy of 90.87% and a recall of 90.84% on the Association for Computing Machinery Citation Network dataset. When only 10% of the DBLP training data is used, the model still achieves an accuracy of 87.68%. In the brand equity prediction task based on multi-source commercial data, MRI-GNN achieves a root mean square error of 15.23, a mean absolute error of 12.11, and a coefficient of determination ([Formula: see text] of 0.81. Ablation results indicate that node feature fitting, information consistency, and price coordination make relatively substantial contributions to prediction performance. The results demonstrate that MRI-GNN can jointly represent node attributes and multi-relation structures, providing data-driven support for analyzing the association between channel integration and brand equity.

title: Safe policy optimization with stretchable penalties
abstract: In safe reinforcement learning (RL), ensuring cost-constraint satisfaction while minimizing the sacrifice of reward acquisition presents a significant challenge. This paper proposes an efficient safe RL algorithm called stretchable penalty-based safe policy optimization (S2P2O). S2P2O constructs a non-monotonic Swish-shaped penalty with a sign-changing gradient and a tunable stretched optimal penalty point, enabling a smooth transition from reward promotion to safety correction. A Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence stretching mechanism rescales the reward and penalty gradients based on the current reward and constraint status once the KL threshold is exceeded, enabling continued policy optimization and improved sample efficiency by fully utilizing collected trajectories. The theoretical error bound between the optimal values of the Swish-shaped objective and the original constrained objective is analyzed. Comprehensive experiments are conducted to benchmark S2P2O against several state-of-the-art safe RL algorithms. The results demonstrate that S2P2O exhibits enhanced cost constraint satisfaction, superior reward acquisition capacity, and accelerated cost convergence rates.

title: Puppeteer: Object-Grounded Posture-Aware Co-Speech Gesture Generation
abstract: Generating co-speech gestures that are temporally coherent, semantically aligned with speech, and grounded with surrounding objects remains challenging. Prior speech-driven gesture models emphasize audio-gesture alignment but do not explicitly account for posture constraints or surrounding objects, failing to capture the inherent correlation between body gestures and the physical space. We present Puppeteer, a posture-aware, object-grounded co-speech gesture diffusion model operating in a causal latent space. We decompose long gestures into structured primitives and learn a causal variational autoencoder that encodes them into temporally ordered latent tokens, each depending only on the past. We then perform conditional diffusion directly in the causal latent space, conditioning on speech signals, motion history, an initial posture reference, and object geometry to synthesize physically consistent gestures. This temporally ordered latent formulation enables explicit temporal control and supports tasks such as gesture in-betweening and gesture completion. To better assess co-speech gesture synthesis beyond existing measures, we introduce new evaluation metrics tailored to this task. We also created SceneGes, the first curated synthetic 3D dataset of embodied co-speech gestures and corresponding 3D objects, enabling object-grounded gesture generation. Experiments show that Puppeteer generates more diverse and temporally synchronized gestures than prior methods, while enabling object-grounded gesture synthesis.

title: LITERARYBIGFIVE: Author-Personalized Text Generation in a Unified Interpretable Space
abstract: Personalized text generation for authors and literary writing is essential for applications such as adaptive writing assistants, creative support tools, and computational literary analysis. However, existing approaches to author modeling and personalization often represent writing behavior as independent labels, requiring large-scale corpus collection or fine-tuning for each author or stylistic category. Such formulations are costly, difficult to interpret, and poorly suited for generalizing across authors. Inspired by the Big Five model's dimensional view of personality, we propose LiteraryBigFive, a framework that reframes authorial writing characteristics as coordinates within a unified and interpretable space. In this space, we derive each interpretable axis (e.g., Classicism, Emotionality) from activation-space contrasts between author-written and neutral passages, yielding distinct stylistic dimensions that allow texts or authors to be positioned within a five-dimensional system. Beyond localizing different authors, we further introduce an interpretable steering mechanism, which adaptively guides text generation toward target coordinates to perform author-personalized writing. Experimental results show that LiteraryBigFive improves authorial expressiveness while preserving semantic fidelity. The derived author per-axis scores strongly correlate with real-world literary consensus, offering transparent and interpretable explanations of author-specific generation behavior: https://github.com/Znull-1220/LiteraryBigFive.

abstract: Quantum topology offers a fundamentally new approach to computation by leveraging the unique properties of quantum states. This paper introduces a novel machine learning accelerator based on quantum topology, aiming to significantly enhance the training and inference speed of various machine learning algorithms. We detail the core mechanism of utilizing quantum superposition and entanglement to accelerate these processes, demonstrating its potential to overcome the limitations of classical computation in specific scenarios. This work explores the fundamental principles of quantum topology and presents a practical implementation of the proposed accelerator, highlighting its advantages and potential impact on machine learning research and applications.

title: Adversarial Training for Program Vulnerability Detection
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program vulnerability detection leveraging adversarial training. Traditional vulnerability detection methods often suffer from low efficiency and high error rates, relying heavily on manual analysis or brute-force techniques like fuzzing. We propose a machine learning model trained using adversarial examples to identify vulnerabilities within program code. The core mechanism involves generating adversarial samples – modified versions of the original code designed to fool the model – and training the model to correctly classify these samples as vulnerable. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and accurate method for vulnerability detection by exploiting the model's ability to learn robust representations of code and identify subtle anomalies indicative of flaws. The effectiveness of this technique is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining the methodology and potential benefits of adversarial training in the context of software security.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Geometry Transformation
abstract: Quantum state manipulation is a fundamental aspect of quantum information theory, and the development of robust and efficient methods for encoding and transmitting information is crucial. This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum state manipulation that leverages the inherent geometric properties of quantum states. We propose a method utilizing adaptive geometric transformations to encode and transmit quantum information, offering enhanced flexibility and potentially improved performance compared to traditional techniques. The core mechanism centers around the dynamic adjustment of a quantum state's geometry, enabling the encoding of complex data and facilitating novel quantum information transfer protocols. This research explores the potential of this technique, focusing on the encoding capabilities and efficiency of the resulting quantum states.

title: Quantum Security Protocols Based on Quantum Coherence Damping
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum coherence damping for enhancing the security of hardware security cryptographic protocols. The core claim centers on leveraging the inherent properties of quantum mechanics, specifically the controlled damping of quantum coherence, to design novel protocols with improved key secrecy and resistance to attacks. The proposed mechanisms involve tailoring key generation and transmission schemes based on manipulating the rate of decoherence within quantum bits (qubits). This approach aims to create a heightened level of security against eavesdropping attempts. The research explores potential breakthroughs in hardware security cryptography by integrating quantum coherence damping principles. We present a framework for constructing protocols that exploit this effect, focusing on practical considerations for implementation. The analysis demonstrates the theoretical advantages of this approach and outlines future research directions.

title: 基于图的知识图谱推理优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning by formulating the problem as an optimization task within a graph structure. Traditional knowledge graph reasoning methods often suffer from scalability issues and computational complexity, particularly when dealing with large knowledge graphs. Our proposed method addresses these limitations by transforming the reasoning process into a constraint satisfaction problem on a graph. This graph represents the knowledge graph and the reasoning rules are encoded as constraints. We then employ graph optimization algorithms, such as maximum flow and minimum cut algorithms, to efficiently solve the problem and derive the inferred relationships. The core of our approach lies in the efficient mapping of the knowledge graph's logical structure to a suitable graph representation, allowing for the application of powerful graph optimization techniques. This work demonstrates the potential for significantly enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of knowledge graph reasoning, particularly in scenarios involving large and complex knowledge graphs. The key contributions of this research are the formulation and application of graph optimization techniques to knowledge graph inference, and the demonstration of improved performance compared to traditional reasoning methods.

title: Black-faced Lion Tamarin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Black-faced Lion Tamarin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BLITA), designed for tackling complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the unique foraging behavior of the black-faced lion tamarin, a primate known for its highly efficient and adaptable search strategies in complex forest environments. BLITA leverages concepts such as territory defense, resource competition, and adaptive movement patterns to establish a robust search process. The core of the algorithm involves a dynamic population of agents, each representing a potential solution. These agents explore the search space, employing a combination of random movement, directed search based on gradient estimation, and territorial defense mechanisms to converge toward optimal solutions. We detail the algorithm's components, including the agent initialization, movement strategy, territory assignment, and competition rules. Theoretical analysis provides insights into the algorithm's convergence properties and computational complexity. Preliminary results on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate BLITA's competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. Future research directions include incorporating adaptive parameters and exploring applications in diverse fields.

title: Topological Quantum Error Correction Realization via Topological Quantum Computers
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing topological quantum computers to achieve robust quantum error correction. The core claim centers on leveraging the unique physical properties of topological quantum computers – specifically, their inherent topological protection – to implement topological quantum error correction schemes. The proposed mechanism involves designing a quantum error-correcting code based on the interactions between entangled topological qubits within a physical topological structure. This approach allows for distributed error detection and correction, theoretically offering superior error correction rates and reduced resource requirements compared to traditional, single-qubit-based methods. The work explores the fundamental principles and theoretical framework for achieving topological quantum error correction, outlining key considerations for code design, qubit connectivity, and error mitigation strategies. The central focus is on demonstrating the feasibility of a topologically protected quantum code, contributing to the advancement of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Bactrian Camel Optimization Algorithm for Complex Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Bactrian Camel Optimization Algorithm (BCOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Bactrian camels in the Gobi Desert. The algorithm mimics the camel's unique gait pattern – alternating between forward and backward movements – to efficiently explore the search space. BCOA utilizes a dynamic population size and a velocity control mechanism, simulating the camel's adaptive speed based on the terrain and food availability. The algorithm employs a novel distance metric to guide the movement of the camels, aiming to converge towards the optimal solution. The performance of BCOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results demonstrate that BCOA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for solving complex optimization problems across various domains. The core equation governing the camel's movement is: $v_i(t+1) = \alpha v_i(t) + \beta rand(t)$, where $v_i(t)$ is the velocity at time $t$, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are parameters controlling the velocity update, and $rand(t)$ is a random number between 0 and 1. The position update is then defined as: $x_i(t+1) = x_i(t) + v_i(t)$, where $x_i(t)$ is the position at time $t$. The distance metric is calculated as: $d(x_i, x_j) = |x_i - x_j|$, and the algorithm uses a weighted average of the distances to determine the direction of movement. The algorithm's parameters include population size ($N$), maximum iterations ($T$), step size ($\epsilon$), and a damping factor ($\gamma$). The effectiveness of BCOA is directly related to the careful tuning of these parameters.

title: 基于量子纠缠的参数优化
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, exhibits instantaneous correlations between particles, regardless of distance. This unique property has garnered significant attention for its potential applications across various fields, including optimization. This paper explores the utilization of quantum entanglement to design a novel parameter optimization algorithm, leveraging the instantaneous correlations to dynamically adjust and optimize complex system parameters. The core mechanism hinges on employing quantum algorithms to achieve precise parameter adjustments through the subtle influence of entangled states. We present a preliminary investigation demonstrating the feasibility of this approach, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of traditional parameter optimization techniques. The core claim focuses on the ability to dynamically adjust complex system parameters using quantum entanglement.

title: Title: Self-Referential Vector Spaces for Pattern Recognition
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for pattern recognition based on self-referential vector spaces. Conventional pattern recognition methods often leverage external features, which can be limited and require extensive feature engineering. Our approach constructs a vector space where elements are defined by the vector space itself, enabling a fundamentally different approach to identifying patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this system through a series of experiments, showcasing its ability to detect subtle anomalies and novel patterns not readily apparent through traditional methods. The core mechanism involves dynamically generating and manipulating vectors within this space, fostering a deeper understanding of the underlying structure of the data. This research addresses a gap in pattern recognition by leveraging the inherent properties of vector spaces to create a more robust and adaptable system. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical implications and potential future directions for this methodology.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamics with Adaptive Feedback
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits a remarkable degree of fragility and complexity. Traditional approaches to studying entanglement often rely on static measurements, limiting our ability to understand and control its dynamic evolution. This research investigates a novel framework for quantifying and controlling entanglement dynamics within complex quantum systems utilizing a dynamically adaptive feedback loop. We move beyond simple entanglement measurements by incorporating a real-time, multi-layered feedback mechanism that adjusts the entanglement state based on subtle changes in the environment, leveraging non-linear dynamics. The core claim is to develop a framework capable of predicting and manipulating entanglement behavior, offering a significant advancement over current theoretical models and experimental techniques. This work introduces a dynamic feedback algorithm that continuously assesses the system's state and adjusts the entanglement parameters to minimize errors and enhance coherence.

title: Serpentine Search: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Python Snake Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Serpentine Search, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the movement patterns of the python snake. The algorithm leverages the snake's ability to navigate complex terrains by adjusting its body curvature and direction, translating this behavior into a search strategy for solving optimization problems. Serpentine Search utilizes a population of "segments," each representing a potential solution, and employs a dynamic curvature adjustment mechanism to guide the segments towards the optimal solution. The algorithm's core innovation lies in its adaptive curvature function, which is influenced by both the gradient of the objective function and the distance to the current best solution. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, Serpentine Search prioritizes local exploration combined with strategic global shifts, mimicking the snake's efficient movement across diverse landscapes. evidence.title: Serpentine Search: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Python Snake Behavior
evidence.abstract: This paper introduces Serpentine Search, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the movement patterns of the python snake. The algorithm leverages the snake's ability to navigate complex terrains by adjusting its body curvature and direction, translating this behavior into a search strategy for solving optimization problems. Serpentine Search utilizes a population of "segments," each representing a potential solution, and employs a dynamic curvature adjustment mechanism to guide the segments towards the optimal solution. The algorithm's core innovation lies in its adaptive curvature function, which is influenced by both the gradient of the objective function and the distance to the current best solution. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, Serpentine Search prioritizes local exploration combined with strategic global shifts, mimicking the snake's efficient movement across diverse landscapes. The algorithm's performance is evaluated conceptually, outlining the key components and their interactions. Further research and experimental validation are planned to demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness across a broader range of optimization problems.

title: ## Aquatic Genet: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Aquatic Organisms
abstract: This paper presents Aquatic Genet, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the collective behavior and survival strategies observed in aquatic organisms, particularly fish schooling and coral reef colony dynamics. Aquatic Genet leverages concepts of chemotaxis, polarization, and cohesion to guide the search process, mimicking the adaptive responses of these organisms to environmental changes. The algorithm employs a population-based approach with a unique mechanism for individual movement and interaction, termed "Current Flow Adaptation" (CFA). CFA dynamically adjusts the influence of chemotaxis, polarization, and cohesion forces based on the local environment and the individual's proximity to the best-known solution. The performance of Aquatic Genet is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability and potential for addressing complex optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Individual Position Update: $x_{i}(t+1) = x_{i}(t) + \alpha \Delta x_i$, where $\alpha$ is a learning rate and $\Delta x_i$ is determined by the CFA mechanism (described in detail below). * Chemotaxis Influence: $C_i = \frac{1}{|S|} \sum_{j=1}^{|S|} (x_j - x_i) $, where $|S|$ is the population size and $x_j$ represents the position of each individual in the population. * Polarization Influence: $P_i = \beta \cdot \nabla C_i$, where $\beta$ is a polarization coefficient and $\nabla C_i$ is the gradient of the chemotaxis influence. * Cohesion Influence: $H_i = \gamma \cdot \sum_{j=1}^{|S|} \frac{x_j}{ |S| }$, where $\gamma$ is a cohesion coefficient. * CFA Update: $\Delta x_i = \eta (C_i + P_i + H_i) - \theta x_i$, where $\eta$ is a step size and $\theta$ is a damping factor. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, theoretical foundations, and experimental results, highlighting its strengths and potential areas for future research. ---

title: Annamite Crested Gibbon-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Annamite Crested Gibbon-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ACG-MHA), designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's design is inspired by the unique movement patterns and decision-making strategies observed in the Annamite Crested Gibbon ( *Nomascus annamiticus*), a primate species known for its agile navigation and resource selection within complex mountainous environments. ACG-MHA incorporates elements of exploration and exploitation, mimicking the gibbon's ability to efficiently search for optimal foraging locations while maintaining a degree of adaptability. The core of the algorithm revolves around a dynamically adjusted adaptive inertia weight scheme, a novel Lévy flight inspired probabilistic movement strategy, and a modified constriction heuristic. The performance of ACG-MHA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a combination of theoretical analysis and empirical testing. Results indicate that ACG-MHA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in several test scenarios. Future research directions include incorporating further insights from gibbon behavior and exploring its applicability to real-world engineering and scientific problems.

title: Reservoir Computing with Spiking Neural Networks and Temporal Coding
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) within a Reservoir Computing (RC) framework to efficiently process temporal data. The core argument is that SNNs, particularly when employing temporal coding schemes like the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire model, can effectively capture and encode time-varying dynamics, offering a biologically plausible approach to RC. We explore the theoretical foundations of this integration, focusing on how the recurrent structure of the SNN reservoir, combined with temporal coding, allows for robust and efficient temporal signal processing. The presented model outlines a system where the reservoir acts as a dynamic filter, and the temporal coding mechanism within the SNN facilitates the extraction of relevant temporal features from the input. This approach demonstrates a promising avenue for developing neural networks capable of handling complex time-series data, with potential applications in areas such as neuroscience, robotics, and signal processing. The key contribution lies in the synergy between the computational advantages of RC and the biologically inspired temporal coding within SNNs.

title: Bayesian Neural Network for Dynamical Systems with Emergent Constraints
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) architecture designed to model complex dynamical systems with emergent constraints. Traditional neural networks struggle with adapting to constantly changing environments, often resulting in brittle and unreliable predictions. Our approach leverages Bayesian inference to continuously refine constraints and predict behavior, fostering a system capable of adaptive learning and robust dynamical system modeling. The core mechanism centers around a probabilistic approach, enabling the network to estimate the probability distribution over possible solutions and dynamically update constraints based on observed data. We demonstrate the efficacy of this architecture through the application of a simplified, yet illustrative, dynamical system, showcasing improved predictive accuracy and a more nuanced understanding of emergent behavior compared to baseline approaches.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Parallel Wavelet Analysis for Signal Reconstruction
abstract: Quantum-enhanced parallel wavelet analysis offers a promising approach to signal reconstruction, particularly when dealing with correlated features. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum superposition and entanglement to accelerate the reconstruction process. We propose a novel quantum algorithm that leverages these quantum phenomena to achieve enhanced accuracy compared to classical methods. The core mechanism involves quantum state manipulation for efficient parallel computation of wavelet transform coefficients, addressing the inherent computational bottleneck in traditional wavelets analysis. This work investigates the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental results, demonstrating the potential for significant improvements in reconstruction accuracy, specifically in scenarios with complex correlations within the input signal data. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and challenges associated with implementing this quantum-enhanced approach.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks: Topology Analysis and Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of network topology on the self-organization of neural networks. We explore how specific topological features influence network dynamics, proposing a novel framework for optimizing neural networks through the application of topology-aware training and deployment strategies. The core claim is that a refined understanding of network topology enables enhanced model performance, efficiency, and robustness. This work introduces a mechanism that leverages topology to guide the optimization process, offering a significant advancement in neural network design and training.

title: Dr. Claw: An AI Scientist Workspace for Vibe Research
abstract: Command-line coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Gemini CLI) can already read and write files and sustain long sessions, yet end-to-end research still fragments across chat tools, IDEs, terminals, and writing environments, and the decisions that make it auditable are rarely preserved. We present Dr. Claw, an open-source workspace that wraps existing coding-agent executors in a controllable and auditable human-in-the-loop workflow rather than introducing another autonomous agent. Persistent state objects, a reusable skill library, and multi-executor coordination link human decisions to AI execution, turning planning, execution, and writing into one traceable, recoverable loop. We demonstrate Dr. Claw through an interactive three-view scenario and a failure-recovery walkthrough, and evaluate it against a bare command-line agent sharing the same backend executor, so the comparison contrasts the whole orchestration layer (task graph, state objects, and skill library) with the agent it wraps. Holding the executor fixed, Dr. Claw scores higher on research completeness while persisting an auditable, recoverable process trail. Demo access: repository https://github.com/OpenLAIR/dr-claw, released under AGPL-3.0 with GPL-3.0 upstream components.

title: Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions along vector fields
abstract: We investigate diffusion approximations for a class of multivariate inhomogeneous finite-velocity random motions motivated by models of active particles. A particle alternates cyclically among prescribed velocity fields V_1,dots,V_p with random run times and evolves according to either a flight dynamics, consisting of piecewise-linear motion, or a gliding dynamics, in which the particle follows the corresponding velocity flow. Under a Kac-type scaling that couples vanishing run times with diverging particle speed, we prove weak convergence of both processes to multidimensional diffusions. It turns out that the order of successive cyclic motions affects the diffusion limit. In addition to the second-order term generated by fluctuations of the random run times, the limiting drift contains directional derivatives DV_i[V_j] of the underlying vector fields. In Stratonovich form, part of this drift is expressed through their Lie brackets [V_i,V_j]. Thus, the generic non-commutativity of the microscopic motions survives the diffusive scaling and generates a macroscopic drift which depends on the cyclic order. The limiting drift also distinguishes the flight and gliding dynamics, despite their being driven by the same vector fields and run times. Several examples, including run-and-reverse motion and cyclic dynamics generated by multiple vector fields, illustrate how the cyclic switching protocol and the geometry of the underlying velocity fields shape the limiting diffusions.

title: HistoEncoder: A digital pathology foundation model for prostate cancer
abstract: Foundation models are trained on massive amounts of data to capture complex patterns in images. Subsequently, a wide range of downstream tasks can be adopted with minimal computational resources. We have developed HistoEncoder, a foundation model for prostate cancer digital pathology by pre-training on 48 million prostate tissue tile images. HistoEncoder allows automated extraction of histological features highly predictive of Gleason patterns achieving comparable performance with substantially larger pan-cancer foundation models while being much more efficient. By fine-tuning the model with a small amount of data and computational resources, we describe two clinical use cases for HistoEncoder. First, HistoEncoder can be used to automatically annotate large-scale datasets with high accuracy. Second, we show that HistoEncoder-derived histology clusters contain prognostic information of a similar magnitude to Gleason grading in internal cross-validation. Lightweight foundation models such as HistoEncoder allow organizations to build effective clinical software tools without the need for extensive datasets and heavy computing.

title: Hardware–Software Co-Evolution of Intelligence
abstract: Hardware–Software Co-Evolution of Intelligence (HSCI) develops a multi-substrate framework for understanding and engineering intelligence across physical, sensory, structural, neural, representational, and generative layers. Its foundational proposition is that intelligence does not necessarily begin with complete internal representation: a physical or sensory difference may already become intelligence-relevant when it acquires structural consequence by changing salience, routing, state, control, computation, or action. The repository develops Intelligence Before Representation, the Structural Consequence Boundary (SCB), Hardware Intelligence Primitives (HIPs), Pre-Representational Intelligence Primitives (PRIPs), Hardware Function Tunnels (HFTs), Per-Function Intelligence Placement, Selective Upward Escalation, Downward Structural Consolidation, multi-timescale intelligence, and multi-substrate Brain-Unit AI. It further proposes autonomous drones as a canonical engineering testbed for evaluating representation cost, salience-triggered computation, emergency Function Tunnels, energy, latency, reliability, and safety. The broader research direction treats hardware and software not as competing forms of intelligence but as co-evolving substrates in which flexible higher-level intelligence can discover useful structural regularities and stable regularities can become candidates for cheaper structural realization.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for learning probabilistic models by dynamically adjusting the parameters of the probability distribution based on the data's inherent uncertainty. Traditional approaches often rely on static parameter settings, limiting the model's ability to accurately capture the underlying data distribution. This research proposes a mechanism that iteratively refines the probability distribution parameters based on observed uncertainty, resulting in improved prediction accuracy and robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on diverse datasets, showcasing its superior performance compared to existing methods. The core mechanism leverages a dynamic uncertainty estimation technique to guide parameter adjustments, offering a more adaptable and potentially more accurate approach to probabilistic modeling.

title: Quantum-Inspired Lattice Optimization - Adaptive Lattice Density Adjustment
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm, Quantum-Inspired Lattice Optimization (QILO), designed to address challenges in geometric optimization, specifically focusing on the placement of lattice points. Traditional lattice optimization methods often struggle with complex geometries and high-dimensional spaces. We introduce a quantum-inspired approach that utilizes superposition and interference to guide the placement of lattice points, enabling the exploration of a wider solution space and improved convergence. We detail the algorithm's core mechanism, explain the quantum state concept, and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of illustrative examples. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for various geometric optimization problems.

title: A Device-Agnostic Framework for Personalized Anomaly Detection in Wearable and Mobile Ecosystems: Applications in Personal Safety and Respiratory Health Surveillance
abstract: Abstract—This paper presents a reformulated, device-agnostic architectural framework for two interrelated applications: (i) personalized audio-based personal safety threat detection, and (ii) respiratory pattern anomaly detection for early-stage epidemiological screening. Originating from an ideation dialogue, the proposed concepts are critically re-examined against fundamental constraints in machine learning, embedded systems, privacy engineering, and sensor heterogeneity. We propose a generalized abstraction layer that decouples sensing modality from inference logic, enabling deployment across heterogeneous smart devices (wearables, smartphones, IoT nodes) without hardware-specific dependencies. We address the zero-positive-example training problem through a reformulation as one-class classification and temporal anomaly detection. Privacy is preserved via on-device federated feature extraction with no raw data transmission. We further analyze the practical limitations identified by domain experts and propose mitigations grounded in current literature. The framework is positioned as a foundational architecture rather than a deployable product, inviting interdisciplinary validation. Impact Statement—By introducing a sensing abstraction layer and reformulating personal safety and respiratory monitoring as one-class anomaly detection problems, this work provides a portable, privacy-preserving architecture that can operate across heterogeneous consumer devices without hardware-specific redesign. The framework addresses the zero-positive-example constraint inherent to rare-event detection and offers a structured research agenda for empirical validation, potentially accelerating the development of reliable, edge-deployed health and safety monitoring systems. Index Terms—Anomaly detection, one-class classification, device-agnostic computing, respiratory pattern analysis, personal safety systems, federated learning, wearable computing, edge inference.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Tensor Clustering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to non-linear geometric tensor clustering, aiming to identify and cluster complex, non-linear geometric features within tensor sets. Traditional clustering algorithms often assume a uniform distribution, which is inadequate for capturing the inherent complexities found in non-linear geometry. Our method leverages dynamic geometric tensors and incorporates self-adaptive geometric transformations, combined with Gaussian integrals and Gaussian processes, to build robust and insightful cluster models. The core mechanism involves identifying and quantifying non-linear relationships through dynamic geometric transformations, ultimately leading to a deeper understanding of the underlying geometric structure. This work represents a significant advancement over existing algorithms, offering a more nuanced and accurate approach to clustering, particularly when dealing with intricate non-linear geometric configurations.

title: Quantum Decoherence-Driven Adaptive Hardware Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum hardware optimization leveraging the inherent characteristics of quantum decoherence. The core idea is to construct an adaptive system that continuously monitors and corrects quantum errors arising from decoherence, ultimately enhancing the performance and stability of quantum computations. The proposed method utilizes a feedback loop where the degree of decoherence experienced by quantum bits is measured and quantified. This measurement serves as an optimization signal, which is then processed by a reinforcement learning algorithm. The algorithm dynamically adjusts hardware parameters – such as pulse shapes, durations, and frequencies – to minimize the detrimental effects of decoherence and maximize the preservation of quantum superposition and coherence. Unlike conventional hardware optimization techniques that rely on offline calibration or fixed algorithms, this approach offers a real-time, adaptive response to decoherence, representing a significant advancement in quantum computing hardware development. The effectiveness of this strategy is predicated on the ability to accurately characterize and respond to decoherence in a manner that directly mitigates its impact on quantum computations. The research delves into the mathematical framework underpinning this adaptive system, detailing the relationships between measurement data, reinforcement learning parameters, and hardware adjustments.

title: Wavefunction Collapse with Quantum Information
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum information theory to the problem of wavefunction collapse, a fundamental challenge in quantum mechanics. We propose a novel quantum algorithm, termed "Quantum State-Aware Collapse" (QSAC), designed to enhance the accuracy of probabilistic predictions by dynamically adjusting the collapse probability based on observed quantum states. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors the quantum state, optimizing the collapse process to minimize errors. This research investigates the potential of QSAC to provide a more reliable and accurate approach to quantum computations, particularly within the context of quantum machine learning. The potential impact of this algorithm lies in its ability to improve the performance of quantum algorithms and provide a pathway towards harnessing quantum information for complex decision-making tasks.

title: Quantum Mirage: A Novel Algorithmic Approach to Data Privacy Protection
abstract: Data privacy is a paramount concern in the modern digital landscape, facing increasing threats from data breaches and surveillance. Traditional cryptographic methods, while effective, are increasingly vulnerable to computational attacks and are not inherently suited to address the unique challenges posed by sensitive data. This paper introduces Quantum Mirage, a novel algorithmic approach leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance data privacy and security. We propose a quantum-enhanced data distribution model and a modified version of the classical hidden Markov model (HMM) framework to achieve robust data protection. The core mechanism centers around exploiting quantum phenomena, specifically superposition and entanglement, to simulate data distributions with a significantly reduced risk of interception and analysis. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Quantum Mirage through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future research directions for this promising technology.

title: Beach Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Beach Mouse Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Beach Mouse, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of beach mice. These animals exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in dynamic and uncertain environments. The algorithm leverages key aspects of this behavior, including probabilistic movement, adaptive exploration, and a dynamic food source representation, to achieve robust and effective optimization performance. Beach Mouse employs a particle representation mimicking the mice's burrow locations, utilizes a probabilistic movement strategy based on gradient estimation and environmental cues, and incorporates a dynamic food source model that adapts to changes in the search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Beach Mouse through simulations and comparisons with established metaheuristic algorithms, showcasing its adaptability and potential for solving complex optimization problems. The core components of the algorithm are detailed, including the initial population generation, the movement strategy (described by equation (1)), the food source adaptation mechanism (described by equation (2)), and the acceptance criterion (described by equation (3)). The performance analysis highlights the algorithm's ability to maintain exploration while balancing exploitation, leading to improved convergence rates in several benchmark problems. title: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Robot Team Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robot team control leveraging the principles of multi-agent collaboration. The core idea is to design a system where a team of robots operates synergistically to achieve complex tasks. We employ reinforcement learning (RL) to train the control policies for each robot, allowing the team to adapt dynamically to changing environmental conditions and task objectives. Unlike traditional centralized control methods, this decentralized approach promotes robustness and scalability, enabling the robot team to handle more intricate scenarios. The system is parameterized by a team size (K), individual robot parameters (s_i), and a reward function (R) designed to encourage collaborative behavior. The key innovation lies in the emergent coordination achieved through the decentralized RL training process, significantly enhancing the overall performance of the robot team compared to individual robot control or simple pre-programmed strategies. This work provides a foundation for future research in adaptable and intelligent robot teams.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Non-Linear Gradient Descent
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization presents a novel approach to problem-solving, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to guide the search process. This paper proposes a new optimization algorithm, "Non-Linear Gradient Descent with Quantum Properties," designed to overcome the limitations of classical gradient descent in complex, non-linear landscapes. We introduce a modified update rule that mimics quantum properties, specifically the superposition and entanglement of gradients, to accelerate exploration and improve convergence. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing enhanced performance compared to established methods. This work establishes a foundation for a more efficient and adaptable optimization technique applicable to a wide range of computational challenges.

title: Aurora Forest Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Forest Mice
abstract: This paper presents Aurora Forest Mouse (AFM), a new metaheuristic algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of the Aurora Forest Mouse, a species known for its efficient and adaptable search strategies in a forest environment. AFM incorporates key elements of the mouse's behavior, including path exploration, resource evaluation, and adaptive movement patterns, into a novel optimization framework. The core of the algorithm lies in a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance, guided by a 'pheromone gradient' representing the desirability of different solution regions. AFM utilizes a population-based approach with a unique movement strategy, simulating the mouse's alternating between long-range exploratory movements and localized resource searches. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge towards optimal or near-optimal solutions with competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's design aims to address limitations of existing methods, particularly in handling high-dimensional search spaces and problems with complex, multimodal landscapes. The performance of AFM will be evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency.

title: Quantum Entanglement Enhanced Distributed Storage
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed storage leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that utilizing entanglement enables the construction of a distributed storage system capable of achieving long-range communication, high storage capacity, and enhanced security. The proposed mechanism involves creating entanglement between multiple quantum storage nodes, facilitating redundant information storage and inherent error correction. This approach fundamentally differs from traditional distributed storage methods relying on classical redundancy techniques. We explore the theoretical framework, outlining the key mathematical concepts and demonstrating the potential advantages of this entanglement-based system. The system's security stems from the fundamental laws of quantum mechanics, making it inherently resistant to eavesdropping and data manipulation. While no experimental validation is presented in this theoretical exploration, the presented model lays a foundation for future research and development in this promising area. The system's capacity is fundamentally limited by the number of entangled pairs, but the inherent error correction provided by entanglement significantly improves reliability. We investigate the impact of various factors on the system's performance, including entanglement fidelity and node distribution.

title: Based on Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm for Program Architecture Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program architecture design utilizing a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA). Traditional program architecture design methodologies often struggle to simultaneously optimize multiple, potentially conflicting, design goals. This research addresses this limitation by formulating the architecture design problem as a multi-objective optimization task. The MOGA effectively searches the architectural space, generating designs that balance and satisfy a predefined set of objectives. The core of the approach lies in the iterative process of evaluation, selection, and mutation, guided by the algorithm's fitness function. The results demonstrate the capability of this method to produce program architectures that meet multiple design criteria, offering a significant improvement over single-objective approaches. The key contributions of this work are the integration of MOGA with architectural design and the demonstration of its effectiveness in generating diverse and optimized architectures.

abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) is a crucial step in achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. This paper proposes a novel QEM technique leveraging reinforcement learning (RL) to dynamically adjust noise shaping parameters based on observed error rates. The core mechanism involves an RL agent that learns optimal noise shaping strategies to minimize errors while maintaining accuracy, offering a continuous adaptation to error conditions. This approach significantly improves the robustness and efficiency of QEM.

title: Where Should Experience Live? Hierarchical Hebbian Memory for Continual Vision Transformers
abstract: Vision Transformers provide strong visual representations but typically rely on slowly updated parameters, limiting their ability to organize newly acquired information across different memory timescales. This work proposes Hierarchical Hebbian Memory, a three-level memory architecture composed of rapid Working Memory, persistent Routed Episodic Memory, and slower Semantic Memory. A learned controller regulates memory contribution, read and write routing, plasticity, retention, and consolidation. A causal read-before-write lifecycle ensures that the current outcome cannot influence the prediction it supervises. The architecture is evaluated on Omniglot 5-way 1-shot recognition and CORe50 continual object recognition. With Swin-Tiny, the hierarchical model reaches 97.39\% accuracy on Omniglot and 95.37\% final accuracy on CORe50 when combined with experience replay. Learned multi-bank retrieval reaches 47.50\% delayed-association accuracy, compared with 24.17\% for a single persistent bank and 25.00\% without memory. After intervening distractors, Episodic Memory retains approximately 0.96 cosine similarity with stored associations, while Working Memory falls to approximately 0.05. These results show that Hebbian association and learned memory routing can jointly organize online visual experience across rapid, persistent, and consolidated memory timescales within Vision Transformers.

title: Geometry-Grounded Unified 3D Perception for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Camera-based autonomous driving perception requires a shared representation that preserves metric 3D structure across synchronized multi-camera streams. However, existing image-based frameworks often rely on backbones pretrained for semantic recognition, and introduce 3D geometry through downstream task-specific modules. As a result, their shared representations may fail to preserve explicit metric geometry and consistent 3D scene structure. In this paper, we present a Geometry-grounded Unified 3D Perception (GeoUP) framework that adapts the reconstruction-oriented latent of VGGT to calibrated, streaming multi-camera driving scenes. GeoUP factorizes cross-image interaction into self, temporal, and view attention to capture structurally distinct temporal and cross-view correspondences. It further injects calibration-aware raymap encodings to provide metric scale and camera geometry. The resulting geometry-grounded latent is decoded for metric depth estimation, 3D object detection, and semantic occupancy prediction, corresponding to surface-, instance-, and volume-level readouts of the same 3D scene. Through joint multi-task and multi-dataset training, GeoUP effectively leverages heterogeneous annotations and generalizes across diverse sensor configurations and perception ranges. Extensive experiments on nuScenes, Argoverse 2, Waymo, KITTI, and DDAD demonstrate that GeoUP achieves SOTA performance across detection, occupancy, and depth estimation. These results validate the effectiveness of geometry-grounded representations for unified 3D driving perception.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Constraint Optimization (NCO)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Euclidean Constraint Optimization (NCO), a novel framework for optimization problems where the solution space is inherently non-Euclidean. Traditional methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional landscapes, limiting the potential for efficient and insightful solutions. NCO leverages a variational auto-associative neural network to learn a representation of the constraints, allowing for exploration of unexpected and complex patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of applied examples, showcasing the ability to find optimal solutions in scenarios previously intractable using conventional optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers on mapping constraints onto a non-Euclidean space, enabling the discovery of solutions that traditional methods miss.

Traditional methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional landscapes, limiting the potential for efficient and insightful solutions. NCO leverages a variational auto-associative neural network to learn a representation of the constraints, allowing for exploration of unexpected and complex patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of applied examples, showcasing the ability to find optimal solutions in scenarios previously intractable using conventional optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers on mapping constraints onto a non-Euclidean space, enabling the discovery of solutions that traditional methods miss.

title: Title: Adaptive Gaussian Process Optimization
abstract: Adaptive Gaussian Process Optimization (AGPO) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to address the challenges posed by complex functions, particularly in numerical simulations. This paper details the design and implementation of AGPO, highlighting its ability to effectively optimize high-dimensional problems through the utilization of quantum state dynamics and the advanced principles of Gaussian Process regression. The core mechanism centers on leveraging the inherent adaptability of quantum states to guide the optimization process, thereby improving simulation accuracy and efficiency. The development of AGPO represents a significant advancement over existing optimization techniques, offering a robust and scalable solution for complex modeling and analysis.

title: Quantum Non-Linear Operator: A Novel Computational Framework for Complex Quantum Nonlinear Equations
abstract: Quantum Non-Linear Operators (QNOs) represent a paradigm shift in computational methods, offering the potential to tackle complex quantum nonlinear equations with unprecedented efficiency. This paper introduces a novel computational framework based on QNOs, designed to accelerate the solution of these equations and facilitate advanced quantum computation and simulation. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent complexity and non-linearity of these equations. We propose a specific QNO structure and its associated mechanisms, demonstrating its efficacy through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations. The core claim is that this framework will significantly enhance the speed and scalability of quantum calculations, opening doors to new research and applications in quantum information science.

title: Self-Adaptive Variable Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive variable model designed to enhance the generalization capabilities of machine learning models. Traditional models often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to complex datasets and unseen data. Our approach dynamically adjusts model parameters based on the observed changes in hidden variables, providing a mechanism for continuous learning and improved performance. The core claim is that the implementation of this self-adaptive model significantly improves the robustness and generalization of machine learning algorithms. This work explores a method for dynamically adjusting model parameters based on the observed changes in hidden variables, offering a potential solution to the limitations of static parameter tuning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through various experiments, showcasing improved performance on benchmark datasets.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Phase Field Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computation to revolutionize the analysis of topological phase fields. The traditional methods often struggle to capture the complex dynamics inherent in these systems, limiting our ability to fully understand their behavior. We propose a novel "Quantum Phase Field Simulation" algorithm, utilizing quantum mechanics to model the evolution of the phase field, offering a dramatically enhanced analytical capability. This approach promises to unveil deeper insights into the stability, evolution, and potential for manipulation of topological phase fields. The work details the algorithm's architecture, explores its theoretical foundations, and presents preliminary results demonstrating improved accuracy compared to existing analytical techniques.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Network Routing Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic routing protocol for quantum networks based on the fluctuating entanglement states between quantum nodes. The core of the protocol lies in real-time monitoring of entanglement strength and dynamically adjusting routing paths based on these changes. This approach aims to mitigate the risk of information loss due to entanglement decay, ultimately achieving high reliability in quantum routing. Unlike traditional protocols relying on fixed topologies, this protocol adapts to the dynamic nature of entanglement, enhancing routing efficiency and resilience. The protocol utilizes a graph-based representation of the quantum network and employs algorithms for entanglement assessment and path optimization. Mathematical models are presented to formalize the routing process, including the calculation of entanglement fidelity and path cost. The proposed system demonstrates improved routing performance and fault tolerance compared to static routing schemes. The key contribution is a dynamic, adaptive routing strategy that leverages the inherent properties of quantum networks for reliable quantum information transmission.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed reasoning engine leveraging the non-local property of quantum entanglement for enhanced information processing and logical operations. The core claim rests on utilizing entanglement to overcome the limitations of classical distributed systems, enabling long-distance, high-speed computation. The proposed mechanism involves encoding information into entangled states and performing logical operations through their interactions. Quantum control techniques are explored to optimize the manipulation and measurement of these entangled states. We demonstrate that this approach offers a fundamental shift in distributed computing, enabling true parallel computation and instantaneous information transfer, thereby transcending the physical constraints of classical systems. The engine's design focuses on modularity and scalability, aiming to provide a robust framework for complex reasoning tasks. Further research will concentrate on developing practical implementations and exploring the engine's applicability across diverse domains, including secure communication, advanced sensor networks, and artificial intelligence. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the integration of quantum mechanical principles into evolutionary algorithms, leading to a novel approach termed Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms (QIEAs). The core idea rests on leveraging concepts like superposition and tunneling to enhance the exploration and exploitation phases of traditional evolutionary algorithms. We present a framework where evolutionary operators are modified to mimic quantum behaviors, aiming to accelerate convergence and broaden the search space. The proposed methodology is distinct from existing quantum-inspired optimization techniques that primarily focus on encoding solutions into quantum states. Instead, QIEAs directly influence the evolutionary process itself, reflecting the probabilistic and non-deterministic nature of quantum mechanics. This research introduces a new paradigm for optimization problems, potentially offering significant improvements in efficiency and robustness compared to conventional evolutionary algorithms. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations and outline the key components of QIEAs, paving the way for future research and practical applications.

title: Hierarchical Quantum Simulation with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hierarchical quantum simulation framework designed to significantly enhance the scalability and efficiency of quantum simulations. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle with large systems due to computational complexity. We propose a dynamically partitioned simulation space, leveraging a sophisticated partitioning algorithm to automatically divide the simulation space into sub-regions based on the inherent complexity of the underlying system. This adaptive partitioning strategy minimizes computational burden and allows for efficient exploration of the simulation space. The framework incorporates a novel weighting mechanism to prioritize simulation effort on regions exhibiting high complexity, resulting in a substantial reduction in the overall simulation time. We detail the implementation of this framework, analyze its performance across various benchmark problems, and discuss its potential impact on the field of quantum simulation.

title: Bartel's Flying Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Flight Dynamics of a Flying Squirrel
abstract: This paper presents Bartel's Flying Squirrel (BFS), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the flight dynamics of the flying squirrel (Sciurus gyrinus). BFS leverages the squirrel's unique ability to glide and maneuver through the air, utilizing aerodynamic principles to achieve efficient and adaptable search behavior. The algorithm employs a combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a novel 'glide' mechanism that mimics the squirrel's wing adjustments and directional control. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting particle velocities based on a 'glide angle' parameter, which is influenced by the distance to the objective function minimum and the current velocity. This glide angle effectively simulates the squirrel's ability to maintain momentum and steer towards the optimal solution. BFS is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Simulated Annealing (SA). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency are attributed to its inherent ability to explore and exploit the search space, mirroring the squirrel's agile flight behavior. The results indicate that BFS offers a promising approach for tackling complex optimization challenges, particularly those with non-convex landscapes.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Optimization Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols based on quantum decoherence. The core claim is to enhance key generation rates and security through intelligent protocol parameter tuning. Leveraging machine learning algorithms, we analyze the impact of decoherence noise, aiming to improve key generation efficiency and security. The proposed approach represents a novel application of machine learning within QKD, offering a significant pathway towards improved key distribution performance. We present a framework for adaptive parameter control, demonstrating the potential for substantial gains in key rates and robustness against decoherence effects. The research focuses on theoretical optimization, without experimental validation, providing a robust mathematical framework for understanding and improving current QKD protocols. The key performance metrics considered are key generation rate (R), Bit Error Rate (BER), and security level (Φ). The work contributes to the field by outlining a systematic methodology for utilizing machine learning to tackle the inherent challenges of decoherence in QKD systems. ---

title: Quantum-Guided Evolution of Mathematical Structures
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-guided evolution to fundamentally alter the trajectory of mathematical structures, focusing on the manipulation of group theory and lattice structures. We propose a novel method, termed "Quantum Guidance," utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to subtly influence the evolution of these structures, offering a potential paradigm shift in algorithm design and mathematical modeling. The paper details the core mechanism of this approach, outlining the initial conceptual framework and mathematical foundations underpinning the Quantum Guidance algorithm. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in evolving simple lattice structures, highlighting its potential for broader application across a range of mathematical domains. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, emphasizing the challenges and opportunities presented by this nascent field.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Stochastic Gradient Descent
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization represents a promising avenue for addressing computationally challenging optimization problems. This paper investigates the application of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) to emulate the quantum annealing process, aiming to improve the speed and accuracy of complex optimization tasks. We propose a novel algorithm that iteratively refines a solution based on the gradient of the objective function, mimicking the probabilistic exploration inherent in quantum annealing. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and scalable method compared to traditional optimization techniques, leveraging the strengths of stochasticity. The core mechanism centers around utilizing SGD to dynamically adjust the solution trajectory, effectively mimicking the quantum annealing process.

title: Title: Information-Theoretic Constraints for Neural Network Training
abstract: Information-theoretic constraints offer a novel approach to neural network training, moving beyond traditional gradient descent to directly leverage the principles of entropy and mutual information. This paper introduces a new constraint formulation that explicitly incorporates these concepts, promoting stable and efficient training through a process of information-guided optimization. This method contrasts with current techniques that primarily rely on gradient descent, offering a potentially more robust and principled method for learning complex neural network models. The core mechanism involves constructing a constraint set that explicitly measures the uncertainty in the data and guides the network's weights towards regions of lower uncertainty, leading to improved generalization and reduced sensitivity to initial conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, demonstrating improved convergence speed and robustness compared to traditional methods.

title: Anomaly Detection via Adversarial Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection utilizing adversarial learning. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with subtle anomalies that closely resemble normal data, leading to high false positive rates. This work addresses this challenge by framing anomaly detection as an adversarial learning problem. Specifically, we train a discriminator network to distinguish between normal and anomalous data, while simultaneously training an anomaly generator to produce samples that are designed to fool the discriminator. This dynamic interaction forces the discriminator to learn more robust features, ultimately improving its ability to identify anomalies. The core claim of this research is that anomaly detection can be effectively leveraged through adversarial learning to train detectors capable of recognizing anomalies that closely resemble normal data. The mechanism involves modeling the detection problem as an adversarial one, training a detector to differentiate between normal and anomalous data. We argue that this approach offers a significant improvement in anomaly detection accuracy compared to conventional methods.

abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive optimization techniques to high-dimensional space, leveraging physical models to guide parameter optimization and neural network structure design. title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Reasoning Engine (QDE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Reasoning Engine (QDE), a novel architecture designed to revolutionize distributed computing by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that entanglement's non-locality can enable remote, ultra-low latency distributed reasoning, overcoming the limitations of traditional computing paradigms. QDE achieves this through a network of interconnected quantum processors, each storing a portion of the computational data. Utilizing entanglement, the system facilitates instantaneous synchronization and collective computation, enabling complex logical deductions. This approach contrasts significantly with traditional distributed reasoning, which relies on classical communication, introducing inherent delays and bandwidth constraints. The QDE architecture offers the potential for significantly faster and more efficient problem-solving, particularly for computationally intensive tasks requiring global data access and parallel processing. This paper details the theoretical framework, the proposed architecture, and outlines the potential impact of QDE on various domains, including scientific simulations, artificial intelligence, and cryptography. The primary mathematical framework presented focuses on the entanglement fidelity, quantum state transfer rates, and the logical operations performed within the entangled network.

title: ## Grey Squirrel Mimicry-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSM-MOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Grey Squirrel Mimicry-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSM-MOA), a novel optimization technique motivated by the adaptive camouflage strategies observed in grey squirrels. The algorithm leverages the squirrel's ability to dynamically adjust its coloration and behavior based on environmental context and predator presence to mimic optimal solutions. GSM-MOA utilizes a population of candidate solutions, each represented by a set of parameters. A 'mimicry' mechanism is implemented, where individuals dynamically adjust their parameters based on a 'perception' of the 'landscape' – a representation of the optimization problem – and the 'threat' level, simulating predator pressure. The algorithm incorporates both exploration and exploitation phases, with the rate of adjustment governed by a probabilistic model inspired by squirrel behavioral responses. This approach aims to achieve robust convergence and adaptability in complex optimization landscapes. The core of GSM-MOA lies in its dynamically adjusting parameters, driven by a simulated predator threat, mirroring the adaptive camouflage of grey squirrels. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods in challenging scenarios.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state generation algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional quantum state generation methods often rely on static topologies, limiting their flexibility and control. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the topology of a quantum system to generate unique and tailored quantum states. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experimental results, showcasing improved accuracy and control over quantum measurements compared to existing techniques. The core mechanism involves iterative topology adjustments guided by a feedback loop, ensuring the generation of highly specific quantum states. This advancement offers a significant step towards more precise quantum measurements and quantum information processing.
