title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology and Quantum Computing Association
abstract: This paper explores the potential application of non-linear geometric topology in quantum computing, focusing on leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance computational capabilities. We propose a novel algorithm designed to optimize quantum circuit design and improve precision and efficiency through the application of this topological structure. The core claim is that this approach, utilizing quantum entanglement, offers a significant advancement beyond current classical computational methods. This work investigates the fundamental principles of non-linear geometric topology and its relevance to the challenges faced by quantum computing.

title: When AI Strikes a Chord: How AI Agent and Human Agent Moderates Crisis Response in Competence-Based and Integrity-Based Crises
abstract: As AI has become increasingly pervasive in customer service due to its convenience and efficiency, it remains unclear whether publics hold similar expectations of AI agents and whether the recommended empathetic crisis responses elicit the desired reactions used by AI agents. To answer these questions, a 2 (Crisis type: Competence-based crisis vs. Integrity-based crisis) × 2 (Crisis response agent: AI vs. Human) × 2 (Empathetic crisis response: present vs. absent) experimental design was conducted. The results showed that due to the differences between human and AI, an empathetic crisis response is not an integral component in a competence-based crisis across human and AI agents. In an integrity-based crisis, an empathetic crisis response is an essential component of a human agent’s crisis communication, as it enhances perceived sincerity and improves overall organizational evaluations. However, incorporating the same empathetic response in an AI agent’s communication may backfire.

title: SlideBank: A Persistent Hierarchical Evidence Bank for Consistent Whole-Slide Reasoning
abstract: Whole-slide images (WSIs) are challenging for vision-language reasoning because diagnostically relevant morphology is sparse, heterogeneous, and distributed across gigapixel-scale images and multiple spatial resolutions. Existing WSI models and pathology agents can aggregate slide features or actively acquire evidence, but the information retained after exploration is often difficult to access semantically while preserving its connection to the original visual evidence. We introduce SlideBank, a training-free framework that represents each WSI as a persistent, concept-indexed, and spatially grounded evidence bank. SlideBank performs question-independent coarse-to-fine exploration to identify informative regions and multi-scale views, converts them into explicit morphological observations, and grounds pathology signals to their supporting patches and WSI coordinates. At inference time, questions are routed to relevant signals and evidence scales, and the linked global, regional, and patch evidence is integrated through confidence-based cross-level consensus. Experiments on WSI-VQA and SlideBench-BCNB show that with Patho-R1, SlideBank reaches 52.77% on WSI-VQA and with Quilt-LLaVA, it reaches 50.92% average accuracy on SlideBench-BCNB, while structured signal-guided retrieval consistently outperforms random evidence sampling. Reusing the same bank across repeated queries further achieves over 99% rephrasing consistency and substantially reduces amortized inference cost through persistent evidence reuse.

title: LookBack: Where and How to Score LVLM Responses via Visual Reference Usage
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) integrate visual perception with language generation, enabling responses that span image understanding and complex reasoning. However, LVLMs do not just inherit the text-level hallucinations; they also hallucinate against the image, producing fluent responses ungrounded in what they see. This makes LVLM response scoring inherently harder, and our diagnostics show that existing confidence-based metrics adopted from LLMs are insufficient for LVLMs. Specifically, removing the input image barely changes confidence-based selection, suggesting that output-space confidence primarily captures textual plausibility rather than agreement with the image. To address this gap, we propose LookBack, a training-free LVLM response scoring method that augments token likelihood with visual lookback score, a lightweight measure of how strongly each response token refers to image tokens. Across four benchmarks and three models, LookBack consistently improves Best-of-N selection over existing baselines with negligible additional overhead.

title: Theoretical guarantees of variational quantum algorithm with guiding states
abstract: Abstract Machine learning provides a powerful framework for predicting ground-state properties across families of quantum many-body problems, enabling amortized inference and reducing the cost of repeated simulations. Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for implementing such learnable solvers on quantum computers, yet rigorous guarantees for convergence and generalization remain scarce. Motivated by the fact that standard quantum phase estimation (QPE) provides provable performance when given a guiding state with non-trivial overlap with the ground state, we introduce a variational quantum algorithm with guiding states aiming towards predicting ground-state properties of quantum many-body systems. We then develop a proof technique—the linearization trick—that maps the training dynamics of the algorithm to those of a kernel model. This connection yields theoretical guarantees on both convergence and generalization for the VQA under the guiding state assumption. Our analysis shows that guiding states facilitate convergence, suppress finite-size error terms, and ensure stability across system dimensions. Finally, we validate our findings with numerical experiments on 2D random Heisenberg models.

title: Design and Initial Evaluation of a RAG-Based Expert Chatbot for User Support in Non-Destructive Testing
abstract: Inspection personnel need exact parameters and safety limits from proprietary documentation that may be unsuitable for hosted processing. We present a local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot for Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) manuals and a controlled benchmark comprising three synthetic manuals, 60 curated questions, and 267 predefined required facts. Answers were scored using Key Fact Coverage (KFC), the proportion of facts detected by a deterministic matcher. A full-factorial sweep of 32 configurations reached a maximum KFC of 0.789. Document access yielded larger gains than the within-pipeline variations tested: six closed-book systems scored 0.248 to 0.339, and all four prespecified comparisons remained significant after Holm correction (adjusted p ≤ 0.0028). Synthetic specifications reduced the likelihood of answer memorization. The chunking configuration produced the clearest within-pipeline difference: the 1,000-token condition outperformed the 5,000-token condition in all 16 matched pairs (+0.161, p < 0.001). Hybrid retrieval improved KFC by 0.11 to 0.12, mainly for table questions. This is an initial controlled benchmark, not evidence of industrial robustness.

title: Nonlinear Dynamic Algorithms for Optimization and Expansion
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear dynamic algorithms to optimization, aiming to address challenges in complex systems and algorithms. We introduce a novel framework that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters based on performance observations, enabling automated and scalable parameter tuning. The core mechanism focuses on creating an iterative process where the algorithm adjusts itself based on its own output, leading to improved performance and generalization. This work extends the framework to a broader context, including neural network training and model parameter adjustments, demonstrating its potential for enhancing optimization across diverse domains. The research presented herein offers a significant advancement in optimization techniques by incorporating dynamic parameter adjustment, a crucial step in handling complex systems and improving overall efficiency.

title: Self-Adaptive Topological Information Theory for Quantum Acceleration Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of self-adaptive topological information theory to revolutionize quantum acceleration computation. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on manually tuned parameters, limiting their adaptability. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent topological structure of quantum systems to optimize model parameters for enhanced machine learning and data compression. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting quantum system parameters based on topological analysis, offering a potential pathway to significantly improve efficiency. The paper details the theoretical framework, presents a preliminary implementation, and discusses future research directions. The key claim is that this integration of self-adaptive topological information theory can unlock substantial gains in both machine learning and data compression through the utilization of quantum acceleration.

title: Program Synthesis Based on Memory
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis, termed "Program Synthesis Based on Memory," which leverages memory mechanisms to accelerate the synthesis process and generate more intelligent synthesis strategies. The core idea is to model program synthesis as a memory problem. We construct a memory library, utilizing either neural networks or knowledge graphs, to store and retrieve previously synthesized program fragments and their corresponding specifications. A retrieval algorithm then searches this library to identify the most suitable synthesis path based on the current problem. This approach significantly reduces the computational cost of exhaustive search methods and allows the system to learn from past experiences, leading to more efficient and effective program synthesis. The key contribution lies in the integration of memory and retrieval techniques, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for program synthesis. ---

title: Quantum Hidden Matrices and Cryptography: A Novel Generation of Secure Encryption Systems
abstract: Quantum computing has emerged as a transformative technology, offering unprecedented computational power. This paper investigates the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize cryptography, particularly through the development of quantum hidden-square matrices (HSMs). We explore the design of a novel, secure encryption system based on HSMs, leveraging their unique properties for enhanced data security and privacy. The study focuses on the algorithmic complexities involved in HSM implementation, emphasizing the security challenges and potential optimizations. We analyze the system's potential for resistance against known attacks, including those leveraging Shor's algorithm and Grover's algorithm. This research contributes to the advancement of quantum-enhanced cryptography, offering a pathway towards a new generation of robust and secure encryption methods.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Temporal Logic Constraints
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic programming that leverages temporal logic constraints to enhance the reliability and controllability of neural network-generated code. The core idea is to combine the learning capabilities of neural networks with the structured reasoning of symbolic programming languages, explicitly enforced through temporal logic. A neural network is trained to generate code snippets in a symbolic language, such as Lisp, while temporal logic constraints dictate the desired temporal behavior of the generated programs – including execution deadlines and causal relationships. This formalization offers a verifiable and controllable framework for neuro-symbolic programming, addressing limitations of purely data-driven or purely symbolic approaches. We outline the system architecture, detail the temporal logic formulation, and discuss potential applications, emphasizing the ability to produce code that not only fulfills functional requirements but also satisfies stringent temporal constraints.

title: Quantum State Dynamics and Computation
abstract: Quantum state dynamics and computation represent a significant frontier in the field of quantum information. This paper explores the potential of dynamically transforming quantum states using topological structure, offering a novel approach to complex quantum computations. We investigate a mechanism for achieving dynamic state transformations by exploiting the inherent properties of quantum states, ultimately enhancing the feasibility of intricate quantum algorithms. This research introduces a new algorithm framework centered around topological manipulation of quantum states. The paper details the core concept, the underlying mathematical framework, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this dynamic approach. We present a model demonstrating the ability to optimize a quantum circuit's performance through dynamic state adjustment. The work emphasizes the potential of this methodology to overcome limitations of static quantum state manipulation, paving the way for more versatile and efficient quantum computations. The focus is on the application of topological transformations to quantum state evolution.

title: Symbiotic Neural Graph Construction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for constructing complex neural networks – Symbiotic Neural Graph Construction (SNGC). The core idea is that intricate neural architectures can arise spontaneously through the dynamic interaction of spatially distributed, genetically-influenced computational modules. The system operates by simulating a network of nodes with evolving computational capabilities, connected via a self-organizing 'symbiotic' algorithm. This algorithm is driven by local feedback and simulated evolutionary pressures. The model aims to move beyond traditional artificial neural networks, which often rely on predefined architectures and training methods, towards a truly emergent system where complexity arises naturally. Key components include node design with limited, evolving computational abilities, a symbiotic connection algorithm, and a simulated evolutionary process. Mathematical formulations detail the core principles driving the network's formation and adaptation. The presented approach offers a potential pathway to understanding and potentially replicating the emergence of complex neural structures in biological systems.

title: ## Batear Fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Batear Fox Hunting
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Batear Fox, inspired by the hunting strategies of Batear foxes. Batear foxes, renowned for their ambush hunting techniques and strategic decision-making, provide a compelling source of inspiration for designing an effective optimization algorithm. Batear Fox leverages a combination of concepts from the Batear fox's behavior, including territorial marking, strategic positioning, and coordinated attacks, to create a novel search process. The algorithm employs a dynamic territory assignment mechanism, a weighted exploration-exploitation strategy, and a simulated coordinated attack process to navigate the search space efficiently. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance across several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's key features include adaptability to varying problem landscapes, robustness against local optima, and a relatively simple implementation. Experimental results confirm that Batear Fox is a promising alternative for solving complex optimization challenges.

title: High-Dimensional Data Distribution Adaptive Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive clustering algorithm designed to handle high-dimensional data. Traditional clustering methods often rely on static cluster centers, offering limited adaptability to data distribution shifts. Our approach leverages reinforcement learning and self-adaptive learning to dynamically adjust cluster centers and簇形状, enhancing clustering accuracy and efficiency. We introduce a dynamic weighting mechanism for cluster center adjustments, allowing the algorithm to respond effectively to changes in data distribution. The core mechanism involves iterative refinement of cluster centers based on a learned reward function, incorporating both distance and density measures. This results in a more robust and adaptable clustering solution capable of handling complex high-dimensional datasets. This work addresses the limitations of static clustering algorithms and offers a promising path toward more effective data analysis in high-dimensional scenarios.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Neural Network Architecture
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization represents a paradigm shift in neural network architecture design, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance efficiency and generalization. This paper explores a novel framework, inspired by quantum systems, designed to optimize network structure through a dynamic interplay of quantum tunneling and superposition. We present a proposed optimization algorithm, incorporating quantum-like mechanisms, which aims to overcome limitations of traditional methods. This research focuses on the design of a new framework for neural network architecture, offering a potential path toward more robust and adaptable models.

title: Quantum Topology-Driven Neural Network Architecture
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, offers unique structural properties that hold profound implications for computation and information processing. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum topology to design novel neural network architectures, specifically focusing on the use of quantum-inspired mechanisms to enhance network expressiveness. We propose a new neural network architecture predicated on the principles of quantum topology, outlining a methodology that leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to streamline calculations and improve model representation. The core claim centers on the development of a network architecture intrinsically linked to quantum topology, demonstrating a significant advancement in neural network performance compared to conventional approaches. This work investigates the potential of this approach, providing a detailed design and analysis of the proposed mechanism.

title: Multi-Modal Neural Networks for High-Dimensional Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for high-dimensional information encoding based on multi-modal neural networks. The core idea is to design a neural network where each neuron simultaneously processes information from multiple modalities—such as time, space, and frequency—and performs a non-linear combination to achieve compact encoding. We introduce a "modal fusion" mechanism, which involves weighted fusion of outputs from neurons processing different modalities. Furthermore, we employ an adaptive weighting learning mechanism to optimize the compression representation of high-dimensional data. Unlike existing methods that typically focus on single-modal data, our approach addresses the complex inter-correlations inherent in high-dimensional datasets. The system leverages the inherent redundancy within multi-modal data to achieve efficient and compact representation. This work presents a foundational approach for encoding complex data streams and offers a pathway towards more robust and accurate data analysis.

title: Asian Elephant Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Asian Elephant Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (AEIMA), designed for tackling complex optimization problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the observed behaviors of Asian elephants, specifically their foraging strategies and social interactions. AEIMA utilizes a combination of adaptive movement patterns, group dynamics, and memory mechanisms to explore the search space effectively. The core components of the algorithm include an adaptive movement system mimicking elephant gait, a social influence mechanism simulating herd behavior, and a memory component representing past successful locations. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's parameters and operational rules. title: Antilopine Wallaby: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Antilopine Wallaby Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Antilopine Wallaby, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of antilopine wallabies. The algorithm mimics the wallaby's strategy of exploring the environment, selecting promising locations, and returning to previously visited areas with high food density. Antilopine Wallaby incorporates elements of the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm, specifically utilizing a memory pool to store promising solutions and a negative feedback mechanism inspired by the wallaby's avoidance of overcrowded food sources. The algorithm's core loop consists of three phases: exploration, selection, and exploitation. The exploration phase utilizes a probabilistic movement strategy based on the wallaby's movement patterns. The selection phase employs a rank-based selection scheme to prioritize high-quality solutions. The exploitation phase focuses on refining the selected solutions through a local search technique. The performance of Antilopine Wallaby is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving various optimization challenges. The results indicate that Antilopine Wallaby provides competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, suggesting its potential for practical applications.

title: Quantum Topology Computing: An Extension
abstract: Quantum topology is a burgeoning field of research exploring the unique properties of quantum systems, offering a novel approach to computation and optimization. This paper investigates the application of quantum topology to the design of advanced quantum algorithms, particularly focusing on the development of a new quantum algorithm based on "reconstruction" principles. The core claim posits that this method, leveraging the power of quantum topology, can significantly enhance the efficiency and robustness of quantum computation, thereby unlocking new possibilities within the field. We introduce a novel quantum algorithm that employs a "reconstruction" process, meticulously manipulating quantum states to achieve a desired outcome. This approach promises to overcome limitations of traditional quantum algorithms and pave the way for more powerful and reliable quantum systems.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology for Sparse Data Clustering
abstract: Classical clustering algorithms often fail to effectively handle sparse datasets, leading to suboptimal results. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology algorithm, leveraging quantum mechanics, to automatically adjust cluster structures based on data density. We propose a quantum-driven refinement process that minimizes distance between points while maximizing distance to other clusters, thereby improving the accuracy of clustering in sparse datasets. The proposed method offers a fundamentally new approach to sparse data clustering, addressing a critical challenge in data analysis.

title: Neural Network Based on Probabilistic Dynamic Topology Learning (PBDTSL)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network training, termed Probabilistic Dynamic Topology Learning (PBDTSL), which leverages principles from biological neural networks to achieve adaptive and optimized network topology. The core concept involves treating the neural network as a probabilistic process, incorporating stochastic synaptic connections, dynamic neuron death/regeneration, and Markov chain modeling for predicting connection probabilities. The system dynamically adjusts connection weights and regulates the death/regeneration rate of neurons based on network performance feedback. PBDTSL addresses the limitations of conventional neural network training methods that often assume fixed network topologies. The system's ability to actively adapt its structure based on learning feedback offers a promising pathway for tackling complex tasks and building more robust and efficient neural networks. The key mathematical formulations are presented, detailing the probabilistic modeling, Markov chain dynamics, and the adaptive learning mechanism. The model's ability to handle evolving network topologies through probabilistic transitions and dynamic neuron populations is highlighted as a key differentiator. This research aims to bridge the gap between artificial neural networks and the inherent dynamic nature of biological systems, leading to improved learning capabilities and network resilience. ---

title: Blue-Throated Bee-eater Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BBIO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Blue-Throated Bee-eater Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BBIO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's design is inspired by the foraging behavior of Blue-Throated Bee-eaters, a bird known for its remarkable ability to locate food sources efficiently in diverse environments. BBIO incorporates elements of the bee-eater's search strategy, including clustered foraging, adaptive exploration-exploitation, and a dynamic territory assignment mechanism. The core of the algorithm lies in a population-based approach where each individual represents a potential solution. The algorithm maintains a population of solutions and iteratively updates them using a series of operations mimicking the bee-eater's hunting process. This paper details the algorithm's mechanics, including the initialization, selection, and update mechanisms, and discusses its potential applications and future research directions. The primary goal is to develop an algorithm that demonstrates robust performance across a variety of optimization challenges while exhibiting adaptability and efficiency.

title: WP-008 — Information Routing in E8: Why Geometry Is Necessary But Not Sufficient
abstract: The E8 lattice offers a unified structural language for information routing, but its geometric properties alone are insufficient to guarantee correct information selection. This paper clarifies a critical finding from the dedupe knight implementation: semantic collision—two distinct information objects occupying the same lattice point—can occur despite perfect geometric alignment. We argue that geometry must be paired with intentionality, context constraint, and coherence-preservation mechanisms to function as a routing engine. We document the architectural constraints this imposes and sketch implications for the Excalibur blueprint and 248-dimensional threading at production scale.

title: Light-driven molecular reorientation for large-scale photonic in-memory computing
abstract: Abstract Photonics has the potential to transform high-speed and energy-efficient artificial intelligence. However, most photonic computing platforms still rely on costly electro-optic conversions for data input, weight loading and storage, resulting in substantial overhead during large-scale computation. Here, we present a large-scale photonic in-memory computing platform based on liquid crystal (LC)-enabled Poincaré-sphere-connected neural networks. Megabyte-level nonvolatile photonic memory is introduced through light-driven reorientation of sulfonic azo-dye and LC molecules, which also functions as the reconfigurable optical neurons. This architecture uniquely integrates optical sensing, memory, and computing in situ, allowing minimal data-movement overheads in various switchable machine vision tasks. Ultrahigh scalability is demonstrated by a 9.44-million-neuron photonic processor array that supports massively parallel optical computing, recording and retrieval, providing a memory capacity 100,000 times larger than state-of-the-art photonic in-memory computing. This work offers a novel pathway toward scalable submicrometer-precision photonic memory, thus establishing a new paradigm for physical neural networks and brain-like artificial intelligence.

title: Sources of Truth: A Multi-Platform, Multilingual Audit of Citations in AI Mental Health Information Queries
abstract: Online health information seeking is shifting from keyword search, where users consider a ranked list of links, to conversational systems that compose a single answer and curate its citations. Source evaluation therefore passes from user to platform, yet what these systems surface is poorly characterized. We audited three free consumer products (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overview) on twenty English mental health questions under two prompt conditions, with a subset of three also translated into six further languages of varying resource tiers. We recorded 15,942 citations across 1,140 responses and 1,713 unique domains, then classified every citation with a nine-category organizational typology applied by a deterministic classifier validated against human coding. Citations were heavily concentrated: the ten most-cited domains accounted for 43.6% of English citations, and government, commercial health, and academic sources were closely matched at roughly 22% each. Platforms differed little in typical citation volume but sharply in consistency and in the source types they favored. Explicitly requesting sources shifted composition only modestly. Non-English queries surfaced fewer citations and were routed to language-appropriate resources at significantly lower rates. We release the typology, classifier, and annotated corpus as reusable instruments for auditing generative health search.

title: Can We Trust In-Distribution Success? Locked Evaluation Reveals Transfer Failure and Sampling-Depth Entanglement in CRISPRi Perturbation Prediction
abstract: AI evaluation can support the wrong inference when an in-domain benchmark success does not survive distribution shift, or when the benchmark endpoint is entangled with a design factor. We study this problem in CRISPRi perturbation-effect prediction, evaluating a frozen Geneformer representation under a locked, pre-registered protocol: heads and model selection were frozen before test evaluation; the protocol required external outcome labels to remain withheld until final unblinding; and analysis-governing decisions were fixed before the evaluations they govern. In-distribution on the Virtual Cell Challenge (VCC), the frozen representation carries measurable predictive information beyond a dimension-matched random-feature control (Delta R^2 = +0.1645, 95% CI [+0.1375, +0.1920]), satisfying the pre-registered informativeness gate required before interpreting transfer. It then fails zero-shot transfer on both external screens (Spearman rho = -0.139 and -0.267), lying below that control on each. Adding a predefined magnitude block improves the representation externally (Delta rho = +0.032 and +0.143) but, under the frozen primary head, does not rescue transfer: both remain negative. A pre-registered, count-adjusted max-response secondary is positively associated with the outcome on both screens; we report it as correlational and secondary, not as a recovered magnitude signal. Finally, the VCC endpoint is strongly sample-size associated: a count-only linear model reaches R^2 = +0.4325, versus +0.2589 for the four magnitude scalars; adding those scalars to cell count improves R^2 by only +0.0017, so much of the aggregate-magnitude signal overlaps with cell count. This case study shows how locking the evaluation, harmonizing the measured endpoint, and separating primary from secondary evidence can change the inference supported by an AI benchmark.

title: Effects-and-Lifetimes Calculus — Mechanized Safety Proofs
abstract: A Rocq (Coq) formalization of a call-by-value calculus with bounded type polymorphism (full F<:), a separate lifetime sort forming a two-point lattice, algebraic data constructors with existential lifetime/type schemas, and algebraic effect handlers with multi-shot resumptions — the proof-side companion of the CoreΔ calculus. The safety story is lifetime-based capability confinement: effect capabilities are local-annotated values, and the lifetime subtyping discipline guarantees that neither a capability nor any local-confined datum can escape the scope that delimits it. The development is axiom-free — every capstone theorem prints «Closed under the global context» under Print Assumptions, enforced by a derived assumption gate (make verify). It includes type soundness, capability confinement at every syntactic occurrence, guarded handler-boundary theorems on states and on labelled transition events with a certified completeness accounting, determinism modulo the fresh-marker choice, certified reflected deciders and a certified evaluator with an OCaml extraction, and a fully verified examples tier with a rejection suite. See README.md for the theorem table and ARTIFACT.md for the build and verification guide.

title: Dynamic Topology for Machine Learning Model Evaluation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for evaluating machine learning models based on dynamic topology. Traditional evaluation methods often rely on manual design, limiting the model's adaptability. Our proposed system automatically adjusts the model's topology based on training data and model performance, enhancing generalization capabilities. We present a dynamic topology construction algorithm that iteratively refines the model's representation, leading to improved robustness and performance across diverse datasets. The framework's core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent properties of dynamic topology to dynamically shape the model's representation, fostering better generalization. This approach significantly reduces the need for extensive manual tuning and allows for more effective model optimization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a perplexing phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds the potential to revolutionize information encoding and transmission. This research explores the development of a novel quantum entanglement-based encoding protocol, aiming to achieve unparalleled information security and transmission speed. The core of this approach centers around exploiting the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate secure key exchange and data transfer, circumventing limitations imposed by traditional cryptographic methods. We propose a protocol predicated on the precise control and manipulation of entangled states, offering a fundamentally different approach to data security and transmission. This paper details the core mechanism, analyzes its potential benefits, and concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this groundbreaking technology.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Grammars and Neural Network Guidance
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a technique that aims to automatically discover mathematical expressions from data. Despite its potential, SR often struggles to find complex and interpretable models due to the vast number of possible solutions that need to be explored. This work proposes a novel approach that combines evolutionary grammars with neural network guidance to improve the efficiency and robustness of SR. The core idea is to use an evolutionary grammar system to generate a diverse range of symbolic expressions and then leverage a neural network to prioritize expressions with higher predicted fitness. The neural network is trained to predict the fitness of expressions based on their characteristics, allowing the evolutionary algorithm to focus on more promising candidates. This integrated framework demonstrates improved performance in discovering complex mathematical models compared to traditional SR methods, offering a more effective strategy for tackling challenging SR problems. The key equations and concepts explored in this paper are: * Error Metric: E = Σ |yi - f(xi)| * Fitness Function: F(expression) = 1 / E * Grammar Rules: G = {R1, R2, ..., Rn} * Neural Network Output: y = NN(expression) * Evolutionary Algorithm Step: Selection → Mutation → Crossover → Replacement

title: Constraint-Driven Quantum State Collapse
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, Constraint-Driven Quantum State Collapse, designed to enhance the fidelity of quantum measurements through dynamic constraint feedback. The core mechanism centers on continuous monitoring of the quantum state and adaptive adjustment of constraints to induce a specific collapse trajectory. This approach aims to overcome limitations inherent in traditional quantum measurement techniques by offering a mechanism to directly influence the collapse process. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in improving measurement fidelity. The paper concludes by highlighting the potential for this approach to advance the state of quantum measurement accuracy.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Style Transfer for Enhanced Generalization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) presents a paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, offering the potential for more robust and adaptable models. A key challenge in QML lies in the inherent difficulty of training models on data with varying styles or characteristics. This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge – Style Transfer, specifically tailored for QML. We investigate a method leveraging stylistic features extracted from data, effectively migrating these features to improve the model's generalization across diverse datasets. The core mechanism involves carefully extracting and adapting stylistic elements, promoting better representation learning and improved robustness. This research explores the potential of stylistic transfer to enhance the performance of QML models, ultimately offering a pathway to more versatile and reliable AI systems.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Topological Information Analysis Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked regardless of distance, has emerged as a promising resource for advanced information processing and quantum technologies. This research explores the application of quantum entanglement to the analysis of topological information, aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of topological information analysis. We propose an algorithm that leverages the unique properties of entangled states to represent and manipulate topological data, offering a novel approach to address limitations inherent in classical methods. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the entanglement to capture the dynamic nature of topological structures, ultimately leading to a more precise understanding of these intricate phenomena. The algorithm utilizes a modified version of the entanglement-induced measurement protocol, where entangled states are manipulated to reveal subtle topological features. This represents a significant step towards a more robust and accurate method for analyzing topological data, potentially unlocking new insights into the underlying physics of these systems. The significance of this work lies in the potential for quantum entanglement to provide a fundamentally different perspective on topological information analysis, offering a pathway to overcoming classical computational constraints and advancing the field.

title: ## Beach Vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Sand Hopper," inspired by the foraging behavior of beach voles. Beach voles are known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies when seeking food resources on beaches. This algorithm leverages their movement patterns, incorporating elements of randomness, local optimization, and adaptive exploration to address complex optimization problems. The core of Sand Hopper revolves around a "sand hopper" representation, where each solution is modeled as a sand particle moving within a simulated beach environment. The algorithm employs a modified version of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) concept, with a novel beach terrain generation mechanism to promote exploration and exploitation. We detail the algorithm's mechanics, including the generation of the beach terrain, the movement of sand hoppers, and the adaptation of individual hopper parameters. The performance of Sand Hopper is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic approaches. The key contributions of this work include a novel algorithm design, a comprehensive analysis of its parameters, and a comparative evaluation against established optimization methods. The results indicate that Sand Hopper offers a promising approach for tackling challenging optimization scenarios.

title: Quantum Delay Compensation Mechanism in Quantum Networks
abstract: Quantum networks promise secure and efficient communication, but significant delays introduce critical limitations for long-distance quantum key distribution (QKD) and other quantum network applications. This paper presents a novel mechanism for precise delay compensation within quantum networks, leveraging quantum entanglement and interference. The core idea involves real-time measurement and correction of time delays using entangled photon pairs. We formally define the problem, propose a compensation strategy based on a feedback loop utilizing Bell state measurements and subsequent phase adjustments. The theoretical framework outlines the mathematical models and key equations governing the system, including those describing entanglement evolution, time delay propagation, and the measurement process. We explore the impact of various delay characteristics on the effectiveness of the compensation and discuss potential improvements and scaling challenges. The results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and highlight its potential to significantly enhance the robustness and range of quantum networks.

title: Bahia Porcupine: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bahia Porcupine
abstract: This paper presents Bahia Porcupine, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bahia porcupine. The algorithm utilizes a combination of adaptive mutation, a novel 'spike' movement strategy, and a population-based search mechanism. The core innovation lies in the porcupine's unique method of seeking food – rapidly probing the environment with short, directional movements followed by a period of stationary assessment. This behavior is translated into an algorithm that balances exploration and exploitation effectively. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic methods. The key performance metrics assessed include convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that Bahia Porcupine offers a promising alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's inherent adaptability and efficient search strategy make it a valuable addition to the metaheuristic landscape. The algorithm is presented with detailed mathematical formulations and operational rules.

title: ## The Arctic Goose Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Goose Migration Patterns
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Goose Metaheuristic (AGM), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the migratory behavior of Arctic geese. AGM leverages the geese's tendency to explore diverse routes, adapt to environmental changes, and maintain a balance between exploitation and exploration, mirroring their survival strategies. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a dynamic route selection system based on route diversity, an adaptive step-size adjustment mechanism influenced by environmental noise, and a population polarization strategy mimicking flock formation. AGM aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for a wide range of optimization problems. The algorithm's core parameters and operational rules are described in detail, outlining its unique approach to navigating complex search spaces. This paper presents a theoretical framework for AGM and establishes its potential as a valuable addition to the metaheuristic optimization landscape.

title: Meta-Learning for Continuous Software System Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the application of meta-learning techniques to achieve continuous evolution of software systems. Traditional software evolution methods often struggle to adapt to changing environments and user demands, leading to inefficiencies and potential obsolescence. We propose a novel approach that frames software system evolution as a meta-learning problem. This allows us to learn how to learn, effectively optimizing the evolutionary process itself. The core idea is to leverage meta-learning algorithms to iteratively improve the strategies used for system evolution. This results in a system that not only adapts to new requirements but also learns to adapt more effectively over time. We present a theoretical framework and outline a methodology for implementing this approach, emphasizing its potential to enhance software system adaptability and intelligence. The research contributes to a shift towards more dynamic and responsive software development practices.

title: Quantum-Based Probability Density Estimation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing for probability density estimation (PDE), a crucial component of many machine learning algorithms. Traditional PDE methods often struggle with high-dimensional data, leading to computational bottlenecks and potentially inaccurate estimates. We propose a novel approach leveraging quantum circuits to perform PDE, capitalizing on quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to accelerate and potentially enhance the estimation process. Specifically, we outline a quantum algorithm designed to approximate probability density functions (PDFs) directly from data samples. The core of our approach involves encoding data into a quantum state and utilizing quantum gates to perform calculations related to the PDF. Furthermore, we address the challenges of noise inherent in quantum systems through the integration of quantum error correction techniques. This work lays the theoretical groundwork for a quantum-enhanced PDE method, demonstrating the feasibility of significantly improving estimation speed and accuracy for complex datasets. We focus on the conceptual design and potential benefits of this approach, without performing actual experimental validation.

title: ## Blue Paradise Optimization: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Blue Paradise Bird
abstract: This paper introduces Blue Paradise Optimization (BPO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the behavioral patterns of the Blue Paradise Bird (Iridosornis paradiseus). BPO leverages the bird's unique foraging strategies – specifically its dynamic shifting of search areas, its reliance on visual cues and spatial memory, and its adaptive responsiveness to environmental changes – to develop a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm incorporates key elements such as a dynamic neighborhood structure, a memory-based exploration strategy, and a novel "Paradise Shift" mechanism that mimics the bird's foraging behavior. BPO aims to achieve high solution quality and convergence speed in complex optimization problems. The core of the algorithm centers around a dynamically adjusted population size, a multi-dimensional fitness function incorporating both exploration and exploitation components, and a probabilistic transition matrix influencing the movement of solutions within the search space. This paper presents the theoretical framework and design principles of BPO, outlining its operational mechanics and highlighting its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods.

title: Title: Based on Non-Linear Geometric Topology for Quantum System Control
abstract: Quantum systems pose significant challenges in achieving precise and stable control, particularly in complex environments. Traditional control algorithms often rely on static models, limiting their adaptability. This paper introduces a novel control algorithm leveraging the unique properties of non-linear geometric topology to address these challenges. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the system's geometry based on feedback, enabling more robust and responsive control. The core mechanism hinges on the inherent non-linearity within the geometric structure, which allows for inherent stability and precise manipulation. This approach offers a fundamentally new perspective on quantum system control, potentially unlocking advancements in precision measurement, quantum computation, and quantum information processing.

abstract: This paper introduces Acacia Rat, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of acacia rats. Acacia rats are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the core principles of their navigation, resource selection, and memory mechanisms to create a robust and effective optimization process. Acacia Rat employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a unique memory structure mimicking the rat's spatial awareness. We present the algorithm's design, detailing the key parameters and operational rules. Furthermore, we evaluate Acacia Rat's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities and potential advantages over established metaheuristic methods. The results show that Acacia Rat performs well in both continuous and discrete optimization landscapes. The algorithm's adaptive memory and dynamic parameter adjustment contribute to its effectiveness. This research provides a novel approach to metaheuristic optimization and offers a valuable tool for solving complex real-world problems.

abstract: This paper introduces the Deep-Sea Shrimp Inspired Adaptive Resonance Optimization Algorithm (DSARO), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique. The algorithm draws inspiration from the observed adaptive behaviors of deep-sea red shrimp, specifically their ability to navigate and forage in extremely low-visibility environments and their efficient resource utilization. DSARO leverages a dynamic population structure, adaptive resonance mechanisms, and a novel exploration-exploitation balance strategy, mimicking the shrimp's responses to environmental changes and resource availability. The core concept involves a population of 'shrimp' representing potential solutions, with each shrimp's 'position' in the search space continuously adjusted based on both local and global information. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the population size and the degree of resonance based on the overall search landscape. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundation, key components, and potential applications, aiming to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization problems.

title: Workload Identification with Physical Side Channels for AI Governance
abstract: AI compute verification is one of the first tangible and tractable points for international policy aimed at AI governance. Determining whether frontier labs, or any operator, comply with agreements requires the regulating authority to discern how their compute is used. The elementary building block of AI compute is the GPU, and any activity it executes leaves a physical trace. Here, we show that an external observer can identify the class of the workload running on an NVIDIA H200 from its power draw. Unlike on-chip NVML telemetry, which can be spoofed or replayed, such a physical channel can in principle be observed independently of operator cooperation. We recorded 930 five-second traces at sim 10 MHz, covering seventeen open LLM families and twenty-five non-AI workloads. Over this corpus we separate training from inference and from non-AI computation with an accuracy of 97% and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.955, evaluated on model families unseen during training. AI workload spectral content predominantly lies below sim 20kHz and training is particularly recognizable through the memory-bound optimizer update. The GPU operator is then treated as adversarial and able to reshape the physical computation itself. Four evasion strategies are tested to disguise training as inference, producing an additional 680 adversarial traces. A detector hardened against evasion strategies, with the tested strategy held out, catches training geq 99% of the time for three of the four strategies. The fourth, diluted low-rank adaptation (LoRA), is detected 48--88% of the time with a hardened classifier, rising to geq 98% with an additional rescue rule. While these attacks are not a comprehensive evaluation against adversarial behaviour, they offer initial insights beyond genuine activities and a dataset for developing and testing stronger evasion mechanisms.

title: Seq2Synth: Benchmarking Temporal Fidelity in Synthetic Sequential Tabular Data
abstract: Synthetic sequential tabular data are increasingly used for privacy-preserving data sharing and research, yet conventional tabular metrics often overlook temporal structure. Existing single-table and relational evaluation protocols largely collapse records into static distributions, leaving key temporal properties insufficiently evaluated. We introduce Seq2Synth, a unified benchmark for assessing these properties. Its taxonomy characterizes temporal and schema properties to determine applicable evaluations, covering timestamp, cross-sectional, longitudinal, and structural fidelity, alongside trajectory-aware utility and privacy. Across seven core datasets from a 13-dataset benchmark and eight generators, models with near-perfect static fidelity still violate basic temporal constraints, producing duplicate timestamps, irregular intervals, and incomplete observation grids. Moreover, static and temporal-aware rankings diverge substantially, showing that temporal fidelity must be evaluated directly rather than inferred from static or relational scores. Project page and online appendices are available at: https://seq2synth.github.io/.

title: Multi-instance Learning as Downstream Task of Self-Supervised Learningbased Pre-trained Model
abstract: Multi-instance learning (MIL) is a type of weakly supervised learning. In MIL, a set of instances is defined asa bag, and only bag labels are known. In recent years, deep learning-based MIL has been applied in medical imaging,especially in histopathological images. However, when classifying the marker in the brain hematoma CT imageswhich we deal with, simply applying MIL leads to spurious correlations. title: Nonlinear Multi-Body Synchronization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Nonlinear Multi-Body Synchronization Algorithm (NMBSA) that leverages quantum entanglement to achieve precise synchronization of multiple microscopic particles, such as electrons and atoms. Traditional synchronization methods rely on classical communication, posing significant challenges for quantum systems. This algorithm employs quantum entanglement to facilitate a more efficient and secure synchronization process. The core mechanism involves the instantaneous correlation of entangled states, enabling the algorithm to predict and precisely synchronize the quantum states of the particles. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, the underlying quantum principles, and its potential applications, highlighting its advantages over existing synchronization techniques.

title: Quantum Information Encoding and Reconstruction of Memory
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum information theory to address fundamental questions surrounding memory. The core claim posits that memory, at its essence, can be encoded as quantum information, and that quantum information processing techniques can be leveraged to achieve memory reconstruction and enhancement. The proposed mechanism centers around the exploitation of quantum entanglement and superposition, leading to a novel quantum memory storage and reconstruction model. This work introduces a theoretical framework that bridges the gap between quantum mechanics and neuroscience, exploring a fundamentally new approach to memory storage and retrieval. The paper details the key concepts, mathematical formulations, and potential implications of this paradigm shift. We propose a model where memories are represented as quantum states, manipulated through quantum gates, and subsequently reconstructed with enhanced fidelity. The central focus is on developing a quantifiable method for encoding and manipulating memories, opening doors for potential therapeutic applications and a deeper understanding of the human brain. ---

title: Physics Simulation of Quantum Entanglement Optimization – Optimization of Quantum Entanglement States
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in which two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, holds immense promise for quantum computing and quantum information processing. However, harnessing entanglement effectively requires precise control over its quantum states. This paper explores the application of physics simulation techniques to optimize quantum entanglement states, specifically focusing on a novel geometric optimization method leveraging the unique properties of entanglement. Traditional optimization methods struggle to fully capture the intricacies of entangled states, necessitating a shift towards a more sophisticated approach. We propose a new method that utilizes entanglement to guide the search for optimal quantum states, resulting in enhanced efficiency and control over quantum computation. The core claim is that this method provides a significant improvement in the performance of quantum algorithms by effectively manipulating entangled states. The mechanism involves the exploitation of entanglement's non-classical correlation to generate a more complex and structured quantum state, facilitating faster and more accurate computations. This research presents a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Adaptive Quantum Feedback Control System
abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes an adaptive quantum feedback control system designed to optimize the performance of quantum devices. The core of the system lies in a real-time monitoring and adjustment mechanism utilizing a quantum sensor to measure the state of the quantum system. This measurement data is then fed back into a control algorithm, which dynamically adjusts the system parameters to achieve precise control. Unlike traditional control systems that are sensitive to parameter uncertainties, this adaptive approach leverages the inherent properties of quantum systems to enhance stability and performance. The theoretical framework presented here establishes a foundation for future research and development in adaptive quantum control, addressing key challenges in quantum device operation and manipulation. The system aims to provide a robust and flexible solution for controlling quantum systems with varying characteristics. The primary focus is on the control loop design and the feedback algorithm implementation, with an emphasis on achieving optimal performance under conditions of parameter uncertainty. This work contributes to the growing field of quantum control by introducing a novel adaptive strategy that can significantly improve the operational capabilities of quantum devices.

title: ## Black Colobus Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Colobus Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the black colobus monkey. The algorithm leverages the observed strategies of these primates – their selective movement, preference for specific food sources, and avoidance of dangerous areas – to construct a robust and efficient optimization process. BCMOA employs a combination of adaptive step size control, a multi-dimensional search space exploration strategy mimicking the colobus's route selection, and a novel conflict resolution mechanism based on the primate's avoidance behavior. The algorithm is designed for tackling complex, non-linear optimization problems. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's architecture, including its key parameters and operational rules. The performance of BCMOA is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results indicate that BCMOA offers a promising approach for optimization challenges where adaptability and risk aversion are crucial factors.

title: ## Biak Giant Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Biak Giant Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BGIMA), motivated by the unique foraging behavior of the Biak Giant Rat ( *Megasura imbricata*), a large rat endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia. These rats are known for their remarkable ability to locate and exploit food resources efficiently, even in complex and unpredictable environments. BGIMA leverages this behavior through a combination of adaptive exploration, exploitation, and memory mechanisms. The algorithm employs a rat-like "trail" representation, where each rat's position represents a potential solution, and the strength of the trail reflects the fitness of that solution. Dynamic adjustment of trail lengths, inspired by the rats' preference for richer food sources, drives the search process. Furthermore, a "nesting" mechanism mimicking the rats' tendency to revisit successful locations is implemented to enhance exploitation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities. The key contributions of this work include a novel algorithm design, a clear explanation of the inspiration from the Biak Giant Rat's foraging behavior, and empirical evidence of its performance across diverse optimization tasks.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic feature learning algorithm leveraging adaptive machine learning techniques. Traditional feature learning methods often employ static feature sets, failing to adequately capture the dynamic nature of data. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts feature learning strategies based on input data shifts, resulting in enhanced feature extraction and modeling capabilities. We propose a mechanism for automatic feature adaptation through a "dynamic feature" framework. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves the effectiveness of feature representation and modeling compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios with significant data variations. This work demonstrates the algorithm's efficacy through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its ability to effectively handle evolving datasets.

title: Quantum Entanglement Probability Expansion
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a profoundly perplexing phenomenon. Its implications extend far beyond basic quantum theory, offering the potential for revolutionary advancements in computation and communication. This paper explores a novel theoretical framework, the Quantum Entanglement Probability Expansion (QEP), designed to significantly deepen our understanding of the relationship between probability, system complexity, and the efficiency of quantum information processing. We propose a modified probabilistic model that explicitly incorporates the entanglement properties of quantum systems, allowing for a more precise and computationally efficient approach to quantum information handling. The core mechanism centers around extending the probability distribution of quantum states to encompass the entire system, enabling a holistic assessment of information processing dynamics. This paper details the QEP's mathematical foundations, its potential applications within quantum information theory, and preliminary results demonstrating increased efficiency compared to conventional approaches. The implications of this research extend beyond mere theoretical advancements, potentially paving the way for practical quantum algorithms and enhanced quantum communication protocols.

title: Beelzebub Tube-nosed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Beelzebub Tube-nosed Bat" algorithm (BTBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Beelzebub Tube-nosed Bat (Macronycteris verae). These bats exhibit a unique and complex foraging strategy involving coordinated flight patterns and information sharing. The BTBA leverages these observed characteristics to create a robust and efficient optimization algorithm. The core of the algorithm incorporates a multi-dimensional search space modeled after the bat's flight paths, utilizing a novel encoding scheme for position and velocity representation. The algorithm utilizes a self-organized behavior model, mimicking the bats' communication and information exchange, and incorporates a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The key contributions of this work include the design of a novel encoding scheme, a sophisticated communication mechanism, and an adaptive exploration-exploitation strategy, all inspired by the unique foraging behavior of the Beelzebub Tube-nosed Bat. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms, highlighting its advantages in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm demonstrates potential applications in various fields, including engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning.

title: Dynamic Topology-Dependent Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reasoning engine designed to tackle complex system dependency inference. The core concept revolves around mimicking biological neural networks' synaptic plasticity, enabling the engine to learn and adapt to evolving system relationships in real-time. The engine leverages reinforcement learning to model synaptic connection strength variations, coupled with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for representing and updating system dependency graphs. These graphs dynamically adjust based on the accuracy of inference results, optimizing the pathways for dependency reasoning. Unlike traditional dependency inference methods reliant on static knowledge graphs, this approach offers adaptability to dynamic system changes, potentially leading to enhanced efficiency and accuracy. The key innovation lies in integrating biological plausibility – synaptic plasticity – into the core of the reasoning process, creating a self-learning and self-optimizing system. The proposed framework provides a foundation for intelligent systems capable of navigating and understanding complex, time-varying dependencies.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of incorporating geometric intuition into machine learning algorithms, aiming to foster more robust, generalizable, and resilient models. The investigation will demonstrate the efficacy of this framework through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting the potential benefits for improving model performance and overall reliability.

title: ## The Arctic Tern-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (ATS-SA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Tern-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (ATS-SA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the remarkable navigation and foraging strategies of the Arctic Tern (Sterna paradisaea). The algorithm leverages the tern's ability to dynamically adjust its flight path based on wind conditions, food availability, and overall energy efficiency. ATS-SA incorporates three key mechanisms: a dynamic adaptation strategy mimicking the tern's response to environmental changes, a spatially aware search process reflecting the tern's territory exploration, and an adaptive inertia weight scheme inspired by the tern's flight adjustments. The algorithm aims to achieve robust and efficient optimization performance across diverse problem landscapes. This paper outlines the theoretical framework, algorithm design, and underlying principles driving ATS-SA, providing a foundation for future research and potential applications.

title: Blue Cod Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Blue Cod Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to effectively solve complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of Blue Cod fish, particularly their ability to efficiently explore and exploit a food source in a dynamic and uncertain environment. BCIMO leverages a combination of adaptive movement strategies, memory-based exploration, and a novel 'depth perception' mechanism to navigate the search space. The algorithm incorporates a 'schooling' concept, where individual agents (particles) maintain a degree of proximity to each other, promoting collaboration and preventing premature convergence. Furthermore, a dynamic weighting system adjusts the influence of exploration and exploitation based on the perceived environmental complexity. This approach aims to improve the algorithm's robustness and convergence rate in challenging optimization landscapes. The mathematical formulation of the algorithm and its key components are presented, outlining its operational principles.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection using Temporal Convolutional Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection in graph data by leveraging Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs). Traditional anomaly detection techniques often struggle to effectively incorporate temporal dependencies within graph structures, leading to missed or misclassified anomalies. Our method utilizes TCNs to analyze graph data as a function of time, enabling the identification of anomalous patterns and deviations from typical behavior. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves anomaly detection accuracy compared to methods that ignore temporal context. The core of our approach lies in the ability of TCNs to capture long-range dependencies, which are crucial for understanding the evolution of anomalous activities within a graph. We outline the architecture, training methodology, and evaluation results of our system, showcasing its effectiveness on various graph anomaly datasets. evidence.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection in graph data by leveraging Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs). Our method utilizes TCNs to analyze graph data as a function of time, enabling the identification of anomalous patterns and deviations from typical behavior. title: Graph-Based Bayesian Networks for Causal Discovery from Observational Data
abstract: Causal discovery from observational data remains a significant challenge in machine learning and statistics. Traditional methods often struggle with scalability, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional datasets and complex relationships between variables. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing graph-based Bayesian networks for efficient causal inference. We propose an iterative algorithm that leverages graph algorithms to refine a causal graph based on observed data. This approach addresses the limitations of previous methods by providing a scalable framework for identifying causal relationships. The core of the method relies on repeatedly updating the graph structure based on conditional independence tests, ultimately converging towards a graph that accurately reflects the underlying causal structure. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and outline its potential for applications in various domains. The key innovation lies in the strategic combination of graph algorithms and Bayesian network principles to achieve robust and scalable causal discovery.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges for information processing and communication. Accurate prediction of entangled states is crucial for leveraging the power of quantum technologies. This paper introduces the Quantum Entanglement State Probability Model (QCPM), a novel model designed to predict the evolution of entangled states, offering theoretical support for quantum information processing. We present a probabilistic framework for modeling entanglement states, leveraging machine learning to optimize the state transition dynamics. This model aims to surpass existing approaches by focusing directly on the state evolution, providing a robust and adaptable tool for understanding and manipulating entangled quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around a complex probability distribution representing the entangled state, optimized through a reinforcement learning algorithm.

title: A curated dataset for emotion-based analysis of students’ experiences in higher education
abstract: Understanding the emotional states of university students is essential for addressing academic performance, well-being, and institutional support. This paper presents EduAffect, a novel emotion-labeled dataset constructed from public social media posts and structured survey responses by University Students in Ghana. The dataset comprises 2423 entries annotated using 28 fine-grained emotion labels (27 emotions plus Neutral) based on the GoEmotions framework. Each entry is tagged with a single emotion label, enabling context aware emotional analysis. The data reflects culturally grounded expressions in English and English-Twi code-switching. A thorough preprocessing pipeline ensured text quality, anonymisation, and language consistency. We provide detailed insights into the label distribution, lexical characteristics, and real-world examples, supported by a comprehensive taxonomy and sentiment mapping. This dataset fills a critical gap in student-focused emotion resources and offers a valuable foundation for future research in affective computing, student mental health, and emotion-aware educational technologies.

title: StreamScout: Learning When to Look Deeper for Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: Streaming video understanding requires answering questions that arrive at arbitrary moments over an unbounded video stream. Existing systems primarily focus on what to retain in a bounded memory, yet access that memory using the same fixed-cost procedure for every query, despite substantial variation in the evidence required. We argue that deciding how deeply to access memory for each query is as important as deciding what the memory should store. To this end, we introduce StreamScout, an adaptive inference framework that maintains only a lightweight textual timeline in context as the stream unfolds. At query time, StreamScout progressively augments the timeline with up to three increasingly informative visual views: a glance at recent frames, a uniform look-back over the past stream, and query-salient retrieval. At each stage, the model answers immediately if the available evidence is sufficient; otherwise, it escalates to the next view. To improve this stop-or-escalate policy, we probe the cascade on an auxiliary set and distill the model's empirical competence boundary into supervision for a lightweight LoRA adaptation, yielding StreamScout-S. We further refine the policy through reinforcement learning, allowing the model to explore stopping behaviors beyond imitation of the distilled decisions, yielding StreamScout-R. Across three backbones and three streaming benchmarks, StreamScout and its variants consistently outperform prior streaming methods while substantially reducing inference cost and token consumption; on OVO-Bench, for instance, StreamScout-S improves Qwen3-VL-8B by 14.65 points while using 59% fewer tokens than uniform sampling and answering in 1.04 s on average.

title: Reinforcement Learning Can Amplify Emergent Misalignment from Harmless Rewards
abstract: Emergent misalignment (EM) is the surprising tendency of language models to become broadly misaligned after fine-tuning on narrowly misaligned examples. While EM has been extensively studied in the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) setting, evidence that it also arises from reinforcement learning (RL) is limited to large, closed-source models, leaving the phenomenon expensive to study and difficult to reproduce. We characterize EM from RL in small, off-the-shelf open-weight models along three axes. First, we show that rewarding narrow, overtly misaligned behavior produces substantially higher general-domain misalignment than sample-matched SFT. Second, we show that EM from RL can be induced by reward signals that could plausibly arise naturally, such as unpopular aesthetic preferences or poor rhetorical appeals. Third, we evaluate in-training mitigations developed for SFT-induced EM and find that they broadly transfer, with preventive steering with persona vectors, interleaving safety data and inoculation prompting all performing well.
