title: Ampere: Communication-Efficient and High-Accuracy Split Federated Learning
abstract: A Federated Learning (FL) system collaboratively trains neural networks across devices and a server but is limited by significant on-device computation costs. Split Federated Learning (SFL) systems mitigate this by offloading a block of layers of the network from the device to a server. However, in doing so, it introduces large communication overheads due to frequent exchanges of intermediate activations and gradients between devices and the server and reduces model accuracy for non-IID data. We propose Ampere, a novel collaborative training system that simultaneously minimizes on-device computation and device-server communication while improving model accuracy. Unlike SFL, which uses a global loss by iterative end-to-end training, Ampere develops unidirectional inter-block training to sequentially train the device and server blocks with a local loss, eliminating the transfer of gradients. A lightweight auxiliary network generation method decouples training between the device and server, reducing frequent intermediate exchanges to a single transfer, which significantly reduces the communication overhead. Ampere mitigates the impact of data heterogeneity by consolidating activations generated by the trained device block to train the server block, in contrast to SFL, which trains on device-specific, non-IID activations. Extensive experiments on multiple CNNs and Transformers show that, compared to state-of-the-art SFL baseline systems, Ampere (i) improves model accuracy by up to 11.70 percentage points while training up to 18.6x faster, (ii) incurs up to 911x lower device-server communication overhead and up to 14.5x lower on-device computation, and (iii) reduces standard deviation of accuracy by 71.13% for various non-IID degrees highlighting superior performance when faced with heterogeneous data. Ampere is available from https://github.com/blessonvar/Ampere.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Geometric Optimization – Algorithm Design
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a unique paradigm for computational exploration, potentially enabling breakthroughs in complex optimization problems. This paper explores the design of a novel geometric optimization algorithm leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced precision and efficiency. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters using entangled qubit states, allowing for a fundamentally different optimization process compared to classical methods. The core mechanism centers around the exploitation of entanglement to create a parallel exploration of the solution space, resulting in a more robust and adaptable optimization strategy. The research investigates the potential of this algorithm to tackle challenging geometric optimization tasks, specifically focusing on the design of a self-adaptive system for parameter tuning within complex shapes. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical implications and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Self-Synchronous Chaos (ASCC)
abstract: Quantum State Adaptive Self-Synchronous Chaos (ASCC) is a novel quantum computing algorithm designed to enhance the stability and synchronicity of quantum computations through the utilization of adaptive self-synchronous chaos. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to achieve this goal by employing a quantum state evolution strategy that dynamically adjusts the quantum state's temporal dynamics. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the inherent chaotic nature of quantum systems, allowing for automated tuning of the evolution rate to mitigate decoherence and promote stable quantum states. The algorithm's potential benefits include increased robustness against environmental disturbances and improved coherence times – critical factors for practical quantum applications. We detail the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of ASCC in stabilizing quantum states. The proposed method represents a significant advancement in quantum algorithm design, offering a pathway towards more reliable and controllable quantum systems.

title: Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) for Anomaly Detection in Time Series
abstract: This paper explores the application of Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) to the challenging problem of anomaly detection in time series data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with the complexity and inherent variability found in real-world time series. HTM, originally developed for predictive coding and pattern recognition, offers a fundamentally different approach by learning hierarchical representations of temporal patterns. This work presents a framework for adapting HTM principles to time series anomaly detection, focusing on the use of "stocks" and "sequences" to capture and maintain temporal dependencies. The core claim is that HTM's ability to learn local patterns can be effectively leveraged to identify anomalies when these patterns are disrupted. We detail a system designed specifically for time series, outlining the key components and operational principles. The system learns by creating a hierarchy of temporal patterns, allowing for robust detection of deviations from the norm. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the potential of this approach, highlighting its ability to capture complex temporal relationships and identify subtle anomalies that might be missed by conventional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the broader implications of HTM for time series analysis.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Machine Learning Extension
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum machine learning approach leveraging dynamic topology to enhance data distribution modeling. Traditional machine learning often struggles with complex, high-dimensional data due to static models, necessitating complex parameter tuning. We introduce a quantum algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology of a quantum state space, allowing for a non-linear representation of data and an adaptive learning strategy. This design addresses challenges in data analysis and prediction, particularly when dealing with intricate datasets. The core mechanism centers around the creation and manipulation of dynamic quantum states, enabling the algorithm to capture complex correlations and patterns inherent in the input data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and initial experimental results on benchmark datasets, showcasing improved performance in data distribution modeling and prediction compared to existing quantum machine learning techniques.

title: Causal Discovery from Observational Data using Bayesian Networks with Dynamic Structure Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery from observational data utilizing dynamic Bayesian networks. Traditional Bayesian network structure learning methods often assume static datasets, failing to capture evolving causal relationships encountered in dynamic environments. Our methodology addresses this limitation by incorporating a dynamic structure learning algorithm that continuously adapts the Bayesian network's topology and parameter estimates as new data streams arrive. We leverage a variational inference technique to efficiently maintain probabilistic representations throughout this adaptation process. The core innovation lies in the iterative refinement of the network structure, allowing it to accurately represent causal dependencies that may shift over time. This approach offers a robust solution for causal discovery in scenarios where the underlying data distribution is not stationary, a common characteristic of many real-world applications. The system is designed to provide a more accurate understanding of causal relationships compared to static Bayesian network approaches, significantly improving decision-making capabilities in dynamic systems. The presented method is scalable and can handle large datasets, offering a practical solution for complex causal inference problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement for Matrix Calculation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar quantum phenomenon, offers a promising avenue for accelerating computations and enhancing security in the realm of quantum computing. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entangled quantum states to efficiently calculate complex matrices, specifically focusing on the application of a novel algorithm designed to address the challenges posed by quantum decoherence. We outline a proposed method predicated on quantum entanglement, detailing the core mechanisms and potential benefits. The work centers around leveraging the correlations inherent in entangled states to achieve a significant speedup in matrix operations compared to classical methods. This research investigates the feasibility of this approach for specific matrix types and proposes a preliminary assessment of its potential impact on quantum algorithm design and security protocols. The ultimate goal is to provide a foundational understanding of how entanglement can be strategically employed to expand the capabilities of quantum computation.

title: Title: Non-Local Graph Entanglement for Data Compression
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-local graph entanglement as a novel approach to data compression. Traditional data compression methods often rely on static algorithms and limited representations of data structure. We propose a new technique leveraging the inherent entanglement within graph structures to achieve significantly higher compression ratios than existing methods. This involves the development of a dynamic, self-replicating entanglement graph, which allows for compression and decompression based on the graph's topology and connectivity. We explore the mathematical foundations of this approach, detailing the entanglement generation and manipulation process, and present preliminary results demonstrating improved compression performance compared to traditional techniques. The research also considers the challenges of implementing this method on a practical scale, including efficient entanglement generation and management.

title: ## Baluchi Brush-tailed Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Baluchi Brush-tailed Mouse Algorithm" (BBMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Baluchi Brush-tailed Mouse (Trinomys sabralis). This rodent's unique method of navigating and locating food sources – characterized by erratic movements, strategic pauses, and a tendency to explore seemingly random areas before converging on a promising location – forms the core concept behind the BBMA. The algorithm leverages these observed behaviors to create a new search strategy within a metaheuristic framework. Specifically, the BBMA incorporates elements of stochastic exploration, adaptive pausing, and localized refinement, mimicking the mouse's efficient foraging process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results indicate that BBMA exhibits robust convergence properties and competitive performance, particularly in complex, multi-dimensional landscapes. Future research will explore the algorithm's adaptability to various problem domains and its integration with other optimization techniques.

title: Title: Adaptive Noise Shaping in Deep Learning (ANDS)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Noise Shaping (ANDS), a novel method for dynamically adjusting noise distributions within deep learning models to enhance generalization and robustness. Traditional noise shaping techniques often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's ability to adapt to diverse data. ANDS leverages a neural network to learn optimal noise levels based on a model's performance, creating a continuously evolving noise profile. This adaptive approach addresses the limitations of static shaping methods, offering a promising pathway towards improved model performance across a wider range of datasets and tasks. The core mechanism involves training a neural network to predict the impact of noise on model output, allowing for real-time adjustment. This paper details the architecture, training procedure, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of ANDS in improving model robustness and generalization. Keywords: Noise Shaping, Deep Learning, Neural Networks, Robustness, Generalization, Adaptive Learning.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Simulation of Complex Dynamical Systems (QESCS)
abstract: Abstract: Quantum-enhanced simulation of complex dynamical systems presents a significant challenge in scientific research and engineering. Traditional computational methods often struggle to effectively model and analyze intricate systems exhibiting nonlinear behavior. This paper introduces the Quantum-Enhanced Simulation of Complex Dynamical Systems (QESCS) methodology, a novel approach leveraging quantum computing to accelerate the simulation of these systems. We detail the fundamental principles behind the QESCS, outlining its architecture, computational steps, and potential benefits in terms of speed and accuracy. This research aims to provide a viable pathway for tackling computationally intensive dynamical systems simulations, offering a dramatic reduction in time and resource requirements.

title: ## Arabian Sheath-tailed Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Sheath-tail Bat Optimization (SBO)," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Arabian sheath-tailed bat ( *Tadarida thrasei*). This algorithm leverages the bat's unique hunting strategy – utilizing frequency-modulated ultrasonic calls – to efficiently explore the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. SBO incorporates a novel parameter, the "Echo Intensity," which dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance based on the bat's perceived information density. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, mimicking the bats' collective intelligence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SBO through its application to several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic techniques such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The core of SBO lies in the adaptive adjustment of the search radius and the 'Echo Intensity' parameter, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. The algorithm's design emphasizes robustness and adaptability, making it suitable for a broad range of complex optimization challenges. The performance evaluation is presented using metrics like convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational cost.

title: ## The Australian Magpie-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AMIOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Australian Magpie-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AMIOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of Australian Magpies. Magpies are known for their intelligent and adaptive search strategies when locating food sources. AMIOA leverages this behavior by mimicking the magpie's exploratory and exploitative phases, combined with a novel 'nest-building' mechanism to represent and refine solutions. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, similar to Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), but incorporates a dynamic weighting system influenced by the perceived 'richness' of the search space, mirroring a magpie's tendency to prioritize promising areas. The core innovation lies in the 'nest' representation, which provides a compact and informative summary of the current solution, guiding the search towards more promising regions. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundations, detailing its key components and operational rules, and providing a conceptual framework for its implementation.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Dynamics and Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear matrix dynamics to quantum entanglement, aiming to develop a robust and scalable framework for quantum information processing and quantum computation. We introduce a novel model that incorporates dynamic entanglement evolution, significantly enhancing the simulation and control capabilities of quantum systems. The core mechanism revolves around the implementation of a non-linear matrix dynamics, enabling a more realistic representation of entanglement and facilitating exploration of potential applications within quantum information handling. The resulting model offers a promising pathway toward enhanced computational efficiency and expanded quantum information processing possibilities. This work presents a fundamental framework for quantum entanglement modeling and control, pushing the boundaries of current quantum technologies.

title: The Mantis-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mantis-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies of the Chinese praying mantis. MIASA leverages the mantis's unique ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on prey movement and environmental changes. The algorithm incorporates adaptive parameter adjustment, a multi-stage search process mimicking the mantis's stalking, attack, and retreat behavior, and a novel "focusing" mechanism designed to concentrate exploration around promising regions of the search space. The core of MIASA lies in its dynamically adjusted 'attack range' and 'observation interval', which are governed by an adaptive rule set derived from observed mantis behavior. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods in complex, non-convex optimization landscapes. Future research will focus on implementing MIASA in various benchmark problems and evaluating its performance through simulations.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Automated Hypothesis Generation in Scientific Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to scientific discovery leveraging probabilistic programming for automated hypothesis generation. The core idea is to represent complex scientific theories as probabilistic programs, allowing for exploration of parameter spaces and the generation of testable hypotheses. This work outlines the methodology, focusing on the integration of probabilistic modeling with the iterative process of hypothesis formation, testing, and refinement. The system dynamically adapts to data, prioritizing hypotheses with high probability and minimizing the need for human intervention in the initial stages of exploration. The potential impact of this approach on accelerating scientific research is significant, offering a framework for systematically investigating complex systems and identifying new research avenues. The paper details a framework for representing scientific theories using probabilistic programs, generating hypotheses based on parameter space exploration, and evaluating the consistency of generated hypotheses with observed data. It emphasizes the role of probabilistic inference in guiding the hypothesis generation process and provides a conceptual architecture for such a system. Furthermore, the paper highlights the advantages of this approach in terms of objectivity, efficiency, and the ability to uncover hidden relationships within data.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Latent Counterfactual Exploration
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning – the process of reasoning about what would have happened if something had been different – is a cornerstone of human decision-making and a critical component of causal inference. However, traditional causal Bayesian networks often struggle to perform robust counterfactual reasoning, especially when dealing with unobserved latent variables that significantly influence the system under investigation. This paper introduces a novel framework for addressing this challenge, integrating latent counterfactual exploration using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method. The core mechanism involves iteratively sampling counterfactual scenarios while explicitly modeling the influence of these latent variables through a latent space representation. This approach enhances the reliability of counterfactual inference by accounting for the potentially confounding effects of unobserved factors. The resulting model provides a statistically rigorous combination of causal inference and counterfactual reasoning, overcoming limitations of existing approaches and offering a more nuanced understanding of causal relationships. The proposed method's ability to handle latent variables is key to its robustness and applicability in diverse scenarios where causal relationships are complex and incompletely understood.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unprecedented information security and, potentially, ultra-fast communication. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum entanglement information encoding and decoding algorithm, leveraging the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled states. We propose a new approach to secure communication and quantum computation, focusing on a dynamic encoding scheme that adapts to the environment, enhancing data resilience and offering potential for novel quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around establishing and managing entangled states, enabling secure key distribution and efficient data transfer. We investigate the potential of this algorithm in various quantum computing applications, including quantum key distribution and quantum state manipulation. This research delves into the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental investigations of this algorithm, highlighting its advantages and challenges.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of nonlinear topological quantum computation, focusing on the development of an adaptive topology encoding scheme. The core idea is to leverage quantum entanglement and the inherent adaptability of topological phases to dynamically adjust the structure of the encoded topology. This approach promises to enhance the efficiency of quantum computations by enabling real-time adjustments to the encoded quantum state. The work investigates the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and potential applications of this novel technique. We present a framework for generating and manipulating topological structures through entanglement, demonstrating its capability to create and adapt to varying quantum environments. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this innovative approach on the field of quantum information science.

title: HYED-Net: unified hierarchical feature refinement for co-registered nuclei segmentation and virtual IHC-to-mpIF staining
abstract: Achieving precise nuclei delineation from routine immunohistochemistry (IHC) images remains challenging because of staining variability and densely touching cells. In this work, we propose HYED-Net, a unified framework that jointly synthesizes co-registered virtual staining channels and predicts nuclei segmentation. The generated staining channels are used as auxiliary features within a segmentation-oriented refinement pathway. The segmentation head combines an Evidence-weighted Dirichlet Gate (ED-Gate) for dual-branch feature fusion, SS2D spatial mixing at selected encoder and decoder stages, and HyperKernel Skip Injection (HKSI) for auxiliary-conditioned depthwise skip modulation. Across three random seeds, HYED-Net obtains a Dice coefficient of $$0.758\pm 0.005$$ and an AJI of $$0.588\pm 0.010$$ on BCData, and a Dice coefficient of $$0.764\pm 0.002$$ and an AJI of $$0.470\pm 0.001$$ on DeepLIIF. Together, these results demonstrate stable in-domain performance and support the feasibility of joint virtual staining and nuclei segmentation within a unified feature-refinement framework.

title: Invalidation Contracts for Cross-Episode Agent Memory
abstract: LLM agents that cache recovery suggestions from API errors can skip re-derivation in later episodes, spending fewer tokens and fewer model calls on constraints they have already learned. Server-side data drift turns those cached fixes into silent failures, and the usual remedy, re-deriving on every episode, gives the savings back. We introduce invalidation contracts, a protocol layer that attaches version stamps and cacheability hints to every recovery suggestion so the client can evict stale entries without trial and error, and keep the rest. The contract decomposes realized savings into two independent factors: validity, the fraction of cached suggestions that remain correct after a drift event, and compliance, the fraction the planner applies on the first attempt. Validity depends only on the protocol and is vendor-independent. Compliance depends on the planner model: identical wire bytes yield 100% first-try compliance on Claude Haiku 4.5 and 11% or below on Claude Sonnet 5, which exhibits input-schema conservatism, refusing fixes that add fields the original request did not contain. We evaluate across seven models, three serving paths, two domains, and approximately 9,400 episodes. Row-level invalidation raises compliance by 0 to 66.7 percentage points across the seven models, 55.6 to 66.7 on three, and recovers 29-33% of baseline token cost on four of seven models, while table-level invalidation destroys co-located entries and drops post-drift first-try rates to 0% on five of seven. Eviction precision is 1.00 at row granularity on every model under the row-level oracle of Section 4.1. The contract adds 15% to response payload. Version-stamp validity is deterministic by construction and produced identical results across every model and serving path, with zero contract failures in the entire evaluation.

title: PIU: Proximity-guided Identity Unlearning in ID-Conditioned Diffusion Models
abstract: Identity-conditioned diffusion models enable high-quality and identity-consistent face generation, but they also raise severe privacy concerns, as models may continue to synthesize individuals despite their right to be forgotten. While machine unlearning has been extensively studied for concept and data removal, identity unlearning remains largely unexplored, particularly in models conditioned directly on identity embeddings rather than text prompts. In this work, we study identity unlearning in Arc2Face, a state-of-the-art identity-conditioned latent diffusion model for face generation, and introduce Proximity-guided Identity Unlearning (PIU), an anchor-guided framework for identity unlearning. Specifically, we formulate identity removal as an identity replacement objective that reassigns the source identity to a selected anchor identity in the learned identity space, and we complement it with a proximity-based anchor selection strategy motivated by the geometry of ArcFace representations. We further show that effective unlearning can be achieved through localized fine-tuning of a small subset of identity-sensitive cross-attention layers. Experiments across multiple target identities show that our framework effectively suppresses generation of the target identity while preserving realism and identity consistency for retained identities, as validated by improved performance on unlearning and image-quality metrics, together with qualitative evaluation. The source code for the PIU identity unlearning framework is made publicly available at https://github.com/edgarcancinoe/piu-unlearning.

title: Sublinear Space Graph Algorithms in the Continual Release Model
abstract: The graph continual release model of differential privacy seeks to produce differentially private solutions to graph problems under a stream of edge updates where new private solutions are released after each update. Previously known edge differentially private algorithms for most graph problems including densest subgraph and matchings in the continual release setting only output real-valued estimates (not vertex subset solutions) and do not use sublinear space. In this paper, we leverage sparsification to address the above shortcomings for edge-insertion streams. Our edge differentially private algorithms use sublinear space with respect to the number of edges in the graph. In addition, for the densest subgraph problem, we output edge differentially private vertex subset solutions; no previous graph algorithms in the continual release model output such subsets. We make novel use of sparsification techniques from the non-private streaming and static graph algorithms literature to achieve new results in the sublinear space continual release setting. This includes algorithms for densest subgraph, maximum matching, and the first continual release k-core decomposition algorithm. To complement our insertion-only algorithms, we conclude with polynomial additive error lower bounds for edge-privacy in the fully dynamic setting, where only logarithmic lower bounds were previously known.

To complement our insertion-only algorithms, we conclude with polynomial additive error lower bounds for edge-privacy in the fully dynamic setting, where only logarithmic lower bounds were previously known.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Fraud Investigations: A Critical Review.
abstract: Abstract: AI significantly influences the financial fraud investigations across different parts of the workflow related to detection, automation, transactions prioritization, anomalous discovery, and fraud investigation explanations. This approach has documented highest performance metrics across empirical studies, to support detecting fraud in a set number of parameters. Random assessment gave up to 96% Accuracy (with a 98.9% Area under the curve); fuzzy logistic regression provides an AUC up to >0.99, with up to 0.90+ Sensitivity and Specificity on credit-card. Fraud investigation explanation AI ensemble “FraudX AI” provides 95% Recall and a 97% AUCPRC” (Afriyie et al., 2023; Baisholan et al., 2025; Charizanos et al., 2024). Machine learning cut unexpected losses by 15% compared with static heuristics. Meanwhile economic optimization showed a further reduction in expected losses and produced false positive rate of 0.4 percent (Vanini et al., 2023) which shows, that machine intelligence actually carries some operational weight once it predicts results in a financial decision. Although some performance measures that are heterogeneous among studies such as - a variety of approaches does not include specificity (often called precision), sensitivity (sometimes referred to as recall, or true positive rate), expected lost value added (often denoted by false positive burden, that for financial decision tasks refers to economic value) is frequently missed from reporting. None of the surveyed machine learning applications has achieved reasonable industrial applicability from their authors own perspective, except that there are few surveyed approaches which for an assessment of scalability and reliability are reported with reasonable degree of success in an industrial environment. (Ryman-Tubb et al., 2018). Explainability appears to be the furthest behind in Anti money laundering (AML) applications with 51% of machine learning models under review being categorized noninterpretable and no documented application of explainable AI reported at the time of writing in AML literature (Kute et al. 2021). On the whole AI best functions as a support in an investigation, not a tool that replaces auditor, compliance officer or investigation. Its effectiveness is related to managing class imbalance, dealing with dynamic fraud profiles, using privacy-preserving methods for data sharing, accurate labelling and obtaining evidence that can be understood by humans and is verifiable institution-to-institution, jurisdiction-to-jurisdiction.

title: 基于自适应的神经元网络的强化学习算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm based on adaptive neuron networks, designed to automate the learning and parameter adjustment of neural network structures. The core innovation lies in a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism driven by environment feedback, coupled with an adaptive learning process that optimizes the network's topology. The algorithm aims to improve the efficiency of reinforcement learning by reducing the reliance on manual tuning and promoting more robust and adaptable neural network configurations. We analyze the algorithm's performance across diverse tasks and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving significant improvements in training speed and generalization ability compared to traditional RL methods.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Discovering Graph Embeddings
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have achieved significant success in various graph-related tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. However, a critical limitation of many GNN approaches is their dependence on large amounts of labeled data for training. Obtaining such labeled data can be costly, time-consuming, and often impractical, particularly for large and complex graphs. This paper proposes a novel approach to learning graph embeddings using self-supervised learning (SSL). We hypothesize that intrinsic relationships within a graph structure can be leveraged to learn informative embeddings without relying on explicit labels. Our method utilizes self-supervised tasks designed to exploit the graph's connectivity and structure. Specifically, we explore techniques like contrastive learning and masked node prediction to learn embeddings that capture the underlying graph topology. We demonstrate that our self-supervised approach can learn effective graph embeddings, achieving comparable or superior performance compared to traditional supervised methods when labeled data is scarce. The key contributions of this work are the application of SSL to graph embedding learning and the design of novel self-supervised tasks tailored for graph data.

title: Quantum Topology and Machine Learning: A Hybrid Learning Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a theoretical framework describing the properties of space and its connection to quantum mechanics, has emerged as a promising area of research with potential applications in various fields, including quantum computing and machine learning. This paper explores the integration of quantum topology with machine learning, specifically focusing on the design of a novel self-adaptive learning algorithm leveraging the unique characteristics of quantum computation. The core idea is to utilize the inherent adaptability of quantum systems to optimize the learning process, thereby enhancing model performance and efficiency. The presented approach aims to address limitations of traditional machine learning algorithms by incorporating quantum computational principles. This research investigates the potential benefits of such a hybrid approach, presenting a framework for leveraging quantum topology to accelerate and refine machine learning models.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization via Wave Function Mirroring
abstract: Quantum information processing demands robust synchronization across distributed quantum systems. Current approaches often struggle with maintaining coherence over significant distances, limiting the scalability of quantum computations. This paper introduces a novel protocol, Wave Function Mirroring, designed to address this challenge by utilizing wave function mirroring to synchronize quantum states across multiple locations. The algorithm meticulously mirrors the evolution of quantum states, mitigating decoherence effects and facilitating distributed quantum computations with enhanced coherence. We present a rigorous mathematical framework and detailed implementation demonstrating the protocol's effectiveness in achieving synchronized states.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Code Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing quantum error correction (QEC) codes, termed Dynamic QEC Code Optimization (DQCO). The core claim is to dynamically adjust both the encoding and decoding parameters of QEC codes to enhance their error correction performance. The proposed mechanism involves real-time adaptation of the encoding rate and decoding strategy based on the observed communication environment and noise levels. This approach strengthens the adaptive capacity of QEC codes, allowing them to better meet the demands of complex communication scenarios. The algorithm employs a feedback loop, continuously monitoring the channel characteristics and adjusting the QEC parameters accordingly. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the optimization process, including the channel capacity estimation, the rate distortion function analysis, and the adaptive adjustment of the coding and decoding parameters. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in error correction performance compared to static QEC schemes.

title: Causal Graph Learning with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal graph learning leveraging the strengths of reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional methods for discovering causal relationships often falter when confronted with high-dimensional datasets and intricate feedback loops, frequently relying on assumptions that may not hold true in real-world scenarios. Our framework addresses these limitations by training an RL agent to iteratively construct a causal graph. The agent's actions involve modifying the graph – adding or removing edges – based on observed system behavior. The reward signal is determined by the accuracy of predictions made using the current graph representation. This integration of causal inference with RL enables the network to adapt and learn causal relationships within complex, dynamic environments, offering a potentially more robust and scalable solution compared to conventional techniques. We outline the core principles, the proposed agent architecture, and the reward function design.

title: 混沌域的自建领域优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-built optimization algorithm based on the concept of a chaotic domain. The algorithm leverages the dynamic nature of chaotic domains to rapidly adapt to varying system parameters, offering a potentially transformative approach to optimizing complex systems. The core mechanism centers around constructing a chaotic domain representation of the system's objective function, allowing for efficient parameter adjustment through iterative refinement. We explore the potential of this approach in the context of machine learning, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experimental results. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and limitations of this new method, emphasizing its potential to address challenges in optimization within complex systems.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state matching algorithm based on an adaptive topological structure. Traditional quantum state matching approaches often rely on static matching methods, while our algorithm leverages the inherent properties of topological structures to dynamically match quantum states and enhance system stability. This work introduces a robust framework for quantum state manipulation, offering a significant improvement over existing methods. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around constructing a topological map that facilitates precise state alignment, achieving higher fidelity and stability in quantum systems. This research explores the potential of utilizing topological structures to address challenges in quantum state preservation and control.

abstract: This paper presents a novel high-order quantum entanglement computing framework designed to enhance computational efficiency and precision. The framework leverages advanced quantum entanglement to enable adaptive quantum algorithms, dynamically adjusting parameters to optimize performance. We explore the architectural design, core mechanisms, and potential benefits of this approach. The research focuses on overcoming limitations inherent in traditional quantum computing approaches, particularly concerning the ability to precisely control and manipulate entangled states. title: Based on Quantum Entanglement Key Agreement Protocol
abstract: This paper presents a novel key agreement protocol leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The protocol, termed the "Quantum Entanglement Key Agreement Protocol" (QEKAP), aims to establish a shared secret key between two parties, Alice and Bob, without relying on classical communication channels for key exchange. The core of the protocol utilizes entangled photon pairs to generate correlated random keys, followed by the application of quantum error correction codes to mitigate the effects of noise and ensure accurate key transmission. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and highlight its potential advantages over traditional key exchange methods, specifically addressing vulnerabilities associated with eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks. The protocol's security rests on the fundamental laws of quantum mechanics, namely the no-cloning theorem and the uncertainty principle. The key parameters influencing the protocol's performance, such as entanglement fidelity and the overhead introduced by the quantum error correction scheme, are analyzed. Simulation results indicate that QEKAP provides a robust and secure solution for key distribution in quantum networks.

title: The Quantum Algorithmic Optimization of Self-Organized Structures
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-organized quantum algorithms to optimize complex geometric structures. Traditional quantum algorithms are often limited by the inherent challenges of quantum systems, particularly in maintaining coherence and entanglement. This work proposes a novel approach that leverages the dynamic nature of graphs to guide the optimization process, enabling global optimization of complex geometries. The core mechanism centers around the design of a self-organizing quantum algorithm that adapts to the structure of the problem, iteratively refining the solution towards the desired outcome. The research explores the potential of using graph representations to model the geometric structure, and the resulting algorithm's ability to enhance the performance of various optimization tasks. The paper introduces a framework for evaluating the effectiveness of such algorithms using a defined metric. Finally, the work discusses the theoretical implications and potential future directions of this approach.

title: ## The Nautilus-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NASAL)
abstract: This paper introduces the Nautilus-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NASAL), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and shell morphology of the Nautilus shell. The algorithm leverages the Nautilus's ability to maintain a stable position while adapting its path to navigate complex environments, mirroring a strategy of exploring diverse solutions while retaining promising ones. NASAL incorporates elements of both adaptive step size control, mimicking the Nautilus's subtle movements, and a dynamic neighborhood structure, reflecting the shell's layered design. The core of NASAL lies in a novel 'Spiral-Adaptive Exploration' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance, and a 'Shell-Based Cluster' strategy for solution representation and diversification. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundation, detailed implementation, and discusses its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Complex Systems Simulation
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference (QEBI) presents a novel approach to complex systems simulation, aiming to significantly improve model accuracy through the application of quantum mechanics in Bayesian inference. This paper introduces a new algorithm, the 'Quantum-Guided Bayesian Network' (QGBN), designed to overcome the computational limitations inherent in traditional Bayesian methods when dealing with highly complex systems. QEBI leverages quantum mechanics to enhance probabilistic inference, reducing computational cost while maintaining high accuracy. The QGBN employs a quantum-guided process that minimizes the influence of noise and allows for more precise uncertainty quantification. We demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations of a dynamic, multi-layered system exhibiting complex interactions and sensitivity to initial conditions. The results show substantial improvements in model accuracy and reduced computational time compared to existing methods.

title: Quantum Sensing Based on Quantum Noise
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum sensing that fundamentally shifts the perspective on quantum noise. Instead of viewing it as an unwanted disturbance, we argue that quantum noise is a critical resource for extracting subtle environmental information. The core concept involves designing a quantum sensor that leverages the statistical properties of quantum noise to precisely measure and interpret its distribution, ultimately enabling the detection of extremely weak signals. This approach moves beyond traditional quantum sensing methodologies which often rely on minimizing noise. We present a theoretical framework and mathematical formalism for this concept, outlining the principles of operation and potential performance characteristics. The underlying mechanism hinges on the ability to correlate the statistical fluctuations of quantum noise with the underlying environmental signal. This work represents a significant departure from conventional thinking and offers a new paradigm for quantum sensing technology. ---

title: Explainable AI for Deep Reinforcement Learning via Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models have demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex tasks, but their inherent complexity often leads to a lack of interpretability. These models are frequently referred to as "black boxes," making it challenging to understand the rationale behind their decisions. This paper proposes a novel approach to explain DRL models by leveraging counterfactual reasoning. We introduce a framework that generates counterfactual examples – "what if" scenarios – by systematically altering the input state and observing the resulting changes in the agent's actions. These counterfactual examples reveal the critical factors driving the agent's behavior, offering a more transparent and understandable explanation of the DRL model's decision-making process. The core of our method relies on identifying the minimal changes in the input that lead to a change in the agent's policy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and discuss its potential applications in various DRL domains. Our approach offers a pathway towards building more trustworthy and reliable DRL systems.

title: ## Blackspot Rhineland Codon Polarized Adaptive Search (BRCPAS) Algorithm
abstract: The blackspot rhineland codon ( *Lophiomusmus manetti*) exhibits remarkable adaptability to changing environmental conditions, particularly in its ability to dynamically adjust its bioluminescence patterns – a process often referred to as "codon polarization". This paper introduces the Blackspot Rhineland Codon Polarized Adaptive Search (BRCPAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by this unique biological behavior. BRCPAS utilizes a polarization mechanism, analogous to the codon's light modulation, to selectively explore and exploit the search space. The algorithm maintains a population of potential solutions, each associated with a 'polarization vector' representing its dominance in a given region. The polarization vectors are iteratively adjusted based on the objective function value and the diversity of the population, promoting both convergence and exploration. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its adaptive nature and suitability for complex optimization problems.

title: ## American Lion: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the American Lion
abstract: This paper presents American Lion, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of the American lion (Panthera leo atrox). The algorithm leverages the lion's strategic movement, hunting tactics, and social dynamics to create a robust and efficient search process. American Lion incorporates key features such as a dynamic territory exploration, a sophisticated decision-making mechanism based on relative fitness, and a social interaction component simulating the lion's collaborative hunting. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The core mechanics are defined by the following: a territory representation, a movement strategy based on fitness gradient, a decision-making rule for territory selection, and a social interaction mechanism for collaborative exploration. The performance of American Lion is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving global optimization. The algorithm is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to showcase its advantages in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The results demonstrate that American Lion provides a competitive and promising approach to tackling complex optimization problems.

title: 基于多模态数据融合的异常检测算法
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection leveraging the fusion of multi-modal data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on single data modalities, which can be susceptible to noise and limited in their ability to capture complex patterns indicative of anomalies. This research posits that integrating information from multiple sources – such as text, images, and audio – provides a more robust and accurate representation of the underlying system. The core mechanism involves a fusion technique that combines these disparate data streams, followed by an anomaly detection algorithm applied to the fused data. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance compared to single-modal approaches, particularly in scenarios with noisy or incomplete data. We present a framework for multi-modal fusion and anomaly detection, focusing on algorithmic design and performance evaluation. The proposed method aims to enhance the accuracy and robustness of anomaly detection systems across various applications.

title: African Manatee Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Manatee Search Algorithm" (MSA), inspired by the foraging behavior of African manatees. Manatees exhibit a unique strategy for locating food sources, characterized by a combination of exploration and exploitation. The MSA leverages these behaviors to generate a new optimization algorithm designed for tackling complex, non-linear optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of manatee foraging, including a "scanning" mechanism for exploring the search space and a "focusing" mechanism for refining promising solutions. Mathematical formulations are presented to explain the core operations of the MSA, including the position update rule, the guiding vector generation, and the selection mechanism. The performance of the MSA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results show that MSA offers a competitive approach to optimization, particularly in scenarios where exploration and exploitation need to be carefully balanced. The algorithm's adaptive nature, stemming from the manatee's natural intelligence, allows it to navigate complex landscapes and converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions effectively.

title: African Hammada Jerboa: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavioral Traits of a Desert Rodent
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, African Hammada Jerboa (AHJ), inspired by the foraging behavior of African Hammada Jerboas, small rodents adapted to the harsh desert environment. These animals exhibit remarkable strategies for resource acquisition, including intermittent movement, clustered searching, and adaptive adjustment based on environmental feedback. AHJ leverages these observed traits to develop a new optimization algorithm suitable for complex, non-linear problems. The algorithm incorporates a clustered search mechanism, a dynamic adjustment of step sizes proportional to resource availability, and a novel 'inertia modulation' technique mimicking the jerboa's response to sand dune shifts. The performance of AHJ is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The key innovations of AHJ lie in its adaptive exploration and exploitation strategies, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. The algorithm's design principles are discussed in detail, and future research directions are proposed.

title: Cost-Sensitive TSK for Recognition of Imbalanced Epilepsy EEG Signal
abstract: Epilepsy EEG signal recognition is an important method for epilepsy detection. However, the traditional machine learning methods used for epilepsy EEG signal recognition face many challenges. For example, traditional intelligent recognition methods often ignore the imbalance of epilepsy EEG signals, which misclassifies positive samples and may cause serious consequences; the existing imbalanced classification methods ignore class-guided global inter-class correlations among samples, resulting in poor classification results. In order to overcome these challenges, a cost-sensitive-based TSK method (CITSK) is proposed for imbalanced epilepsy EEG signal recognition. This proposed method constructs a Class-guided Sample Collaborative Relationship (SCR) matrix to assign higher weight to positive minority samples, and supplements global inter-class collaborative penalty information on the basis of the traditional static cost-sensitive matrix. Then, a model combining the SCR matrix and TSK is proposed, which inherits the good generalization ability and interpretability of TSK while ensuring classification performance. Experiments on real EEG datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and its applicability to the imbalanced classification of epileptic EEG signals. Quantitatively, the CITSK method achieves an average Accuracy of 93.96%, an average F_measure of 88.33%, and an average G_means of 91.34% across various imbalanced datasets. Furthermore, comparative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed CITSK achieves superior overall performance across comprehensive evaluation metrics compared to baseline models, offering a highly robust and interpretable solution for imbalanced data scenarios via reasonable global inter-class penalty compensation.

title: Uso de grafos direcionados ponderados aplicados na criptografia RSA
abstract: A Teoria dos Grafos oferece diversas aplicações na computação, inclusive na segurança da informação. Este trabalho propõe uma abordagem alternativa para a criptografia RSA, utilizando caminhos entre dois vértices de digrafos ponderados com números primos como peso. Em vez de gerar novos primos a cada criação de chaves, como no Multiprime RSA, a proposta utiliza um grafo previamente construído, onde os pesos são atribuídos com base no algoritmo de geração de primos em um intervalo, entre a e b, de Ezz-Eldien et al., que apresenta complexidade de tempo O(b) e espacial O(b-a). Apesar do custo inicial elevado devido à construção do grafo, a geração subsequente de chaves torna-se mais eficiente. A solução mantém a possibilidade de grande quantidade de chaves possíveis que serem criadas do Multiprime RSA, porém aumentando a robustez do sistema e permite paralelismo na cifração e decifração. No entanto, como as variantes do RSA tradicional, continua vulnerável à computação quântica.

title: CoLT-Drive: Counterfactual Long-Tail Benchmarking and Knowledge-Preserving Adaptation for Driving Affordance Prediction
abstract: Long-tail autonomous driving failures are often framed as rare-object recognition errors. We argue that this view is incomplete: the decision-critical question is not only whether a model recognizes an unusual object, but whether it infers how that object changes the ego vehicle's feasible high-level actions. We formalize this problem as decision-level driving affordance prediction, where a model maps a front-view image, ego-motion history, and navigation command to a structured longitudinal--lateral meta-action. To evaluate this capability, we introduce CoLT-Drive, a 3,536-sample counterfactual long-tail benchmark that inserts rare objects into otherwise fixed driving scenes and measures whether models predict acceptable action pairs. To improve deployable small VLMs, we propose KPA, a knowledge-preserving adaptation framework that combines structured perception-to-decision prompting, SLERP-based expert merging, and RegMoE, a regime-aware LoRA mixture-of-experts module. KPA preserves the pretrained model's open-world knowledge while allocating lightweight adaptation capacity to different driving decision regimes. Experiments on an in-domain driving split and CoLT-Drive show that KPA achieves 60.8\% pair accuracy on CoLT-Drive, outperforming the pretrained Qwen3-VL-2B baseline (50.3\%) and LoRA SFT (32.4\%) while maintaining competitive in-domain accuracy. Our benchmark and code are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/tangzx2024/CoLT-Drive and https://github.com/tangzhengxu/CoLT-Drive.

title: SCALE:Scalable Conditional Atlas-Level Endpoint transport for virtual cell perturbation prediction
abstract: Virtual-cell models aim to predict how cell populations respond to perturbations, but control and treated cells are measured as unpaired populations, complicating the learning of perturbation-specific effects. We present SCALE, a conditional transport model that represents cells as unordered sets and predicts treated populations without cell-level matching. A shared set-aware encoder and conditional DiT backbone learn latent transport, making endpoint supervision directly delta-aligned without an auxiliary delta objective. Across genetic, chemical, developmental and immune perturbations, SCALE recovered gene-expression changes, response directions and population structure. In CRISPR data with dominant cell-line effects, SCALE outperformed competing methods across seven metrics and maintained separation among gene-target representations rather than collapsing them into a shared region. SCALE further prioritized cytokines predicted to produce distinct immune activation and inflammatory responses. Experiments using matched PBMC samples from three donors confirmed these predicted differences. Together, SCALE enables perturbation-specific prediction from unpaired populations and supports experimental prioritization.

title: Theory of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry with General Markovian Light Sources
abstract: Quantum optical systems comprising quantum emitters interacting with engineered optical modes generate non-classical states of light that can be used as resource states for quantum-enhanced interferometry. However, outside of well-controlled systems producing either single-mode states (e.g. Fock states or squeezed states) or highly symmetric multi-mode states (e.g. superradiant states), their potential for quantum advantage remains uncharacterized. In this work, we develop a framework to analyze quantum enhanced interferometry with general Markovian quantum light sources. First, by connecting the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the photons emitted by a source to the multi-time correlation functions and the source dynamics, we elucidate the link between the level structure and spectrum of the source to a potential quantum advantage in interferometry. Second, we analyze optimal measurement protocols that can be used to achieve this quantum advantage with experimentally available optical elements. In particular, we show that tunable optical elements with Kerr non-linearity can always be harnessed to implement the optimal measurement for any given source. Simultaneously, we also outline general conditions under which linear optics and photodetection is enough to implement the optimal measurement.

title: STROMATIC PHILOSOPHY of Quantum Computing
abstract: The future that is sketched is not that of an omniscient machine nor of a simple acceleration of what is already known. It is that of a new capacity to generate knowledge about regimes of nature and mathematics that until now remained opaque. That capacity will be fully realized only to the extent that the operative subject continues to weave, with material rigor, conceptual ambition, and historial responsibility, the threads that make possible the passage from the possible to the effective. In that fabric — dense,discontin., co-determined — resides the true philosophical depth of quantum computing.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Framework
abstract: Abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum topology framework designed to automatically optimize quantum computation performance by dynamically adjusting the quantum system's topology based on computational tasks. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on manual intervention, lacking the inherent topological structure of quantum systems. Our framework leverages this structure to enhance quantum computation efficiency through intelligent adjustments. This research explores the potential of this approach to improve the design and execution of quantum algorithms.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry for Quantum Computing Verification
abstract: This paper explores the application of nonlinear topological geometry to quantum computing, focusing on the design of a quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging quantum entanglement. We propose a novel approach that utilizes the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to establish a mathematically verifiable QKD scheme. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum state distribution based on entangled topological structures, facilitating rigorous mathematical analysis and theoretical validation of QKD protocols. The paper demonstrates the potential of this technique to simplify the process of validating quantum computations, offering a fundamentally new way to approach the challenges of quantum security.

title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy: Enhancing Privacy in Decentralized Model Training
abstract: Federated learning (FL) presents a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, the inherent collaborative nature of FL still poses privacy risks. This paper investigates the integration of differential privacy (DP) into the FL framework to provide an enhanced level of privacy protection. We introduce a novel approach where noise is injected into model parameters during the training process, adhering to the principles of DP. This mechanism mitigates the risk of information leakage from individual user data while maintaining model accuracy. We formally define the proposed algorithm and analyze its privacy-utility trade-off. The results demonstrate that the incorporation of DP significantly strengthens the privacy guarantees of FL, offering a robust solution for privacy-sensitive applications. Our work contributes to the growing body of research focused on secure and privacy-preserving FL techniques.

title: 基于自适应自适应学习的神经网络
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture, termed "Dynamic Adaptive Learning Network" (DALLN), designed to enhance convergence and generalization performance through adaptive learning rates. Traditional neural networks often struggle with varying input complexity, necessitating fixed learning rates that can hinder optimization. DALLN incorporates a dynamic learning rate adjustment mechanism, intelligently adjusting the learning rate of each component based on the current input. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments across diverse datasets, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and generalization accuracy compared to baseline networks. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop, continuously monitoring the network's performance and adjusting the learning rates accordingly. The paper provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design and implementation, including mathematical formulations and visualizations to illustrate the dynamic adjustment process.

title: Dynamic Quantum Circuit Synthesis and Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum circuit synthesis and optimization, addressing the significant challenges in designing efficient quantum algorithms. The core idea is to develop a system capable of dynamically generating and optimizing quantum circuits based on the specific characteristics of quantum hardware and the demands of the targeted quantum algorithm. The system employs optimization algorithms, such as quantum annealing or genetic algorithms, to navigate the vast space of possible quantum circuits, incorporating hardware constraints throughout the optimization process. This automated design approach aims to overcome the complexities inherent in traditional quantum circuit synthesis, ultimately accelerating the progress of quantum computing by facilitating the realization of practical and efficient quantum algorithms. The developed system is designed to adapt to varying quantum hardware limitations, leading to optimized circuit designs for a wide range of quantum algorithms. The key contribution lies in the integration of hardware-aware optimization within a dynamic synthesis framework.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum simulation and optimization leveraging the dynamic nature of quantum states. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on static representations, limiting their ability to accurately model complex quantum systems. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the quantum state throughout the simulation process, enabling a more refined and efficient representation of the system's behavior. This dynamic adaptation, coupled with a sophisticated optimization strategy, allows for the exploration of a broader range of possible solutions and improved model accuracy. The core mechanism centers around capturing the intricate dynamics of quantum systems through continuous state evolution, offering a significant advancement over static simulation techniques. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to accelerate the design and analysis of complex quantum systems, particularly in areas of optimization and modeling.

title: Quantum State Prediction of the Non-Bogoshev-Lasshere-Brown-Jordan Equation (NBLJ) – Improved
abstract: Quantum state prediction is a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing. Traditional methods often struggle to accurately predict the probability distribution of quantum states, hindering efficient quantum information handling. This paper introduces a novel approach, the Non-Bogoshev-Lasshere-Brown-Jordan Equation (NBLJ) improved, which leverages quantum entanglement to enhance the prediction process. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through rigorous numerical simulations and analysis of complex quantum systems. The core mechanism involves the utilization of entangled states to accelerate the probabilistic estimation of quantum states. This improved version offers a significant advancement in prediction accuracy and efficiency, offering a pathway toward optimized quantum information processing.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Models Based on Causal Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of interpretability in deep learning models, often referred to as the "black box" problem. Current methods for explaining deep learning decisions frequently lack a fundamental understanding of *why* a model makes a particular prediction. We propose a novel approach that integrates deep learning models with causal reasoning techniques to achieve a more robust and meaningful explanation of model behavior. Specifically, we aim to identify causal relationships within the model's learned representations and use these relationships to elucidate the reasons behind its predictions. This framework allows us to move beyond simply highlighting features that contribute to a prediction (as in methods like LIME or SHAP) and instead focus on the underlying causal mechanisms driving the model's decision-making process. The core idea is to treat the deep learning model as a complex, potentially biased, causal system and leverage established causal inference techniques to analyze and interpret its behavior. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this approach, highlighting its advantages in terms of transparency and trust.

evidence.title: Explainable Deep Learning Models Based on Causal Reasoning
evidence.abstract: This paper investigates the problem of interpretability in deep learning models, often referred to as the "black box" problem. Current methods for explaining deep learning decisions frequently lack a fundamental understanding of *why* a model makes a particular prediction. We propose a novel approach that integrates deep learning models with causal reasoning techniques to achieve a more robust and meaningful explanation of model behavior. Specifically, we aim to identify causal relationships within the model's learned representations and use these relationships to elucidate the reasons behind its predictions. This framework allows us to move beyond simply highlighting features that contribute to a prediction (as in methods like LIME or SHAP) and instead focus on the underlying causal mechanisms driving the model's decision-making process. The core idea is to treat the deep learning model as a complex, potentially biased, causal system and leverage established causal inference techniques to analyze and interpret its behavior. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this approach, highlighting its advantages in terms of transparency and trust.

title: Quantum Algorithm Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm, Quantum Algorithm Dynamic Adjustment (QADA), designed to dynamically adjust quantum parameters during execution to optimize performance across a range of datasets. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to specific input data. QADA leverages quantum circuits with adjustable parameters, allowing the algorithm to dynamically adapt to diverse datasets, resulting in significant performance improvements. This work explores the theoretical and practical aspects of this approach, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of existing quantum algorithms.

title: Decentralized Learning with Federated Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to decentralized learning utilizing Federated Graph Neural Networks (FedGNNs). The core idea is to facilitate collaborative knowledge discovery across a network of devices by employing locally maintained graph representations and periodically synchronized Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). This framework addresses the limitations of traditional federated learning, particularly when dealing with graph-structured data, where raw data sharing poses significant privacy concerns. The system avoids direct data exchange by allowing devices to collaboratively learn through the exchange of model updates, preserving data privacy while enabling effective knowledge transfer. The proposed FedGNN architecture consists of local graphs and locally trained GNNs, synchronized via a novel aggregation mechanism. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components required for implementation. The system is designed to be scalable and adaptable to various decentralized network topologies. This work represents a significant step towards privacy-preserving collaborative learning in complex, graph-based environments.

title: 高维空间自适应算法与机器学习的协同进化
abstract: This paper investigates the synergistic integration of high-dimensional space self-adaptation algorithms and machine learning techniques to enhance the generalization and efficiency of machine learning models. Traditional machine learning methods often struggle with high-dimensional data, presenting a significant challenge in optimizing model performance. We propose a novel framework that leverages the inherent self-adaptability of high-dimensional spaces to improve model capabilities. The core mechanism involves mapping high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional representation, followed by a machine learning algorithm that learns and optimizes this representation. This approach fosters robust models capable of handling complex datasets and achieving superior generalization. The paper explores the benefits of this combined approach and presents a preliminary investigation into its impact on machine learning performance.

title: Barbastelle: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Barbastelle Bats
abstract: This paper presents Barbastelle, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Barbastelle bats. Barbastelle combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a novel adaptive adjustment mechanism mimicking the bats' echolocation and flight patterns. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic population size, velocity updates based on both global and local best positions, and a 'pulse-echo' strategy for exploring the search space. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Barbastelle exhibits competitive convergence rates and solution quality compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The key innovation lies in its ability to dynamically adapt the exploration and exploitation phases based on the perceived complexity and density of the search landscape, mirroring the bats' efficient use of limited information. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be easily tunable, allowing for flexible adaptation to different problem characteristics. This research contributes a novel optimization approach with potential applications in diverse fields including engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Wave Function Collapse Dynamics
abstract: Quantum-enhanced wave function collapse dynamics represents a novel approach to simulating complex quantum processes by leveraging quantum annealing. This paper investigates the potential of this method to optimize the collapse of wave function states, ultimately leading to more accurate simulations of advanced quantum phenomena. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the 'collapse probability' of a quantum state using quantum annealing, a process designed to improve the precision of the simulation. The current research explores this concept through a comprehensive analysis of its theoretical underpinnings and preliminary simulations, highlighting its promise for advancing quantum system modeling.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Collaborative Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed collaborative learning leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that entanglement's non-locality can facilitate high-efficiency information transfer and collaborative learning among nodes in a distributed system, surpassing the limitations imposed by classical communication channels. The proposed mechanism involves each node maintaining a quantum state, shared through entangled states, enabling instantaneous correlations and facilitating collaborative learning. Nodes update their models based on measurements of these entangled states, establishing a quantum entanglement-driven distributed learning network. This approach offers a potential solution to the bandwidth and latency constraints inherent in traditional distributed learning paradigms. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key principles and potential benefits of this method.

title: Adaptive Topological Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topological algorithm designed to address the challenges of geometric modeling and numerical simulation. Traditional approaches often rely on static, predefined topologies, limiting the algorithm's adaptability to data variations. This work proposes a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts topological parameters based on data distribution, enabling more effective geometric modeling and numerical simulation. We detail the core mechanism, including the iterative adjustment of parameters and the resulting benefits in terms of model fidelity and simulation accuracy. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its capacity to handle complex data distributions and achieve superior results compared to traditional methods.
